manualTranslations.zh: 更始敗，建武二年夏，常將妻子詣洛陽，肉袒自歸。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gengshi fell, in summer of the second year of Jianwu Chang led his wife and children to Luoyang, baring his torso to surrender himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Gengshi's fall, in the summer of Jianwu 2 Wang Chang brought his wife and children to Luoyang and surrendered bare-chested.

manualTranslations.zh: 光武見常甚歡，勞之曰：『王廷尉良苦。
manualTranslations.literal: Guangwu saw Chang and was greatly pleased; he comforted him, saying: "Director of Conviction, you have suffered greatly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guangwu was delighted to see him and comforted him: "Director of Conviction, you have borne great hardship.

manualTranslations.zh: 每念往時共更艱厄，何日忘之。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever I recall our shared hardships in the past, how could I forget them?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever I recall the hardships we shared, how could I forget them?

manualTranslations.zh: 莫往莫來，豈違平生之言乎？』
manualTranslations.literal: Do not go and do not come—would that violate our lifelong words?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Do not stay away and do not come back—would that break our lifelong pledge?"

manualTranslations.zh: 常頓首謝曰：『臣蒙大命，得以鞭策托身陛下。
manualTranslations.literal: Chang kowtowed and thanked him, saying: "Your servant received the great mandate and was able to attach himself to Your Majesty by whip and spur.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Chang kowtowed and replied: "I received the great mandate and was able to attach myself to Your Majesty.

manualTranslations.zh: 始遇宜秋，後會昆陽，幸賴靈武，輒成斷金。
manualTranslations.literal: At first we met at Yiqiu; later we met at Kunyang; fortunate to rely on Heaven's martial aid, we at once became sworn brothers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We first met at Yiqiu, later at Kunyang; by Heaven's martial aid we became sworn brothers.

manualTranslations.zh: 更始不量愚臣，任以南州。
manualTranslations.literal: Gengshi did not measure your servant's foolishness and entrusted him with the southern province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gengshi overestimated this foolish servant and entrusted the southern provinces to me.

manualTranslations.zh: 赤眉之難，喪心失望，以為天下復失綱紀。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Red Eyebrows' disaster I lost heart and hope, thinking the realm had again lost its standards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Red Eyebrows' disaster I lost heart and thought the realm had lost its order again.

manualTranslations.zh: 聞陛下即位河北，心開目明，今得見闕庭，死於遺恨。』
manualTranslations.literal: Hearing Your Majesty take the throne in Hebei, my heart opened and my eyes cleared; now able to see the court gate, I die without lingering regret."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When I heard Your Majesty had taken the throne in Hebei, my heart opened and my eyes cleared. Now that I see the court gate, I can die without regret."

manualTranslations.zh: 帝笑曰：『吾與廷尉戲耳。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "I was only jesting with the director of conviction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said: "I was only jesting with the director of conviction.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾見廷尉，不憂南方矣。』
manualTranslations.literal: With the director of conviction in sight, I need not worry about the south."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With you here, I need not worry about the south."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃召公卿將軍以下大會，具為群臣言：『常以匹夫興義兵，明於知天命，故更始封為知命侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he summoned a great assembly of grandees, generals, and those below, and fully told the host of ministers: "Chang raised righteous arms as a common man, clear in knowing Heaven's mandate; therefore Gengshi enfeoffed him as marquis who knows destiny.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then summoned the grandees and generals and told the court: "Wang Chang raised righteous arms as a commoner and knew Heaven's mandate; Gengshi therefore enfeoffed him as marquis who knows destiny.

manualTranslations.zh: 與吾相遇兵中，尤相厚善。』
manualTranslations.literal: Meeting me amid the armies, we were especially thick with goodwill."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Meeting me in the armies, we were especially close."

manualTranslations.zh: 特加賞賜，拜為左曹，封山桑侯。
manualTranslations.literal: He specially added rewards and favors, appointing him director of the left bureau and enfeoffing him as marquis of Shansang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He added special rewards, appointed him director of the left bureau, and enfeoffed him as marquis of Shansang.

sourceRange.text: 及帝崩，閻太后起歷為將作大匠。順帝即位，朝廷咸稱社稷臣，於是遷為衛尉。祋諷、劉瑋、閭丘弘等先卒，皆拜其子為郎；朱倀、施延、陳光、趙代等並為公卿，任職；征王男、邴吉家屬還京師，厚加賞賜；籍建、高梵等，悉蒙顯擢。永建元年，拜歷車騎將軍，弟祉為步兵校尉，超為黃門侍郎。三年，母長公主薨，歷稱病歸第；服闋，復為大鴻臚。陽嘉二年，卒官。

manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Shun took the throne, the court all praised him as a pillar of the state; he was thereupon promoted to commandant of the guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun took the throne, the court hailed Li as a pillar of the state and promoted him to commandant of the guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 祋諷、劉瑋、閭丘弘等先卒，皆拜其子為郎；
manualTranslations.literal: Di Feng, Liu Wei, Qiu Hong of Lüqiu, and others who had died earlier—all their sons were appointed gentlemen of the palace;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Di Feng, Liu Wei, Qiu Hong of Lüqiu, and others who had already died—all their sons were appointed gentlemen of the palace;

manualTranslations.zh: 朱倀、施延、陳光、趙代等並為公卿，任職；
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu Chang, Shi Yan, Chen Guang, Zhao Dai, and others who were all grandees held office;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Chang, Shi Yan, Chen Guang, Zhao Dai, and other grandees were restored to office;

manualTranslations.zh: 征王男、邴吉家屬還京師，厚加賞賜；
manualTranslations.literal: The households of Wang Nan and Bing Ji were summoned back to the capital with generous rewards;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The families of Wang Nan and Bing Ji were recalled to the capital and richly rewarded;

manualTranslations.zh: 籍建、高梵等，悉蒙顯擢。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji Jian, Gao Fan, and others all received prominent advancement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji Jian, Gao Fan, and others were all prominently advanced.

manualTranslations.zh: 永建元年，拜歷車騎將軍，弟祉為步兵校尉，超為黃門侍郎。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yongjian Li was appointed general of chariots and cavalry; his brother Zhi became colonel of foot soldiers and Chao gentleman at the yellow gate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yongjian 1 Li was made general of chariots and cavalry; his brother Zhi became colonel of foot soldiers and Chao gentleman at the yellow gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，母長公主薨，歷稱病歸第；
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year his mother the senior princess died; Li pleaded illness and returned home;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In year 3 his mother the senior princess died; Li pleaded illness and returned home;

manualTranslations.zh: 服闋，復為大鴻臚。
manualTranslations.literal: When mourning ended, he was again made grand herald.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was again appointed grand herald.

manualTranslations.zh: 陽嘉二年，卒官。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Yangjia he died in office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yangjia 2 he died in office.

sourceRange.text: ，遷射聲校尉。，代馮石為執金吾。，尊歷母為長公主。

localRange.text: 永初三年，遷射聲校尉。永寧元年，代馮石為執金吾。延光元年，尊歷母為長公主。

sourceRange.text: 更始立，以通為柱國大將軍、輔漢侯。從至長安，更拜為大將軍，封西平王；軼為舞陰王；通從弟松為丞相。更始使通持節還鎮荊州，通因娶光武女弟伯姬，是為寧平公主。光武即位，征通為衛尉。建武二年，封固始侯，拜大司農。帝每征討四方，常令通居守京師，鎮百姓，修宮室，起學宮。五年春，代王梁為前將軍。六年夏，領破奸將軍侯進、捕虜將軍王霸等十營擊漢中賊。公孫述遣兵赴救，通等與戰於西城，破之，還，屯田順陽。時，天下略定，通思欲避榮寵，以病上書乞身。詔下公卿群臣議。大司徒侯霸等曰：『王莽篡漢，傾亂天下。通懷伊、呂、蕭、曹之謀，建造大策，扶助神靈，輔成聖德。破家為國。忘身奉主，有扶危存亡之義。功德最高，海內所聞。通以天下平定，謙讓辭位。夫安不忘危，宜令通居職療疾。欲就諸侯，不可聽。』於是詔通勉致醫藥，以時視事。其夏，引拜為大司空。

context.beforeSource: 通與光武、李軼相遇棘陽，遂共破前隊，殺甄阜、梁丘賜。
context.afterSource: 通布衣唱義，助成大業，重以寧平公主故，特見親重。

manualTranslations.zh: 更始立，以通為柱國大將軍、輔漢侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gengshi was established, Tong was made pillar-of-state grand general and Marquis Who Aids Han.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gengshi took power, Li Tong was made pillar-of-state grand general and Marquis Who Aids Han.

manualTranslations.zh: 從至長安，更拜為大將軍，封西平王；
manualTranslations.literal: He followed to Chang'an and was again appointed grand general and enfeoffed as king of Xiping;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He followed the court to Chang'an, was again named grand general, and enfeoffed as king of Xiping;

manualTranslations.zh: 軼為舞陰王；
manualTranslations.literal: Yi as king of Wuyin;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Yi as king of Wuyin;

manualTranslations.zh: 通從弟松為丞相。
manualTranslations.literal: Tong's younger cousin from his father's clan, Song, as chancellor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Tong's paternal cousin Song was made chancellor.

manualTranslations.zh: 更始使通持節還鎮荊州，通因娶光武女弟伯姬，是為寧平公主。
manualTranslations.literal: Gengshi sent Tong with staff of authority back to guard Jing province; Tong then married Guangwu's younger sister Boji, who became the Princess of Ningping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gengshi sent Li Tong with credentials to return and hold Jing province. Tong married Guangwu's younger sister Boji, who became the Princess of Ningping.

manualTranslations.zh: 光武即位，征通為衛尉。
manualTranslations.literal: When Guangwu took the throne, he summoned Tong as commandant of the guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Guangwu took the throne, he summoned Li Tong to serve as commandant of the guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 建武二年，封固始侯，拜大司農。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as marquis of Gusi and appointed grand minister of agriculture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 2 he was enfeoffed as marquis of Gusi and appointed grand minister of agriculture.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝每征討四方，常令通居守京師，鎮百姓，修宮室，起學宮。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever the emperor campaigned in the four quarters, he regularly ordered Tong to remain and guard the capital, pacify the people, repair palaces, and establish academy halls.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor campaigned abroad, he left Li Tong in the capital to govern the people, repair palaces, and build academy halls.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年春，代王梁為前將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In spring of the fifth year he replaced Wang Liang as front general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth spring he replaced Wang Liang as front general.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年夏，領破奸將軍侯進、捕虜將軍王霸等十營擊漢中賊。
manualTranslations.literal: In summer of the sixth year he led Break-the-Traitor General Hou Jin, Capture-the-Barbarian General Wang Ba, and ten camps to strike the Hanzhong bandits.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth summer he led Break-the-Traitor General Hou Jin, Capture-the-Barbarian General Wang Ba, and ten camps against the Hanzhong rebels.

manualTranslations.zh: 公孫述遣兵赴救，通等與戰於西城，破之，還，屯田順陽。
manualTranslations.literal: Gongsun Shu sent troops to the rescue; Tong and the others fought at Xicheng, defeated them, returned, and garrisoned fields at Shunyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gongsun Shu sent relief troops; Li Tong and his men fought them at Xicheng, routed them, and then garrisoned and farmed at Shunyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 時，天下略定，通思欲避榮寵，以病上書乞身。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time the realm was largely settled; Tong wished to avoid glory and favor and submitted a memorial begging to retire on grounds of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The realm was nearly settled, and Li Tong wished to step back from honor. He memorialized asking to retire on grounds of illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔下公卿群臣議。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict was sent down for grandees and ministers to deliberate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the matter to the grandees and ministers.

manualTranslations.zh: 大司徒侯霸等曰：『王莽篡漢，傾亂天下。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture Hou Ba and others said: "Wang Mang usurped Han and overturned the realm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Agriculture Hou Ba and others said: "Wang Mang usurped Han and threw the realm into chaos.

manualTranslations.zh: 通懷伊、呂、蕭、曹之謀，建造大策，扶助神靈，輔成聖德。
manualTranslations.literal: Tong bore plans like Yi Yin, Lü Shang, Xiao He, and Cao Can, framed a great design, aided the divine spirit, and helped complete sage virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Tong carried plans worthy of Yi Yin, Lü Shang, Xiao He, and Cao Can, framed a great design, aided the divine mandate, and helped complete sage rule.

manualTranslations.zh: 破家為國。
manualTranslations.literal: He ruined his house for the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He ruined his own house for the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 忘身奉主，有扶危存亡之義。
manualTranslations.literal: He forgot himself in serving his lord, possessing the righteousness of upholding peril and preserving extinction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He forgot himself in serving his sovereign, with the righteousness of saving a realm in peril.

manualTranslations.zh: 功德最高，海內所聞。
manualTranslations.literal: His merit and virtue were highest, known throughout the realm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His merit was supreme and known throughout the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 通以天下平定，謙讓辭位。
manualTranslations.literal: Tong, because the realm was pacified, modestly declined his post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now that the realm was pacified, Li Tong modestly asked to step down.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫安不忘危，宜令通居職療疾。
manualTranslations.literal: In security one must not forget danger; it is fitting to order Tong to hold office and treat his illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In security one must not forget danger; Li Tong should remain in office and treat his illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 欲就諸侯，不可聽。』
manualTranslations.literal: To wish to become a mere feudal lord—this cannot be allowed."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To seek only a feudal lord's ease cannot be granted."

manualTranslations.zh: 於是詔通勉致醫藥，以時視事。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Tong to exert himself to obtain medicine and attend to affairs on schedule.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Li Tong to obtain treatment and attend to office on schedule.

manualTranslations.zh: 其夏，引拜為大司空。
manualTranslations.literal: That summer he was summoned and appointed grand minister of works.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That summer he was summoned and appointed grand minister of works.

sourceRange.text: 建光元年，太后崩，未及大斂，帝復申前命，封騭為上蔡侯，位特進。帝少號聰敏，及長多不德，而乳母王聖見太后久不歸政，慮有廢置，常與中黃門李閏侯伺左右。及太后崩，宮人先有受罰者，懷怨恚，因誣告悝、私、閶先從尚書鄧訪取廢帝故事，謀立平原王得。帝聞，追怒，令有司奏悝等大逆無道，遂廢西平侯廣德、葉侯廣宗、西華侯忠、陽安侯珍、都鄉侯甫德皆為庶人。騭以不與謀，但免特進，遣就國。宗族皆免官歸故郡，沒入騭等資財田宅，徙鄧訪及家屬於遠郡。君縣逼迫，廣宗及忠皆自殺。又徙封騭為羅侯，騭與子鳳並不食而死。騭從弟河南尹豹、度遼將軍舞陽侯遵、將作大匠暢皆自殺，惟廣德兄弟以母閻後戚屬得留京師。

context.beforeSource: 騭畏太后，遂髡妻及鳳以謝，天下稱之。
context.afterSource: 大司農朱寵痛騭無罪遇禍，乃肉輿櫬，上疏追訟騭曰：『伏惟和熹皇后聖善之德，為漢文母。

manualTranslations.zh: 建光元年，太后崩，未及大斂，帝復申前命，封騭為上蔡侯，位特進。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jian'guang the empress dowager died; before the great encoffinment was finished the emperor again renewed his earlier command, enfeoffing Zhi as marquis of Shangcai with rank of special advancement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jian'guang 1 the empress dowager died. Before she was even laid out for burial, Emperor An renewed an earlier order and made Deng Zhi marquis of Shangcai with the rank of special advancement.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝少號聰敏，及長多不德，而乳母王聖見太后久不歸政，慮有廢置，常與中黃門李閏侯伺左右。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor in youth was styled clever and keen, but when grown he was largely without virtue; his wet nurse Wang Sheng, seeing that the empress dowager long did not return government, feared there might be deposition and replacement, and constantly with palace attendant Li Run watched and waited at his side.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a boy the emperor had been called clever, but as a man he was mostly without virtue. His wet nurse Wang Sheng, seeing the empress dowager hold power so long, feared she might depose him and constantly watched for a chance with the palace attendant Li Run.

manualTranslations.zh: 及太后崩，宮人先有受罰者，懷怨恚，因誣告悝、弘、閶先從尚書鄧訪取廢帝故事，謀立平原王得。
manualTranslations.literal: When the empress dowager died, palace women who had earlier been punished harbored resentment and hatred, and thereupon falsely accused Kui, Hong, and Chang of first going with Master of Writing Deng Fang to take precedents for deposing an emperor, plotting to establish Prince De of Pingyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager's death, palace women who had once been punished bore a grudge and falsely accused Deng Kui, Deng Hong, and Deng Chang of consulting Master of Writing Deng Fang about precedents for deposing an emperor and plotting to set up Liu De, Prince of Pingyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝聞，追怒，令有司奏悝等大逆無道，遂廢西平侯廣德、葉侯廣宗、西華侯忠、陽安侯珍、都鄉侯甫德皆為庶人。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor heard and pursued his anger, ordering the responsible officials to memorialize that Kui and the others were guilty of great rebellion and lawlessness; thereupon Guangde, marquis of Xiping, Guangzong, marquis of Ye, Zhong, marquis of Xihua, Zhen, marquis of Yang'an, and Fude, marquis of Duxiang, were all demoted to commoners.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had officials charge Deng Kui and his kin with treason. Marquis Guangde of Xiping, Marquis Guangzong of Ye, Marquis Zhong of Xihua, Marquis Zhen of Yang'an, and Marquis Fude of Duxiang were all reduced to commoners.

manualTranslations.zh: 騭以不與謀，但免特進，遣就國。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi, because he had not joined the plot, was only stripped of special advancement and sent to his state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because Deng Zhi had not joined the plot, he was only stripped of special advancement and sent to his fief.

manualTranslations.zh: 宗族皆免官歸故郡，沒入騭等資財田宅，徙鄧訪及家屬於遠郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The whole clan was dismissed from office and returned to their home commanderies; Zhi's and the others' wealth, goods, fields, and houses were confiscated; Deng Fang and his household were relocated to a distant commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The whole Deng clan was stripped of office and sent home. Their property was confiscated, and Deng Fang and his family were exiled to a distant commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 郡縣逼迫，廣宗及忠皆自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Commanderies and counties pressed them; Guangzong and Zhong both killed themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under pressure from local officials, Guangzong and Zhong both took their own lives.

manualTranslations.zh: 又徙封騭為羅侯，騭與子鳳並不食而死。
manualTranslations.literal: Again Zhi was transferred and enfeoffed as marquis of Luo; Zhi and his son Feng both died by refusing food.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi was then transferred to the marquisate of Luo. He and his son Deng Feng starved themselves to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 騭從弟河南尹豹、度遼將軍舞陽侯遵、將作大匠暢皆自殺，惟廣德兄弟以母閻後戚屬得留京師。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi's younger cousin Bao, intendant of Henan, Zun, general who crosses the Liao and marquis of Wuyang, and Chang, grand master of works, all killed themselves; only Guangde and his brothers, by their mother's kinship with Empress Yan, were allowed to remain in the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi's cousin Bao, intendant of Henan, his cousin Zun, general who crosses the Liao and marquis of Wuyang, and his cousin Chang, grand master of works, all killed themselves. Only Guangde and his brothers, as kin of Empress Yan through their mother, were allowed to stay in the capital.

sourceRange.text: 永初元年，封騭上蔡侯、悝葉侯、弘西平侯、閶西華侯，食邑各萬戶。騭以定策功，增邑三千戶。騭等辭讓不獲，遂逃避使者，間關詣闕，上疏自陳曰：『臣兄弟汙濊，無分可采，過以外戚，遭值明時，托日月之末光，被雲雨之渥澤，並統列位，光昭當世。不能宣贊風美，補助清化，誠慚誠懼，無以處心。陛下躬天然之姿，體仁聖之德，遭國不造，仍離大憂，開日月之明，運獨斷之慮，援立皇統，奉承大宗。聖策定於神心，休烈垂於不朽，本非臣等所能萬一，而猥推嘉美，並享大封，伏聞詔書，驚惶慚怖。追觀前世傾覆之誡，退自惟念，不寒而栗。臣等雖無逮及遠見之慮，猶有庶幾戒懼之情。常母子兄弟，內相敕厲，冀以端愨畏慎，一心奉戴，上全天恩，下完性命。刻骨定分，有死無二。終不敢橫受爵士，以增罪累。惶窘征營，昧死陳乞。』太后不聽。騭頻上疏，至於五六，乃許之。

context.beforeSource: 騭謙遜不欲久在內，連求還第，歲餘，太后乃許之。
context.afterSource: 其夏，涼部畔羌援蕩西州，朝廷憂之。

manualTranslations.zh: 永初元年，封騭上蔡侯、悝葉侯、弘西平侯、閶西華侯，食邑各萬戶。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu Zhi was enfeoffed as marquis of Shangcai, Kui as marquis of Ye, Hong as marquis of Xiping, and Chang as marquis of Xihua, each with a fief of ten thousand households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 1 Deng Zhi was made marquis of Shangcai, Deng Kui marquis of Ye, Deng Hong marquis of Xiping, and Deng Chang marquis of Xihua, each with ten thousand households of revenue.

manualTranslations.zh: 騭以定策功，增邑三千戶。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi, for merit in fixing the succession plan, had his fief increased by three thousand households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For his role in settling the succession, Deng Zhi received an additional three thousand households.

manualTranslations.zh: 騭等辭讓不獲，遂逃避使者，間關詣闕，上疏自陳曰：『臣兄弟汙濊，無分可采，過以外戚，遭值明時，托日月之末光，被雲雨之渥澤，並統列位，光昭當世。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi and the others declined but could not be refused; thereupon they evaded the envoys, made their way by hard stages to the palace gate, and submitted a memorial stating their case, saying: "We brothers are stained and defiled, with no merit worth gathering; by chance as outer kin we met a bright age, relied on the last rays of sun and moon, received the rich rain of cloud and shower, and together held rank in succession, our glory shining in the age."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They protested but could not refuse. They dodged the envoys, made their way to court by difficult routes, and memorialized in their own words: "We brothers are unworthy men. Only as consort kin in a fortunate age did we catch the last light of imperial favor and rain of grace, holding office together until our names shone in the world."

manualTranslations.zh: 不能宣贊風美，補助清化，誠慚誠懼，無以處心。
manualTranslations.literal: We could not proclaim and praise fine customs or assist pure transformation; we are truly ashamed and truly afraid, with no way to set our hearts at rest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We could neither spread good custom nor aid honest rule. We are ashamed and afraid, with no peace of mind.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下躬天然之姿，體仁聖之德，遭國不造，仍離大憂，開日月之明，運獨斷之慮，援立皇統，奉承大宗。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty personally bears Heaven-given bearing and embodies benevolent and sage virtue; meeting an ill-formed state, you still parted from great grief, opened the brightness of sun and moon, exercised independent deliberation, supported and established the imperial succession, and received and served the great lineage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty bears Heaven's gift and sage benevolence. Though the realm was broken and you were still in mourning, you brought back daylight, acted with firm resolve, raised the imperial line, and upheld the great house.

manualTranslations.zh: 聖策定於神心，休烈垂於不朽，本非臣等所能萬一，而猥推嘉美，並享大封，伏聞詔書，驚惶慚怖。
manualTranslations.literal: The sage plan was fixed in the divine heart and its glorious achievement hangs down to imperishability; it was originally not something we ministers could match in the slightest, yet we were unworthily praised with fine beauty and together enjoyed great enfeoffment; prostrate we heard the edict and were startled, fearful, ashamed, and terrified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That sacred decision was Heaven's own, its glory everlasting. We could not claim the smallest share, yet we were praised and given great fiefs. When we heard the edict we were shaken with shame and fear.

manualTranslations.zh: 追觀前世傾覆之誡，退自惟念，不寒而栗。
manualTranslations.literal: Looking back on the warnings of overturn in former ages and withdrawing to reflect for ourselves, we shiver though there is no cold.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Remembering how former consort clans were ruined, we shudder at the thought.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣等雖無逮及遠見之慮，猶有庶幾戒懼之情。
manualTranslations.literal: Though we ministers have no reach to far-seeing plans, still we have some measure of warning and fear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We are not men of long foresight, but we know enough to be afraid.

manualTranslations.zh: 常母子兄弟，內相敕厲，冀以端愨畏慎，一心奉戴，上全天恩，下完性命。
manualTranslations.literal: Constantly mother, sons, and brothers admonished one another within, hoping by upright caution and fearful care to serve with one heart above, fulfill Heaven's grace, and below preserve our lives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mother, sons, and brothers constantly warned one another to stay upright and cautious, serve faithfully, repay Heaven's grace, and keep our lives intact.

manualTranslations.zh: 刻骨定分，有死無二。
manualTranslations.literal: The mark is carved on the bone and the allotment is fixed; there is death but no second thought.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Our duty is fixed to the bone; we would die rather than waver.

manualTranslations.zh: 終不敢橫受爵士，以增罪累。
manualTranslations.literal: We ultimately dare not accept rank and fief against right, thereby increasing our burden of guilt.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We dare not accept titles and fiefs unworthily and heap guilt upon ourselves.

manualTranslations.zh: 惶窘征營，昧死陳乞。』
manualTranslations.literal: In fear and distress we wander anxiously and, risking death, state our plea."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In terror and distress we beg you, at the risk of our lives, to hear us out."

manualTranslations.zh: 太后不聽。
manualTranslations.literal: The empress dowager would not listen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The empress dowager refused.

manualTranslations.zh: 騭頻上疏，至於五六，乃許之。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi repeatedly submitted memorials, as many as five or six times, and only then was it permitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi memorialized again and again, five or six times, before she relented.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cen Peng first broke through Jingmen, drove hard to Wuyang, kept his troops in tight order, and harmed not even a blade of grass.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ren Gui, king of Qionggu, hearing of Cen Peng's reputation, sent envoys thousands of li to welcome him and submit.

manualTranslations.zh: 會彭已薨，帝盡以任貴所獻賜彭妻子，謚曰壯侯。
manualTranslations.literal: It happened that Peng had already died; the emperor gave all that Ren Gui had presented to Peng's wife and children, and gave the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But Cen Peng had already died. The emperor gave Ren Gui's gifts to Peng's wife and children and posthumously titled him Marquis Zhuang.

sourceRange.text: 光武即位，拜為執金吾，封冠軍侯。先度河攻朱鮪於洛陽，與白虎公陳僑戰，連破降之。建武二年，益封穰、朝陽二縣。更始郾王尹尊及諸大將在南方未降者尚多，帝召諸將議兵事，未有言，沈吟久之，乃以檄叩地曰：『郾最強，宛為次，誰當擊之？』復率然對曰：『臣請擊郾。』帝笑曰：『執金吾擊郾，吾復何憂！大司馬當擊宛』。遂遣復與騎都尉陰識、驍騎將軍劉植南度五社津擊郾，連破之。月餘，尹尊降，盡定其地。引東擊更始淮陽太守暴汜，汜降，屬縣悉定。其秋，南擊召陵、新息，平定之。明年春，遷左將軍，別擊赤眉於新城、澠池間，連破之。與帝會宜陽，降赤眉。

manualTranslations.literal: When Guangwu took the throne, he appointed Fu Bearer of the Mace and enfeoffed him as marquis of Guanjun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Guangwu took the throne he named Jia Fu Bearer of the Mace and enfeoffed him as marquis of Guanjun.

manualTranslations.zh: 先度河攻朱鮪於洛陽，與白虎公陳僑戰，連破降之。
manualTranslations.literal: First he crossed the river and attacked Zhu You at Luoyang, fought with the White Tiger Duke Chen Qiao, and in succession broke and reduced him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He crossed the river first to attack Zhu You at Luoyang, fought the White Tiger Duke Chen Qiao, and broke and reduced them in turn.

manualTranslations.zh: 建武二年，益封穰、朝陽二縣。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he had his fief increased by the two counties of Rang and Chaoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 2 his fief was enlarged by the counties of Rang and Chaoyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 更始郾王尹尊及諸大將在南方未降者尚多，帝召諸將議兵事，未有言，沈吟久之，乃以檄叩地曰：『郾最強，宛為次，誰當擊之？』
manualTranslations.literal: Gengshi's Prince of Yan Yin Zun and the many great generals in the south who had not yet surrendered were still numerous; the emperor summoned the generals to discuss military affairs; none spoke; he pondered long; then he struck the ground with a dispatch and said: "Yan is strongest, Wan is next—who should strike them?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Many southern commanders, including Gengshi's Prince of Yan Yin Zun, still held out. Guangwu called his generals to council, but no one spoke. After a long silence he struck a dispatch on the ground and asked, "Yan is strongest and Wan next—who will take them?"

manualTranslations.zh: 復率然對曰：『臣請擊郾。』
manualTranslations.literal: Fu forthwith and plainly replied, saying: "Your servant requests to strike Yan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Fu answered at once, "Let me take Yan."

manualTranslations.zh: 帝笑曰：『執金吾擊郾，吾復何憂！
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "The Bearer of the Mace strikes Yan—what more have I to worry about!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "With the Bearer of the Mace on Yan, what have I to fear!

manualTranslations.zh: 大司馬當擊宛』。
manualTranslations.literal: The grand marshal should strike Wan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The grand marshal can handle Wan."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂遣復與騎都尉陰識、驍騎將軍劉植南度五社津擊郾，連破之。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Fu together with cavalry commandant Yin Shi and valiant cavalry general Liu Zhi south across the Wushe Ford to strike Yan, and in succession broke them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then sent Jia Fu with cavalry commandant Yin Shi and valiant cavalry general Liu Zhi south across the Wushe Ford against Yan and broke them repeatedly.

manualTranslations.zh: 月餘，尹尊降，盡定其地。
manualTranslations.literal: After more than a month Yin Zun surrendered and all his territory was pacified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within a month Yin Zun surrendered and his whole territory was secured.

manualTranslations.zh: 引東擊更始淮陽太守暴汜，汜降，屬縣悉定。
manualTranslations.literal: He led his forces east to attack Gengshi's Huaiyang governor Bao Si; Si surrendered and all subordinate counties were pacified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He marched east against Gengshi's Huaiyang governor Bao Si; Si surrendered and every county under him was pacified.

manualTranslations.zh: 其秋，南擊召陵、新息，平定之。
manualTranslations.literal: That autumn he struck south at Shaoling and Xixin and pacified them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That autumn he struck south at Shaoling and Xixin and pacified them.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年春，遷左將軍，別擊赤眉於新城、澠池間，連破之。
manualTranslations.literal: The next spring he was transferred to left general and separately attacked the Red Eyebrows between Xincheng and Mianchi, breaking them in succession.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next spring he was made left general and separately attacked the Red Eyebrows between Xincheng and Mianchi, defeating them again and again.

manualTranslations.zh: 與帝會宜陽，降赤眉。
manualTranslations.literal: He met the emperor at Yiyang and the Red Eyebrows surrendered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He joined the emperor at Yiyang and the Red Eyebrows surrendered.

sourceRange.text: 更始大將軍呂植將兵屯淇園，彭說降之，於是拜彭為刺奸大將軍，使督察眾營，授以常所持節，從平河北。光武即位，拜彭廷尉，歸德侯如故，行大將軍事。與大司馬吳漢，大司空王梁，建義大將軍朱祐，右將軍萬脩，執金吾賈復，驍騎將軍劉植，楊化將軍堅鐔，積射將軍侯進，偏將軍馮異、祭遵、王霸等，圍洛陽數月。朱鮪等堅守不肯下。帝以彭嘗為鮪校尉，令往說之。鮪在城上，彭在城下，相勞苦歡語如平生。彭因曰：『彭往者得執鞭侍從，蒙薦舉拔擢，常思有以報恩。今赤眉已得長安，更始為三王所反，皇帝受命，平定燕、趙，盡有幽、冀之地，百姓歸心，賢俊雲集，親率大兵，來攻洛陽。天下之事，逝其去矣。公雖嬰城固守，將何待乎？』鮪曰：『大司徒被害時，鮪與其謀，又諫更始無遣蕭王北伐，誠自知罪深。』彭還，具言於帝。帝曰：『夫建大事者，不忌小怨。鮪今若降，官爵可保，況誅罰乎？河水在此，吾不食言。』彭復往告鮪，鮪從城上下索曰：『必信，可乘此上。』彭趣索欲上。鮪見其誠，即許降。後五日，鮪將輕騎詣彭。顧敕諸部將曰：『堅守待我。我若不還，諸君徑將大兵上轘轅，歸郾王。』乃面縛，與彭俱詣河陽。帝即解其縛，召見之，復令彭夜送鮪歸城。明旦，悉其眾出降，拜鮪為平狄將軍，封扶溝侯。鮪，淮陽人，後為少府，傳封累代。

context.beforeSource: 乃貰歆，以為鄧禹軍師。
context.afterSource: 建武二年，使彭擊荊州，下犨、葉等十餘城。
context.beforeLocal: 乃貰歆，以為鄧禹軍師。
context.afterLocal: 建武二年，使彭擊荊州，下犨、葉等十餘城。

manualTranslations.zh: 更始大將軍呂植將兵屯淇園，彭說降之，於是拜彭為刺奸大將軍，使督察眾營，授以常所持節，從平河北。
manualTranslations.literal: Gengshi's great general Lü Zhi led troops encamped at Qiyuan; Peng persuaded him to surrender; thereupon Peng was appointed great general who probes treachery, ordered to inspect and oversee the many camps, granted the tally he constantly carried, and followed in pacifying Hebei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gengshi's great general Lü Zhi held Qiyuan with his troops. Cen Peng talked him into surrendering and was then named great general who probes treachery, charged with inspecting the camps, given his usual tally, and sent to help pacify Hebei.

manualTranslations.zh: 光武即位，拜彭廷尉，歸德侯如故，行大將軍事。
manualTranslations.literal: When Guangwu took the throne, he appointed Peng commandant of justice; marquis of Guide remained as before, and he acted as great general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Guangwu took the throne he made Cen Peng commandant of justice, kept him marquis of Guide, and let him act as great general.

manualTranslations.zh: 與大司馬吳漢，大司空王梁，建義大將軍朱祐，右將軍萬脩，執金吾賈復，驍騎將軍劉植，楊化將軍堅鐔，積射將軍侯進，偏將軍馮異、祭遵、王霸等，圍洛陽數月。
manualTranslations.literal: Together with grand marshal Wu Han, grand minister of works Wang Liang, founding righteousness great general Zhu You, right general Wan Xiu, Bearer of the Mace Jia Fu, valiant cavalry general Liu Zhi, Yanghua general Jian Tan, stacked-shooters general Hou Jin, and lieutenant generals Feng Yi, Ji Zun, Wang Ba, and others, he besieged Luoyang for several months.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With Grand Marshal Wu Han, Grand Minister of Works Wang Liang, Founding Righteousness General Zhu You, Right General Wan Xiu, Bearer of the Mace Jia Fu, Valiant Cavalry General Liu Zhi, Yanghua General Jian Tan, Stacked-Shooters General Hou Jin, and Lieutenant Generals Feng Yi, Ji Zun, and Wang Ba, he besieged Luoyang for months.

manualTranslations.zh: 朱鮪等堅守不肯下。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu You and the others held firm in defense and would not submit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu You and his men held out and refused to yield.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝以彭嘗為鮪校尉，令往說之。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor, because Peng had once been You's colonel, ordered him to go persuade him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because Cen Peng had once served as Zhu You's colonel, the emperor sent him to negotiate.

manualTranslations.zh: 鮪在城上，彭在城下，相勞苦歡語如平生。
manualTranslations.literal: You was on the wall, Peng below the wall; they exchanged greetings of hardship and spoke joyfully as in former days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu You stood on the wall while Cen Peng stood below; they greeted one another warmly as in old times.

manualTranslations.zh: 彭因曰：『彭往者得執鞭侍從，蒙薦舉拔擢，常思有以報恩。
manualTranslations.literal: Peng thereupon said: "Peng in former days obtained the whip and attended in service; I received recommendation and promotion; I constantly think of having something with which to repay grace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cen Peng then said, "In former days I had the honor to serve at your side and was raised by your recommendation; I have long wished to repay that kindness.

manualTranslations.zh: 今赤眉已得長安，更始為三王所反，皇帝受命，平定燕、趙，盡有幽、冀之地，百姓歸心，賢俊雲集，親率大兵，來攻洛陽。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the Red Eyebrows have already taken Chang'an; Gengshi has been turned against by the three kings; the emperor has received the mandate, pacified Yan and Zhao, and fully possesses the lands of You and Ji; the hundred surnames turn their hearts; worthy and eminent men gather like clouds; he personally leads a great army to attack Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Red Eyebrows hold Chang'an, Gengshi has been overthrown by the three kings, and the emperor has received Heaven's mandate, pacified Yan and Zhao, and taken all of You and Ji. The people rally to him, talent gathers, and he leads a great army against Luoyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 天下之事，逝其去矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The affairs of the realm have passed and are gone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The tide of empire has already turned.

manualTranslations.zh: 公雖嬰城固守，將何待乎？』
manualTranslations.literal: Though you shut the city and hold firm in defense, what will you wait for?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even if you bar the gates, what can you hope for?"

manualTranslations.zh: 鮪曰：『大司徒被害時，鮪與其謀，又諫更始無遣蕭王北伐，誠自知罪深。』
manualTranslations.literal: You said: "When the grand minister over the masses met harm, You joined in the plot, and again remonstrated with Gengshi not to send the Prince of Xiao north in campaign—I truly know my guilt is deep."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu You replied, "When Grand Minister Liu Bosheng was killed I took part in the plot, and I also urged Gengshi not to send the Prince of Xiao north—I know my guilt is grave."

manualTranslations.zh: 彭還，具言於帝。
manualTranslations.literal: Peng returned and reported everything to the emperor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cen Peng returned and reported everything to the emperor.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝曰：『夫建大事者，不忌小怨。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor said: "Those who establish great affairs do not begrudge small resentments.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Men who build great enterprises do not nurse small grudges.

manualTranslations.zh: 鮪今若降，官爵可保，況誅罰乎？
manualTranslations.literal: If You now surrenders, office and rank can be preserved—how much more punishment?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Zhu You surrenders now, his rank and titles are safe—let alone punishment.

manualTranslations.zh: 河水在此，吾不食言。』
manualTranslations.literal: The river is here; I do not eat my words."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The river is my witness; I will not break my word."

manualTranslations.zh: 彭復往告鮪，鮪從城上下索曰：『必信，可乘此上。』
manualTranslations.literal: Peng again went to tell You; You let a rope down from the wall and said: "If you are truly trustworthy, you may ascend by this."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cen Peng went again to Zhu You, who lowered a rope from the wall and said, "If you mean what you say, climb up by this."

manualTranslations.zh: 彭趣索欲上。
manualTranslations.literal: Peng hastened to the rope and wished to ascend.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cen Peng seized the rope to climb up.

manualTranslations.zh: 鮪見其誠，即許降。
manualTranslations.literal: You, seeing his sincerity, thereupon promised to surrender.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seeing his sincerity, Zhu You agreed to surrender.

manualTranslations.zh: 後五日，鮪將輕騎詣彭。
manualTranslations.literal: Five days later You led light cavalry to visit Peng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Five days later Zhu You came to Cen Peng with a light escort.

manualTranslations.zh: 顧敕諸部將曰：『堅守待我。
manualTranslations.literal: Turning back he charged the various division generals, saying: "Hold firm and wait for me.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He told his division commanders, "Hold the city and wait for me.

manualTranslations.zh: 我若不還，諸君徑將大兵上轘轅，歸郾王。』
manualTranslations.literal: If I do not return, you gentlemen should directly lead the great army up to Huan Yuan and return to the Prince of Yan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If I do not return, march your main force up Huan Yuan and rejoin the Prince of Yan."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃面縛，與彭俱詣河陽。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon with face bound he went with Peng together to Heyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He bound his hands and went with Cen Peng to Heyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝即解其縛，召見之，復令彭夜送鮪歸城。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor immediately untied his bonds, summoned and received him, and again ordered Peng by night to escort You back to the city.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor freed him, received him in audience, and again ordered Cen Peng to escort Zhu You back to the city that night.

manualTranslations.zh: 明旦，悉其眾出降，拜鮪為平狄將軍，封扶溝侯。
manualTranslations.literal: At dawn the next day he led all his host out to surrender; You was appointed general who pacifies the Di and enfeoffed as marquis of Fugou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day Zhu You led his whole force out to surrender. He was made general who pacifies the Di and enfeoffed as marquis of Fugou.

manualTranslations.zh: 鮪，淮陽人，後為少府，傳封累代。
manualTranslations.literal: You was a man of Huaiyang; later he became minister steward; the enfeoffment was transmitted through successive generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu You was a man of Huaiyang. He later became minister steward, and his title passed down through generations.

sourceRange.text: 光武即位，拜弇爲建威大將軍。與驃騎大將軍景丹、強弩將軍陳俊攻厭新賊於敖倉，皆破降之。建武二年，更封好畤侯，食好畤、美陽二縣。三年，延岑自武關出攻南陽，下數城。穰人杜弘率其眾以從岑。弇與岑等戰於穰，大破之，斬首三千餘級，生獲其將士五千餘人，得印綬三百。杜弘降，岑與數騎遁走東陽。

context.beforeSource: 賊散入遼西、遼東，或爲烏桓、貊人所抄擊，略盡。

manualTranslations.zh: 光武即位，拜弇爲建威大將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Guangwu ascended throne, appointed Yan as General-in-Chief Who Establishes Might.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Guangwu took the throne, he named Geng Yan General-in-Chief Who Establishes Might.

manualTranslations.zh: 與驃騎大將軍景丹、強弩將軍陳俊攻厭新賊於敖倉，皆破降之。
manualTranslations.literal: With General-in-Chief Who Gallops as if Flying Jing Dan, General of Strong Crossbows Chen Jun attacked Yanxin bandits at Aocang, all defeated and surrendered them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With Jing Dan, general-in-chief who gallops as if flying, and Chen Jun, general of strong crossbows, he attacked the Yanxin bandits at Aocang, broke them, and accepted their surrender.

manualTranslations.zh: 建武二年，更封好畤侯，食好畤、美陽二縣。
manualTranslations.literal: Jianwu second year, again enfeoffed as Marquis of Haozhi, income from Haozhi and Meiyang two counties.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Haozhi with revenue from Haozhi and Meiyang counties.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，延岑自武關出攻南陽，下數城。
manualTranslations.literal: Third year, Yan Cen from Wuguan exited attacked Nanyang, took several cities.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year Yan Cen marched out through Wuguan to strike Nanyang and captured several cities.

manualTranslations.zh: 穰人杜弘率其眾以從岑。
manualTranslations.literal: A man of Rang, Du Hong, led his masses to follow Cen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Hong of Rang rallied his followers to join Yan Cen.

manualTranslations.zh: 弇與岑等戰於穰，大破之，斬首三千餘級，生獲其將士五千餘人，得印綬三百。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan with Cen and others battled at Rang, greatly defeated them, beheaded heads more than three thousand grades, alive captured their generals and soldiers more than five thousand men, obtained seals and cords three hundred.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Geng Yan met Yan Cen and his allies at Rang and routed them, taking more than three thousand heads, capturing alive more than five thousand officers and soldiers, and seizing three hundred official seals and cords.

manualTranslations.zh: 杜弘降，岑與數騎遁走東陽。
manualTranslations.literal: Du Hong surrendered, Cen with several horsemen fled escaped to Dongyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Hong submitted; Yan Cen fled east to Dongyang with only a few horsemen.

sourceRange.text: 初，關寵上書求救，時肅宗新即位，乃詔公卿會議。司空第五倫以爲不宜救。司徒鮑昱議曰：「今使人於危難之地，急而棄之，外則縱蠻夷之暴，內則傷死難之臣。誠令權時後無邊事可也，匈奴如復犯塞爲寇，陛下將何以使將？又二部兵人裁各數十，匈奴圍之，歷旬不下，是其寡弱盡力之效也。可令敦煌、酒泉太守各將精騎二千，多其幡幟，倍道兼行，以赴其急。匈奴疲極之兵，必不敢當，四十日間，足還入塞。」帝然之。乃遣征西將軍耿秉屯酒泉，行太守事；遣秦彭與謁者王蒙、皇甫援發張掖、酒泉、敦煌三郡及鄯善兵，合七千餘人，建初元年正月，會柳中擊車師，攻交河城，斬首三千八百級，獲生口三千餘人，駝、驢、馬、牛、羊三萬七千頭，北虜驚走，車師復降。

context.beforeSource: 單于大怒，更益兵圍恭，不能下。
context.afterSource: 會關寵已歿，蒙等聞之，便欲引兵還。

manualTranslations.zh: 初，關寵上書求救，時肅宗新即位，乃詔公卿會議。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, Guan Chong submitted memorial begging rescue, at that time Emperor Zhang newly ascended throne, thereupon edicted dukes and ministers meet in council.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier Guan Chong had sent a memorial begging for relief. Emperor Zhang had just come to the throne, and the court summoned the high ministers to deliberate.

manualTranslations.zh: 司空第五倫以爲不宜救。
manualTranslations.literal: Minister of Works Fifth Lun considered not fitting to rescue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Fifth Lun held that they should not send aid.

manualTranslations.zh: 司徒鮑昱議曰：「今使人於危難之地，急而棄之，外則縱蠻夷之暴，內則傷死難之臣。
manualTranslations.literal: Minister over the Masses Bao Yu discussed saying: "Now send men in danger-hard place, urgent yet abandon them, outside then release barbarian Yi violence, inside then wound die-hard ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Minister Bao Yu argued: "We now have men in mortal peril; to abandon them in crisis would encourage barbarian violence abroad and break the hearts of loyal servants at home.

manualTranslations.zh: 誠令權時後無邊事可也，匈奴如復犯塞爲寇，陛下將何以使將？
manualTranslations.literal: Truly if for a time afterward no border affairs it could be, Xiongnu if again violate passes as raiders, Your Majesty will by what send generals?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If there were truly no frontier trouble afterward, that would be one thing; but if the Xiongnu again breach the passes, whom will Your Majesty send as general?

manualTranslations.zh: 又二部兵人裁各數十，匈奴圍之，歷旬不下，是其寡弱盡力之效也。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover two divisions soldiers only each several tens, Xiongnu besieged them, passed ten days not taken, this is their few weak utmost effort effect.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Each of the two garrisons had only a few dozen men, yet the Xiongnu besieged them for ten days without success—that shows what even a handful can do when it fights to the limit.

manualTranslations.zh: 可令敦煌、酒泉太守各將精騎二千，多其幡幟，倍道兼行，以赴其急。
manualTranslations.literal: Can order Dunhuang, Jiuquan governors each lead elite cavalry two thousand, increase their banners and flags, double road combined march, to go their emergency.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let the governors of Dunhuang and Jiuquan each lead two thousand picked horsemen, multiply their banners and flags, and march by forced stages to relieve the crisis.

manualTranslations.zh: 匈奴疲極之兵，必不敢當，四十日間，足還入塞。」
manualTranslations.literal: Xiongnu exhausted utmost soldiers, certainly not dare withstand, within forty days, enough return enter passes."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Exhausted Xiongnu troops will not dare stand against them, and within forty days the relief force can be back inside the passes."

manualTranslations.zh: 帝然之。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor approved it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃遣征西將軍耿秉屯酒泉，行太守事；
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon dispatched Campaign West General Geng Bing garrison Jiuquan, acting governor affairs;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then sent Geng Bing, general who campaigns west, to garrison Jiuquan and act as governor;

manualTranslations.zh: 遣秦彭與謁者王蒙、皇甫援發張掖、酒泉、敦煌三郡及鄯善兵，合七千餘人，建初元年正月，會柳中擊車師，攻交河城，斬首三千八百級，獲生口三千餘人，駝、驢、馬、牛、羊三萬七千頭，北虜驚走，車師復降。
manualTranslations.literal: Dispatched Qin Peng with herald Wang Meng, Huangfu Yuan to raise Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang three commanderies and Shanshan troops, combined more than seven thousand men, Jianchu first year first month, met at Liuzhong struck Jushi, attacked Jiaohe city, beheaded heads three thousand eight hundred grades, captured alive more than three thousand men, camels, donkeys, horses, cattle, sheep thirty-seven thousand head, north caitiffs startled fled, Jushi again surrendered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and dispatched Qin Peng with the herald Wang Meng and Huangfu Yuan to raise troops from Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Shanshan—more than seven thousand men in all. In the first month of the first year of Jianchu they assembled at Liuzhong, struck Jushi, and attacked Jiaohe city, taking 3,800 heads, more than 3,000 captives, and 37,000 camels, donkeys, horses, cattle, and sheep. The northern tribesmen fled in alarm and Jushi submitted again.

sourceRange.text: 建初元年，拜度遼將軍。視事七年，匈奴懷其恩信。徵爲執金吾，甚見親重。帝每巡郡國及幸宮觀，秉常領禁兵宿衛左右。除三子爲郎。章和二年，復拜征西將軍，副車騎將軍竇憲擊北匈奴，大破之。事並見《憲傳》。封秉美陽侯，食邑三千戶。

context.beforeSource: 明年秋，肅宗即位，拜秉征西將軍，遣案行涼州邊境，勞賜保塞羌胡，進屯酒泉，救戊己校尉。

localRange.text: 七四二頁08行：不忘俎豆[35]，按：王先謙謂東觀記作「不忘王室」。七四二頁08行：可*(為)**[謂]*好禮悅樂[36]，據汲本、殿本改。七四二頁11行：謚曰成侯[39]，按：集解引沉欽韓說，謂袁紀作「威侯」。七四四頁03行：從弟肜[41]，按：汲本、殿本「肜」作「彤」，通鑒或作「彤」，或作「肜」。七四四頁13行：常為士卒*[前]*鋒[43]，御覽三０二引作「常為士卒前鋒」，東觀記作「常為士卒先鋒」，今據御覽補「前」字。七四五頁05行：即擊匈奴左伊*(袟)**[秩]*訾部[46]，據集解本改，與前書匈奴傳合。七四五頁11行：*(功)**[切]*責州郡[47]，據刊誤改。漢官儀曰：「東西曹掾比四百石，余掾比三百石。賊曹，主盜賊之事。^2.02.1集解引惠棟說，謂東觀記「從平河北」。周禮：「隸僕掌□宮中之事。鄭觿曰：「止行清道也，若今警蹕。說文「□」與「蹕」同。^4.04.1披，普彼反。按：「普」原斗「芳」，逕改正。樂陽，縣名，屬常山郡。^6.06.1*[棗]*，今恆州棗城縣也，故城在縣西。據集解引錢大昕說補。按：「棗」當作「□」，字□禾，然各本正文注文皆作「棗」，今仍之。肥累，故肥子國也，漢以為縣，故城在今棗城縣西南，並屬真定國。累，音力追反。兒音五奚反。攝猶正也。唯天子得稱警□。博平，縣名，屬東郡，在今博州縣也。力，苦戰也。建平，縣名，屬沛郡，故城在今亳州酇縣西北，一名馬頭城。葛陵，縣名，故城在汝南，故鮦陽縣也。說文曰：「□，臂上也。□音公弘反。續漢書曰：「上幸廣陽城門，設祖道，閱過諸將，以遵新破漁陽，令最在前。解故謂解脫事故，以為辭說。黃門，署名。前書曰：「是時名倡皆集黃門。武樂，執干戚以舞也。良猶深也，本或作「久」。東觀記曰：「時遵屯汧。詔書曰：『將軍連年距難，觿兵即卻，復獨按部，功勞爛然。兵退無宿戒，徹食不豫具，今乃調度，恐力不堪。國家知將軍不易，亦不遺力。今送縑千匹，以賜吏士。「緣」或作「彩」。東觀記曰：「上還幸城門，閱過喪車，瞻望涕泣。霍光薨，宣帝及上官太后親臨光喪，使太中大夫任宣、侍御史五人持節護喪事。東觀記曰：「時下宣帝臨霍將軍儀，令公卿讀視，以為故事。孔子曰：「尊五美，屏四惡。前書曰：「蕭何奏事不名，入門不趨。疇，等也。言功臣死後，子孫襲封，世世與先人等。前書，高祖與功臣剖符作誓，丹書鐵契，金匱石室，藏之宗廟。漢興至此二百餘年，言「數百」者，謂以百數之。卓，高也。前書賈山上書曰：「古之賢君於其臣也，尊其爵祿而親之，疾則臨視之無數，死則往吊哭之，臨其小斂大斂，可謂盡禮也，故臣下竭力盡死以報其上。即隴坻上。磨，兵磨也。謂吳漢、耿弇等悉奔還，唯遵獨留不卻。言不侵擾。論語孔子曰：「仁以為己任，不亦重乎。死而後已，不亦遠乎。雅歌謂雅詩也。禮記投壺經曰：「壺頸修七寸，腹修五寸，口徑二寸半，容斗五升。壺中實小豆焉，為其矢之躍而出也。矢以柘若棘，長二尺八寸，無去其皮，取其堅而重。投之勝者飲不勝者，以為優劣也。^35.035.1按：王先謙謂東觀記作「不忘王室」。^36.036.1據汲本、殿本改。謚法，周書之篇，周公制焉。容車，容飾之車，像生時也。介士，甲士也。東觀記曰：「遣校尉發騎士四百人，被玄甲、兜鍪，兵車軍陳送葬。^39.039.1按：集解引沉欽韓說，謂袁紀作「威侯」。東觀記曰「上數嗟歎，□尉銚期見上感慟，對曰『陛下至仁，哀念祭遵不已，腢臣各懷慚懼』」也。^41.041.1按：汲本、殿本「肜」作「彤」，通鑒或作「彤」，或作「肜」。襄賁，縣名，屬東海郡，故城在今沂州臨沂縣南。賁音肥。^43.043.1御覽三０二引作「常為士卒前鋒」，東觀記作「常為士卒先鋒」，今據御覽補「前」字。卒，終也。三虜謂匈奴、鮮卑及赤山烏桓。鮮卑名也。^46.046.1即擊匈奴左伊*(袟)**[秩]*訾部，據集解本改，與前書匈奴傳合。(功)**[切]*責州郡，據刊誤改。音之涉反。尚書大傳曰：「孔子曰：『吾有四友焉。自吾得回也，門人加親，是非胥附邪？自吾得賜也，遠方之士日至，是非奔走邪？自吾得師也，前有光，後有輝，是非先後邪？自吾得由也，惡言不至門，是非禦侮邪？若，汝也。皆為文簿而上之。條侯，周亞夫也。為將軍，軍於細柳，文帝幸其營，亞夫持兵揖曰：「介冑之士不拜，請以軍禮見。文帝曰：「此真將軍也！穰苴，齊人田穰苴也。齊景公使為將軍，使莊賈往，穰苴與約曰：「旦日日中會於軍門。穰苴先至，賈後至，於是遂斬莊賈以徇三軍，士皆振栗。獷音古猛反，又音久永反。徼人謂徼外人偏何等也。符，驗也。為偏何請還自□，以驗內屬之信。數級謂偏何斬匈奴，送首級受賞賜。三十年為一世，言承化久也。論語孔子曰：「如有王者，必世而後仁。眚，過也。左傳曰：「不以一眚掩大德。眚音所景反。畏法猶嚴法也。

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，拜俊積弩將軍，與征南大將軍岑彭擊破秦豐，因將兵徇江東，揚州悉定。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year Jun was appointed general of accumulated crossbows; together with Grand General Who Conquers the South Cen Peng he broke Qin Feng, and then led troops to tour Jiangdong until Yang province was entirely pacified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 3 he became general of accumulated crossbows, joined Cen Peng in crushing Qin Feng, then swept Jiangdong until all of Yang province was quiet.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年，卒，謚曰威侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh year he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Jianwu 7 with the posthumous epithet Wei, "The Formidable."

sourceRange.text: 世祖即位，以武為侍中、騎都尉，封山都侯。建武四年，與虎牙將軍蓋延等討劉永，武別擊濟陰，下成武、楚丘，拜捕虜將軍。明年，龐萌反，攻桃城，武先與戰，破之；會車駕至，萌遂敗走。六年夏，與建威大將軍耿弇西擊隗囂，漢軍不利，引下隴，囂追急，武選精騎還為後拒，身披甲持戟奔擊，殺數千人，囂兵乃退，諸軍得還長安。

context.beforeSource: 進至安次、小廣陽，武常為軍鋒，力戰無前，諸將皆引而隨之，故遂破賊，窮追至平谷，浚靡而還。
context.afterSource: 十三年，增邑，更封脩侯。

manualTranslations.literal: When the Shizu ascended the throne, he made Wu gentleman attendant and colonel of cavalry and enfeoffed him as marquis of Shandu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the accession he made Ma Wu gentleman attendant and colonel of cavalry and enfeoffed him as marquis of Shandu.

manualTranslations.zh: 建武四年，與虎牙將軍蓋延等討劉永，武別擊濟陰，下成武、楚丘，拜捕虜將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu, together with tiger-fang general Gai Yan and others he campaigned against Liu Yong; Wu separately struck Jiyin, took Chengwu and Chuqiu, and was appointed general who captures captives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 4 he joined Gai Yan and others against Liu Yong; Ma Wu struck Jiyin on his own, took Chengwu and Chuqiu, and was named general who captures captives.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，龐萌反，攻桃城，武先與戰，破之；
manualTranslations.literal: The next year Pang Meng rebelled and attacked Taocheng; Wu first fought him and broke him;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year Pang Meng rebelled and besieged Taocheng; Ma Wu met him first and routed him;

manualTranslations.zh: 會車駕至，萌遂敗走。
manualTranslations.literal: when the imperial carriage arrived, Meng thereupon was defeated and fled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when the emperor arrived in person, Pang Meng broke and fled.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年夏，與建威大將軍耿弇西擊隗囂，漢軍不利，引下隴，囂追急，武選精騎還為後拒，身披甲持戟奔擊，殺數千人，囂兵乃退，諸軍得還長安。
manualTranslations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, together with Grand General Who Establishes Might Geng Yan he struck west against Wei Xiao; the Han army met with ill fortune and withdrew down from Long, Xiao pressed the pursuit hard, Wu selected elite cavalry to return as rear guard, wore armor and with halberd in hand charged in attack, killed several thousand men, Xiao's troops then withdrew, and the host of armies were able to return to Chang'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jianwu 6 he marched west with Geng Yan against Wei Xiao. When the Han force faltered on the Long descent and Xiao pressed hard, Ma Wu wheeled back with picked cavalry, armored himself, and charged with halberd in hand, killing thousands until Xiao's pursuers broke off and the army regained Chang'an.

sourceRange.text: 王梁字君嚴，漁陽要陽人也。為郡吏，太守彭寵以梁守狐奴令，與蓋延、吳漢俱將兵南及世祖於廣阿，拜偏將軍。既拔邯鄲，賜爵關內侯。從平河北，拜野王令，與河內太守寇恂南拒洛陽，北守天井關，朱鮪等不敢出兵，世祖以來梁功。及即位，議選大司空，而《赤伏符》曰『王梁主衛作玄武』，帝以野王衛之所徙，玄武水神之名，司空水土之官也，於是擢拜梁為大司空，封武強侯。

context.beforeSource: 永初七年，鄧太后紹封苞弟遽為監亭侯。
context.afterSource: 建武二年，與大司馬吳漢等俱擊檀鄉，有詔軍事一屬大司馬，而梁輒發野王兵，帝以其不奉詔敕，令止在所縣，而梁復以便宜進軍。

manualTranslations.zh: 王梁字君嚴，漁陽要陽人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Liang, courtesy name Junyan, was a native of Yaoyang in Yuyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Liang, styled Junyan, came from Yaoyang in Yuyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 為郡吏，太守彭寵以梁守狐奴令，與蓋延、吳漢俱將兵南及世祖於廣阿，拜偏將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: He was a commandery clerk; Governor Peng Chong made Liang magistrate of Hunu, and together with Gai Yan and Wu Han he led troops south to join the Shizu at Guang'a, where he was appointed lieutenant general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A commandery clerk, he was made magistrate of Hunu by Governor Peng Chong, then marched south with Gai Yan and Wu Han to Guangwu at Guang'a and was named lieutenant general.

manualTranslations.zh: 既拔邯鄲，賜爵關內侯。
manualTranslations.literal: After Handan was taken, he was granted rank as marquis within the Pass.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Handan fell he received a marquisate within the Pass.

manualTranslations.zh: 從平河北，拜野王令，與河內太守寇恂南拒洛陽，北守天井關，朱鮪等不敢出兵，世祖以來梁功。
manualTranslations.literal: He followed in pacifying Hebei, was appointed magistrate of Yewang, and together with Governor of Henei Kou Xun resisted Luoyang in the south and guarded Tianjing Pass in the north; Zhu Xin and others did not dare send out troops, and the Shizu came because of Liang's merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Hebei, became magistrate of Yewang, and with Kou Xun of Henei held Luoyang at bay to the south and Tianjing Pass to the north until Zhu Xin and the rest dared not march out—merit that drew Guangwu east.

manualTranslations.zh: 及即位，議選大司空，而《赤伏符》曰『王梁主衛作玄武』，帝以野王衛之所徙，玄武水神之名，司空水土之官也，於是擢拜梁為大司空，封武強侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When he ascended the throne, the court debated the choice of grand minister of works, and the Chifu Text says, "Wang Liang governs Wei and becomes the Dark Warrior." The Emperor took Yewang as the place to which Wei was moved, Dark Warrior as the name of the water deity, and the minister of works as the office over water and earth; thereupon he promoted and appointed Liang grand minister of works and enfeoffed him as marquis of Wuqiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the accession, as the court debated the grand minister of works, the Chifu Text read, "Wang Liang governs Wei and becomes the Dark Warrior." Guangwu noted that Yewang was where Wei had been relocated, that the Dark Warrior was the water deity, and that the minister of works governed water and earth—so Wang Liang was raised to grand minister of works and enfeoffed as marquis of Wuqiang.

sourceRange.text: 建武二年，定封丹櫟陽侯。帝謂丹曰：『今關東故王國，雖數縣，不過櫟陽萬戶邑。夫「富貴不歸故鄉，如衣繡夜行」，故以封卿耳。』丹頓首謝。秋，與吳漢、建威大將軍耿弇、建義大將軍朱祐、執金吾賈復、偏將軍馮異、強弩將軍陳俊、左曹王常、騎都尉臧宮等從擊破五校於羛陽，降其眾五萬人。會陜賊蘇況攻破弘農，生獲郡守。丹時病，帝以其舊將，欲令強起領郡事，乃夜召入，謂曰：『賊迫近京師，但得將軍威重，臥以鎮之足矣。』丹不敢辭，乃力疾拜命，將營到郡，十餘日薨。

context.beforeSource: 』乃以吳漢為大司馬，而拜丹為驃騎大將軍。

manualTranslations.zh: 建武二年，定封丹櫟陽侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu Dan's fief was fixed as marquis of Liyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 2 his title was fixed as marquis of Liyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝謂丹曰：『今關東故王國，雖數縣，不過櫟陽萬戶邑。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor said to Dan: "The old royal domains east of the Pass, though only a few counties, do not exceed a ten-thousand-household fief like Liyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "The old kingdoms east of the Pass may span only a few counties, yet none surpass Liyang's ten-thousand-household fief.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫「富貴不歸故鄉，如衣繡夜行」，故以封卿耳。』
manualTranslations.literal: As the saying goes, 'Wealth and honor that do not return to one's homeland are like embroidering a robe only to wear it at night'—that is why I enfeoff you thus."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 'Wealth and honor that never return home are like wearing embroidered robes in the dark'—that is why I enfeoff you thus."

manualTranslations.zh: 丹頓首謝。
manualTranslations.literal: Dan knocked his head and thanked him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing Dan kowtowed in thanks.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋，與吳漢、建威大將軍耿弇、建義大將軍朱祐、執金吾賈復、偏將軍馮異、強弩將軍陳俊、左曹王常、騎都尉臧宮等從擊破五校於羛陽，降其眾五萬人。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn, together with Wu Han, Grand General Who Establishes Might Geng Yan, Grand General Who Establishes Righteousness Zhu You, Bearer of the Gilded Mace Jia Fu, Lieutenant General Feng Yi, Strong Crossbow General Chen Jun, Left Clerk Wang Chang, Colonel of Cavalry Zang Gong, and others, he followed in striking and breaking the Five Camps at Yiyang and submitted their host of fifty thousand men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That autumn he joined Wu Han, Geng Yan, Zhu You, Jia Fu, Feng Yi, Chen Jun, Wang Chang, Zang Gong, and the rest to crush the Five Camps at Yiyang and accept the surrender of fifty thousand men.

manualTranslations.zh: 會陜賊蘇況攻破弘農，生獲郡守。
manualTranslations.literal: Just then the Shaan bandit Su Kuang broke Hongnong and captured the governor alive.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: About then the Shaan rebel Su Kuang overran Hongnong and took the prefect alive.

manualTranslations.zh: 丹時病，帝以其舊將，欲令強起領郡事，乃夜召入，謂曰：『賊迫近京師，但得將軍威重，臥以鎮之足矣。』
manualTranslations.literal: Dan was then ill; the Emperor because he was an old general wished to order him to force himself up and head the commandery affairs, and at night summoned him in and said: "The bandits press close on the capital—if only we have the general's weight of authority, lying down to hold the place would be enough."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing Dan was ill, but as an old commander the emperor wanted him to rise despite sickness and take the commandery. He summoned him at night and said, "The rebels press the capital. Your prestige alone, even from a sickbed, would be enough to hold it."

manualTranslations.zh: 丹不敢辭，乃力疾拜命，將營到郡，十餘日薨。
manualTranslations.literal: Dan did not dare decline, and therefore forced himself despite illness to accept the commission, led the camp to the commandery, and within more than ten days died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing Dan did not dare refuse. He dragged himself to duty, marched his camp to the commandery, and died within a fortnight.

sourceRange.text: 憲、秉遂登燕然山，去塞三千餘里，刻石勒功，紀漢威德，令班固作銘曰：惟永元元年秋七月，有漢元舅曰車騎將軍竇憲，寅亮聖明，登翼王室，納於大麓，惟清緝熙。乃與執金吾耿秉，述職巡御，理兵於朔方。鷹揚之校，螭虎之士，爰該六師，暨南單于、東烏桓、西戎氐羌侯王君長之群，驍騎三萬。元戎輕武，長轂四分，雲輜蔽路，萬有三千餘乘。勒以八陣，莅以威神，玄甲耀日，朱旗絳天。遂陵高闕，下雞鹿，經磧鹵，絕大漠，斬溫禺以釁鼓，血屍逐以染鍔。然後四校橫徂，星流彗埽，蕭條萬里，野無遺寇。於是域滅區單，反旆而旋，考傳驗圖，窮覽其山川。遂逾涿邪，跨安侯，乘燕然，躡冒頓之區落，焚老上之龍庭。上以攄高、文之宿憤，光祖宗之玄靈；下以安固後嗣，恢拓境宇，振大漢之天聲。茲所謂一勞而久逸，暫費而永寧者也。乃遂封山刋石，昭銘上德。其辭曰：鑠王師兮征荒裔，剿凶虐兮𢧵海外，敻其邈兮亙地界，封神丘兮建隆曷，熙帝載兮振萬世。

manualTranslations.zh: 憲、秉遂登燕然山，去塞三千餘里，刻石勒功，紀漢威德，令班固作銘曰：惟永元元年秋七月，有漢元舅曰車騎將軍竇憲，寅亮聖明，登翼王室，納於大麓，惟清緝熙。
manualTranslations.literal: Xian, Bing thereupon ascended Yanran Mountain—over three thousand li beyond the passes—carved stone to inscribe merit—recorded Han might and virtue—ordered Ban Gu to compose the inscription saying: Only in the seventh month of autumn of the first year of Yongyuan, there was the Han emperor's maternal uncle called General of Chariots and Cavalry Dou Xian, devotedly bright and sagely, uplifting and winging the royal house, received at the great foothills, purely clear and harmoniously glorious.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dou Xian and Geng Bing climbed Yanran Mountain, more than three thousand li beyond the frontier, carved stone to record their victory, and commemorated Han might and virtue; Ban Gu was ordered to compose the inscription: 'In the seventh month of autumn of the first year of Yongyuan, the Han emperor's maternal uncle, General of Chariots and Cavalry Dou Xian, devotedly bright and sagely, uplifts and wings the royal house, received at the great foothills, pure and harmoniously glorious.'

manualTranslations.zh: 乃與執金吾耿秉，述職巡御，理兵於朔方。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon together with Bearer of the Mace Geng Bing, discharged duties touring and guarding, ordered troops at Shuofang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Together with Bearer of the Mace Geng Bing he discharged his duties on patrol and marshaled troops at Shuofang.

manualTranslations.zh: 鷹揚之校，螭虎之士，爰該六師，暨南單于、東烏桓、西戎氐羌侯王君長之群，驍騎三萬。
manualTranslations.literal: Eagle-soaring colonels, dragon-tiger warriors, thereupon encompassing the six armies, together with the southern Shanyu, eastern Wuhuan, western Rong, Di, Qiang marquises, kings, and chieftains' hosts—picked riders thirty thousand.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Colonels fierce as soaring eagles and warriors bold as dragons and tigers mustered the six armies, together with the southern Shanyu, the eastern Wuhuan, and the marquises, kings, and chieftains of the western Rong, Di, and Qiang—thirty thousand picked horsemen.

manualTranslations.zh: 元戎輕武，長轂四分，雲輜蔽路，萬有三千餘乘。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand army light-armed, long axles quartered, cloud supply-wagons blocking the road—thirteen thousand plus chariots.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The main force moved lightly armed; long-shafted chariots fanned out in four columns, and supply wagons clouded the road—more than thirteen thousand vehicles.

manualTranslations.zh: 勒以八陣，莅以威神，玄甲耀日，朱旗絳天。
manualTranslations.literal: Arrayed by the eight formations, presided over by awesome spirit—dark armor dazzling the sun, vermilion banners reddening the sky.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They were drawn up in the eight battle arrays and led by awe-inspiring authority; dark armor flashed in the sun and crimson banners reddened the sky.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂陵高闕，下雞鹿，經磧鹵，絕大漠，斬溫禺以釁鼓，血屍逐以染鍔。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon scaled Gaolque, descended Jilu, crossed saline desert, traversed the great desert—beheaded Wenyu to consecrate the drums, blood and corpses of Zhuo to stain the blades.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They scaled Gaolque, descended to Jilu, crossed the saline wastes, and pierced the great desert; Wenyu was beheaded to consecrate the war drums, and Zhuo's blood and corpse stained the blades.

manualTranslations.zh: 然後四校橫徂，星流彗埽，蕭條萬里，野無遺寇。
manualTranslations.literal: Then the four colonels swept across, stars streaming and comets sweeping—desolate for ten thousand li, in the wilds no remnant raiders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then the four colonels swept across like streaming stars and sweeping comets; for ten thousand li all lay waste, and no enemy remained in the wilds.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是域滅區單，反旆而旋，考傳驗圖，窮覽其山川。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon the borderlands were extinguished and the tribal zones subdued; they turned their banners and returned, examined transmitted records and verified maps, exhaustively viewing its mountains and rivers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The borderlands were pacified and the tribal zones subdued; they turned their banners homeward, checked transmitted records against maps, and surveyed every mountain and river.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂逾涿邪，跨安侯，乘燕然，躡冒頓之區落，焚老上之龍庭。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon crossed Zhuoye, straddled Anhou, ascended Yanran, trod upon Maodun's tribal settlements, burned Laoshang's Dragon Court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They crossed Zhuoye, passed Anhou, climbed Yanran, trod the tribal lands of Maodun, and burned Laoshang's Dragon Court.

manualTranslations.zh: 上以攄高、文之宿憤，光祖宗之玄靈；
manualTranslations.literal: Above, to release Gaozu and Wendi's long-stored wrath, to glorify the ancestors' mysterious spirits;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Above, to release the long-stored wrath of Gaozu and Wendi and glorify the mysterious spirits of the ancestors;

manualTranslations.zh: 下以安固後嗣，恢拓境宇，振大漢之天聲。
manualTranslations.literal: Below, to secure and strengthen posterity, expand the realm, and shake the Great Han's heavenly renown.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: below, to secure posterity, expand the realm, and make the Great Han's heavenly renown resound.

manualTranslations.zh: 茲所謂一勞而久逸，暫費而永寧者也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is what is called one labor and long ease, brief expense and lasting peace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by one effort bringing long ease, and brief cost securing lasting peace.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃遂封山刋石，昭銘上德。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon they sealed the mountain and carved the stone, proclaiming and inscribing the sovereign's virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They sealed the mountain and carved the stone, proclaiming the sovereign's virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 其辭曰：鑠王師兮征荒裔，剿凶虐兮截海外，敻其邈兮亙地界，封神丘兮建隆曷，熙帝載兮振萬世。
manualTranslations.literal: The text says: Bright royal army ah campaigns distant wastes; exterminates fierce cruelty ah cuts off beyond seas; vast its remoteness ah spans earth's bounds; enshrines divine mound ah establishes lofty marker; splendid emperor's reign ah shakes ten thousand generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The text reads: 'The royal host blazes forth to the ends of the earth; it extirpates cruelty beyond the sea; its reach is vast as the horizon; it marks the sacred mound and raises a towering stone; the emperor's reign resounds through the ages.'

sourceRange.text: 肅宗即位，以公主修敕慈愛，累世崇重，加號長公主，增邑三千戶；征固代魏應為大鴻臚。帝以其曉習邊事，每被訪及。建初三年78年，追錄前功，增邑一千三百戶。七年，代馬防為光祿勛。明年，復代馬防為衛尉。

context.afterSource: 固久歷大位，甚見尊貴，賞賜租祿，貲累巨億，而性謙儉，愛人好施，士以此稱之。

manualTranslations.zh: 肅宗即位，以公主修敕慈愛，累世崇重，加號長公主，增邑三千戶；
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Suzong ascended the throne; because the princess was cultivated, disciplined, kind, and loving, honored through successive generations, she was given the additional title Grand Princess and an added fief of three thousand households;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhang came to the throne, the princess was honored for her cultivated kindness and generations of esteem; she was given the title Grand Princess and an added fief of three thousand households;

manualTranslations.zh: 征固代魏應為大鴻臚。
manualTranslations.literal: Gu was summoned to replace Wei Ying as grand herald.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dou Gu was summoned to replace Wei Ying as grand herald.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝以其曉習邊事，每被訪及。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor because he understood frontier affairs, each time was consulted on them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because he understood frontier affairs, the emperor often consulted him on them.

manualTranslations.zh: 建初三年，追錄前功，增邑一千三百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Jianchu, past merit was recorded retroactively; the fief was increased by one thousand three hundred households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianchu his earlier achievements were recognized and his fief was increased by thirteen hundred households.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年，代馬防為光祿勛。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh year, he replaced Ma Fang as superintendent of the imperial household.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he succeeded Ma Fang as superintendent of the imperial household.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，復代馬防為衛尉。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year, again replaced Ma Fang as commandant of the guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The following year he again succeeded Ma Fang, this time as commandant of the guards.

sourceRange.text: 固字孟孫，少以尚公主為黃門侍郎。好覽書傳，喜兵法，貴顯用事。永平元年58年，襲父友封顯親侯。顯宗即位，遷中郎將，監羽林士。後坐從兄穆有罪，廢於家十餘年。時天下乂安，帝欲遵武帝故事，擊匈奴，通西域，以固明習邊事，十五年冬，拜為奉車都尉，以騎都尉耿忠為副，謁者僕射耿秉為駙馬都尉，秦彭為副，皆置從事、司馬，並出屯涼州。明年，固與忠率酒泉、敦煌、張掖甲卒及盧水羌胡萬二千騎出酒泉塞，耿秉、秦彭率武威、隴西、天水募士及羌胡萬騎出居延塞，又太僕祭肜、度遼將軍吳棠將河東北地、西河羌胡及南單于兵萬一千騎出高闕塞，騎都尉來苗、護烏桓校尉文穆將太原、雁門、代郡、上谷、漁陽、右北平、定襄郡兵及烏桓、鮮卑萬一千騎出平城塞。

localRange.text: 苗、護烏桓校尉文穆將太原、雁門、代郡、上谷、漁陽、右北平、定襄郡兵及烏桓、鮮卑萬一千騎出平城塞。

manualTranslations.zh: 固字孟孫，少以尚公主為黃門侍郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Gu, courtesy name Mengsun, in youth because he married a princess served as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dou Gu, styled Mengsun, became Gentleman at the Yellow Gates in his youth by marrying an imperial princess.

manualTranslations.zh: 好覽書傳，喜兵法，貴顯用事。
manualTranslations.literal: Fond of reading books and histories, delighted in military methods; when the clan rose to power he held office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He loved books and histories and delighted in military strategy; when his clan rose to power he held office.

manualTranslations.zh: 永平元年，襲父友封顯親侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yongping, succeeded father You and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xianqin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongping he succeeded his father Dou You and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xianqin.

manualTranslations.zh: 顯宗即位，遷中郎將，監羽林士。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended, was transferred to Leader of Gentlemen, supervising Feathered Forest troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne he was made Leader of Gentlemen and put in charge of the Feathered Forest guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 後坐從兄穆有罪，廢於家十餘年。
manualTranslations.literal: Later because cousin Mu was guilty, was dismissed and stayed at home over ten years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, when his cousin Dou Mu was implicated in a crime, he was dismissed and lived at home for more than ten years.

manualTranslations.zh: 時天下乂安，帝欲遵武帝故事，擊匈奴，通西域，以固明習邊事，十五年冬，拜為奉車都尉，以騎都尉耿忠為副，謁者僕射耿秉為駙馬都尉，秦彭為副，皆置從事、司馬，並出屯涼州。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time the realm was at peace; the emperor wished to follow Emperor Wu's precedent, strike the Xiongnu, and open the Western Regions; because Gu clearly understood frontier affairs, in the fifteenth year winter he was appointed coach commandant, with Colonel of Equerry Geng Zhong as deputy, Usher-Attendant Geng Bing as commandant for imperial sons-in-law, Qin Peng as deputy—all were given senior clerks and majors, and together went out to garrison Liang province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the realm was at peace the emperor wished to follow Emperor Wu's precedent by striking the Xiongnu and opening the Western Regions. Because Dou Gu knew the frontier well, in the winter of the fifteenth year he was made coach commandant, with Colonel of Equerry Geng Zhong as his deputy, Usher-Attendant Geng Bing as commandant for imperial sons-in-law, and Qin Peng as another deputy; each was given senior clerks and majors, and together they encamped in Liang province.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，固與忠率酒泉、敦煌、張掖甲卒及盧水羌胡萬二千騎出酒泉塞，耿秉、秦彭率武威、隴西、天水募士及羌胡萬騎出居延塞，又太僕祭肜、度遼將軍吳棠將河東北地、西河羌胡及南單于兵萬一千騎出高闕塞，騎都尉來苗、護烏桓校尉文穆將太原、雁門、代郡、上谷、漁陽、右北平、定襄郡兵及烏桓、鮮卑萬一千騎出平城塞。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year, Gu and Zhong led Jiuquan, Dunhuang, Zhangye armored troops and Lushui Qiang and Hu twelve thousand riders out Jiuquan pass; Geng Bing and Qin Peng led Wuwei, Longxi, Tianshui recruited soldiers and Qiang and Hu ten thousand riders out Juyan pass; also Grand Coachman Zhai Rong and General Who Crosses the Liao Wu Tang led Hedong, Beidi, Xihe Qiang and Hu and southern Shanyu troops eleven thousand riders out Gaolque pass; Colonel of Equerry Lai Miao and Colonel Who Protects the Wuhuan Wen Mu led Taiyuan, Yanmen, Dai, Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping, Dingxiang commandery troops and Wuhuan, Xianbei eleven thousand riders out Pingcheng pass.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The following year Dou Gu and Geng Zhong led armored troops from Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Zhangye together with twelve thousand Lushui Qiang and Hu horsemen out of Jiuquan Pass; Geng Bing and Qin Peng led recruits from Wuwei, Longxi, and Tianshui with ten thousand Qiang and Hu horsemen out of Juyan Pass; Grand Coachman Zhai Rong and General Who Crosses the Liao Wu Tang led troops from Hedong, Beidi, and Xihe with Qiang, Hu, and southern Shanyu forces—eleven thousand horsemen—out of Gaolque Pass; and Colonel of Equerry Lai Miao and Wen Mu, Colonel Who Protects the Wuhuan, led commandery troops from Taiyuan, Yanmen, Dai, Shanggu, Yuyang, Youbeiping, and Dingxiang with eleven thousand Wuhuan and Xianbei horsemen out of Pingcheng Pass.

items.acceptedSourceText: 固字孟孫，少以尚公主為黃門侍郎。好覽書傳，喜兵法，貴顯用事。永平元年，襲父友封顯親侯。顯宗即位，遷中郎將，監羽林士。後坐從兄穆有罪，廢於家十餘年。時天下乂安，帝欲遵武帝故事，擊匈奴，通西域，以固明習邊事，十五年冬，拜為奉車都尉，以騎都尉耿忠為副，謁者僕射耿秉為駙馬都尉，秦彭為副，皆置從事、司馬，並出屯涼州。明年，固與忠率酒泉、敦煌、張掖甲卒及盧水羌胡萬二千騎出酒泉塞，耿秉、秦彭率武威、隴西、天水募士及羌胡萬騎出居延塞，又太僕祭肜、度遼將軍吳棠將河東北地、西河羌胡及南單于兵萬一千騎出高闕塞，騎都尉來苗、護烏桓校尉文穆將太原、雁門、代郡、上谷、漁陽、右北平、定襄郡兵及烏桓、鮮卑萬一千騎出平城塞。

sourceRange.text: 初，援兄子婿王磐子石，王莽從兄平阿侯仁之子也。莽敗，磐擁富資居故國，爲人尚氣節而愛土好施，有名江淮間，後遊京師，與衛尉陰興，大司空朱浮、齊王章共相友善。援謂姊子曹訓曰：「王氏，廢姓也。子石當屏居自守，而反遊京師長者，用氣自行，多所陵折，其敗必也。」後歲餘，磐果與司隸校尉蘇鄴、丁鴻事相連，坐死洛陽獄。而磐子肅復出入北宮及王侯邸第。援謂司馬呂種曰：「建武之元，名爲天下重開。自今以往，海內日當安耳。但憂國家諸子並壯，而舊防未立，若多通賓客，則大獄起矣。卿曹戒慎之！」及郭后薨，有上書者，以爲肅等受誅之家，客因事生亂，慮致貫高、任章之變。帝怒，乃下郡縣收捕諸王賓客，更相牽引，死者以千數。呂種亦豫其禍，臨命嘆曰：「馬將軍誠神人也！

context.beforeSource: 肅宗即位，追賜勃子穀二千斛。
context.afterSource: 」永平初，援女立爲皇后，顯宗圖畫建武中名臣、列將於雲臺，以椒房故，獨不及援。

manualTranslations.zh: 初，援兄子婿王磐子石，王莽從兄平阿侯仁之子也。
manualTranslations.literal: Early on, Ma Yuan's nephew by marriage Wang Pan, styled Zishi, was a son of Ping'a Marquis Ren, Wang Mang's cousin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early on, Wang Pan (style Zishi), Ma Yuan's nephew by marriage, was a son of Ping'a Marquis Ren, a cousin of Wang Mang.

manualTranslations.zh: 莽敗，磐擁富資居故國，爲人尚氣節而愛土好施，有名江淮間，後遊京師，與衛尉陰興，大司空朱浮、齊王章共相友善。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mang fell, Pan amassed wealth and lived in his homeland. He valued integrity, loved his native soil, and was generous—famed between the Yangtze and Huai. Later he traveled to the capital and became close with Commandant of the Guards Yin Xing, Grand Minister over the Masses Zhu Fu, and Prince Zhang of Qi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang fell, Pan kept great wealth in his homeland. He prized integrity, loved his native district, and was generous, winning fame between the Yangtze and Huai. Later he visited the capital and befriended Yin Xing, commandant of the guards; Zhu Fu, grand minister over the masses; and Prince Zhang of Qi.

manualTranslations.zh: 援謂姊子曹訓曰：「王氏，廢姓也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan said to his sister's son Cao Xun: "The Wang house is a discarded surname.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan told his sister's son Cao Xun, "The Wang clan is a fallen house.

manualTranslations.zh: 子石當屏居自守，而反遊京師長者，用氣自行，多所陵折，其敗必也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zishi ought to live in seclusion and keep himself; instead he visits the capital's elders, asserts himself by force, and bullies many—his ruin is certain."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zishi should live quietly apart and guard himself, yet he roams among the capital's elders, forcing his will on others and humiliating many—his fall is sure."

manualTranslations.zh: 後歲餘，磐果與司隸校尉蘇鄴、丁鴻事相連，坐死洛陽獄。
manualTranslations.literal: A year later Pan was indeed implicated in the affair of Director of Retainers Su Ye and Ding Hong and died in Luoyang prison.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: More than a year later Pan was implicated with the director of retainers Su Ye and Ding Hong and died in Luoyang prison.

manualTranslations.zh: 而磐子肅復出入北宮及王侯邸第。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet Pan's son Su again came and went in the Northern Palace and at the residences of kings and marquises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet Pan's son Su again frequented the Northern Palace and the mansions of kings and marquises.

manualTranslations.zh: 援謂司馬呂種曰：「建武之元，名爲天下重開。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan said to Registrar Lü Zhong: "The first year of Jianwu is called the world's reopening.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan told registrar Lü Zhong, "The inaugural year of Jianwu marks the realm's renewal.

manualTranslations.zh: 自今以往，海內日當安耳。
manualTranslations.literal: From now on the realm should grow more secure day by day.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From now on the empire should grow safer day by day.

manualTranslations.zh: 但憂國家諸子並壯，而舊防未立，若多通賓客，則大獄起矣。
manualTranslations.literal: I only fear that the imperial princes are all grown strong while the old safeguards are not yet in place; if they admit too many guests, a great prosecution will arise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I only fear that the imperial princes are all grown while the old safeguards are not yet set; if they keep too many guests, a great prosecution will follow.

manualTranslations.zh: 卿曹戒慎之！」
manualTranslations.literal: You must all be on guard!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You must all be careful!"

manualTranslations.zh: 及郭后薨，有上書者，以爲肅等受誅之家，客因事生亂，慮致貫高、任章之變。
manualTranslations.literal: When Empress Guo died, memorialists argued that families like Su's, whose kin had been executed, might let their guests stir trouble and bring about another Gao or Ren Zhang affair.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Empress Guo died, memorialists warned that families such as Su's, kin of executed men, might let their guests stir disorder like the Gao or Ren Zhang plots.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝怒，乃下郡縣收捕諸王賓客，更相牽引，死者以千數。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor in anger ordered the commanderies and counties to arrest the princes' guests; mutual denunciations followed and deaths ran into the thousands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor in anger ordered the commanderies and counties to seize the princes' guests; mutual accusations followed and deaths ran into the thousands.

manualTranslations.zh: 呂種亦豫其禍，臨命嘆曰：「馬將軍誠神人也！」
manualTranslations.literal: Lü Zhong also fell into the calamity; facing death he sighed: "General Ma is truly a seer!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Zhong shared the disaster; at the end he sighed, "General Ma was truly a prophet!"
