sourceRange.text: 在事數歲，北邊威服。永康元年，徵為尚書。其夏日食，詔公卿舉賢良方正，下問得失。規對曰：「天之於王者，如君之於臣，父之於子也。誡以災妖，使從福祥。陛下八年之中，三斷大獄，一除內嬖，再誅外臣。而災異猶見，人情未安者，殆賢愚進退，威刑所加，有非其理也。前太尉陳蕃、劉矩，忠謀高世，廢在里巷；劉祐、馮緄、趙典、尹勳，正直多怨，流放家門；李膺、王暢、孔翊，絜身守禮，終無宰相之階。至於鉤黨之釁，事起無端，虐賢傷善，哀及無辜。今興改善政，易於覆手，而腢臣杜口，鑒畏前害，互相瞻顧，莫肯正言。伏願陛下暫留聖明，容受謇直，則前責可弭，後福必降。

context.beforeSource: 」朝廷知而不問，時人以為規賢。
context.afterSource: 」遷規弘農太守，封壽成亭侯，邑二百戶，讓封不受。

manualTranslations.literal: That summer there was a solar eclipse; an edict ordered the high ministers to recommend worthy and upright men and to submit opinions on the government’s strengths and faults.

manualTranslations.zh: 誡以災妖，使從福祥。
manualTranslations.literal: It warns through omens and calamities so that he may follow blessing and good fortune.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下八年之中，三斷大獄，一除內嬖，再誅外臣。
manualTranslations.literal: Within eight years Your Majesty has thrice closed great criminal cases, once removed an inner favorite, and twice executed outer ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In eight years Your Majesty has closed three great prosecutions, removed one palace favorite, and executed two frontier ministers.

manualTranslations.zh: 而災異猶見，人情未安者，殆賢愚進退，威刑所加，有非其理也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet omens still appear and the people are not at ease—likely because the advance and withdrawal of worthy and foolish men and the punishments imposed are not always just.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet omens persist and hearts are uneasy—surely because promotion, dismissal, and punishment have not always been just.

manualTranslations.zh: 前太尉陳蕃、劉矩，忠謀高世，廢在里巷；
manualTranslations.literal: Former Grand Commandant Chen Fan and Liu Ju, whose loyal counsel towered above their age, were cast aside in village lanes;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Former grand commandants Chen Fan and Liu Ju, loyal counsellors of the highest rank, were left idle in their lanes;

manualTranslations.zh: 劉祐、馮緄、趙典、尹勳，正直多怨，流放家門；
manualTranslations.literal: Liu You, Feng Gun, Zhao Dian, and Yin Xun, upright yet much resented, were exiled from their households;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu You, Feng Gun, Zhao Dian, and Yin Xun, upright men who earned hatred, were driven from their homes;

manualTranslations.zh: 李膺、王暢、孔翊，絜身守禮，終無宰相之階。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Ying, Wang Chang, and Kong Yi, who kept their persons pure and observed ritual, never reached the steps of the chief minister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Ying, Wang Chang, and Kong Yi, pure and dutiful, never gained a chancellor’s seat.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於鉤黨之釁，事起無端，虐賢傷善，哀及無辜。
manualTranslations.literal: As for the hook-faction disaster, it arose without cause, cruelly harmed the worthy and the good, and brought grief even to the innocent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The faction prosecutions began without cause, ravaged the worthy, and swept up the innocent.

manualTranslations.zh: 今興改善政，易於覆手，而群臣杜口，鑒畏前害，互相瞻顧，莫肯正言。
manualTranslations.literal: Now to launch good government would be as easy as turning the hand, yet the ministers seal their mouths, dreading past harm, glance at one another, and will not speak plainly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Reform would be as easy as turning the hand, yet ministers seal their lips, fearing past punishments, and none will speak plainly.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏願陛下暫留聖明，容受謇直，則前責可弭，後福必降。」
manualTranslations.literal: I beg Your Majesty for a moment to keep your sacred clarity and accept blunt honesty; then past blame may be stilled and later blessing will surely descend."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will pause in your wisdom and accept forthright counsel; then past blame may cease and later blessing will come."

manualTranslations.zh: 對奏，不省。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: The throne took no notice of the memorial.

sourceRange.text: 永康元年，上疏諫曰：臣聞明主不諱譏刺之言，以探幽暗之實；忠臣不卹諫爭之患，以暢萬端之事。是以君臣並熙，名奮百世。臣幸得遭盛明之世，逢文武之化，豈敢懷祿逃罪，不竭其誠！陛下初從藩國，爰登聖祚，天下逸豫，謂當中興。自即位以來，未聞善政。梁、孫、寇、鄧雖或誅滅，而常侍黃門續為禍虐，欺罔陛下，競行譎詐，自造制度，妄爵非人，朝政日衰，姦臣日彊。伏尋西京放恣王氏，佞臣執政，終喪天下。今不慮前事之失，復循覆車之軌，臣恐二世之難，必將復及，趙高之變，不朝則夕。近者姦臣牢脩，造設黨議，遂收前司隸校尉李膺、太僕杜密、御史中丞陳翔、太尉掾范滂等逮考，連及數百人，曠年拘錄，事無效驗。臣惟膺等建忠抗節，志經王室，此誠陛下稷、党、伊、呂之佐，而虛為姦臣賊子之所誣枉，天下寒心，海內失望。惟陛下留神澄省，時見理出，以厭人鬼喁喁之心。臣聞古之明君，必須賢佐，以成政道。今臺閣近臣，尚書令陳蕃，僕射胡廣，尚書朱宇、荀緄、劉祐、魏朗、劉矩、尹勳等，皆國之貞士，朝之良佐。尚書郎張陵、媯皓、苑康、楊喬、邊韶、戴恢等，文質彬彬，明達國典。內外之職，群才並列。而陛下委任近習，專樹饕餮，外典州郡，內幹心膂。宜以次貶黜，案罪糾罰，抑奪宦官欺國之封，案其無狀誣罔之罪，信任忠良，平決臧否，使邪正毀譽，各得其所，寶愛天官，唯善是授。如此，咎徵可消，天應可待。閒者有嘉禾、芝草、黃龍之見。夫瑞生必於嘉士，福至實由善人，在德為瑞，無德為災。陛下所行，不合天意，不宜稱慶。

sourceRange.text: 建安元年，獻帝自河東還洛陽，操議欲奉迎車駕，徙都於許。衆多以山東未定，韓暹、楊奉負功恣睢，恣睢，肆怒貌。睢音火季反，又火佳反。《史記》：「盜跖日殺不辜，暴戾恣睢。」未可卒制。彧乃勸操曰：「昔晉文公納周襄王，而諸侯景從；《左傳》，卜偃言於晉侯曰：「求諸侯莫如勤王，諸侯信之，且大義也。」晉侯以左師逆王，王入于王城，取太叔於溫，殺之於隰城，遂定霸業，天下服從也。漢高祖爲義帝縞素，而天下歸心。項羽殺義帝於郴，高祖爲義帝發喪。高祖大哭，發使告諸侯曰：「天下共立義帝，北面事之。今項羽放殺義帝，大逆無道，寡人親爲發喪，兵皆縞素。」自天子蒙塵，蒙，冒也。左傳臧文仲曰：「天子蒙塵於外，敢不奔問官守。」將軍首唱義兵，徒以山東擾亂，未遑遠赴，雖禦難於外，乃心無不在王室。《尚書》曰：「雖爾身在外，乃心無不在王室。」乃，汝也。今鑾駕旋軫，鄭玄注《周禮》曰：「軫，輿後橫木也。」東京榛蕪，義士有存本之思，兆人懷感舊之哀。誠因此時奉主上以從人望，大順也；秉至公以服天下，大略也；扶弘義以致英俊，大德也。四方雖有逆節，其何能爲？韓暹、楊奉，安足恤哉！若不時定，使豪桀生心，後雖爲慮，亦無及矣。」操從之。

manualTranslations.literal: Many held that the east of the mountains was not yet settled and that Han Xian and Yang Feng, relying on their achievements, were arrogant and overbearing—zisui means the appearance of wanton rage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Many argued that the east was still unsettled and that Han Xian and Yang Feng, arrogant with past service, could not be subdued in haste—zisui denotes wanton, raging insolence.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Yu urged Cao Cao: "When Duke Wen of Jin received King Xiang of Zhou, the feudal lords flocked to him;

manualTranslations.zh: 《左傳》，卜偃言於晉侯曰：「求諸侯莫如勤王，諸侯信之，且大義也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Zuo Commentary: Boyan said to the ruler of Jin, 'To seek the feudal lords there is nothing like serving the king— the feudal lords will trust it, and it is moreover the great righteousness.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary records Boyan telling the Jin ruler: 'To win the feudal lords, nothing surpasses serving the king— they will trust you, and it is the great righteous cause.'

manualTranslations.zh: 」晉侯以左師逆王，王入于王城，取太叔於溫，殺之於隰城，遂定霸業，天下服從也。
manualTranslations.literal: The ruler of Jin with the left army went to meet the king; the king entered Wangcheng, took the Grand Uncle at Wen, killed him at Yicheng, and thus settled the hegemony—all under Heaven submitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin's ruler met the king with the left army; the king entered Wangcheng, seized the Grand Uncle at Wen, executed him at Yicheng, and secured the hegemony until all under Heaven submitted.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢高祖爲義帝縞素，而天下歸心。
manualTranslations.literal: The High Ancestor of Han wore mourning white for Emperor Yi, and all under Heaven turned their hearts to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor wore mourning for Emperor Yi and won the hearts of the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 項羽殺義帝於郴，高祖爲義帝發喪。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiang Yu killed Emperor Yi at Chen; the High Ancestor held mourning for Emperor Yi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xiang Yu killed Emperor Yi at Chen, the High Ancestor held mourning for him.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖大哭，發使告諸侯曰：「天下共立義帝，北面事之。
manualTranslations.literal: The High Ancestor wept greatly and sent envoys to tell the feudal lords: "All under Heaven jointly enthroned Emperor Yi, and we served him facing north.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor wept and sent envoys to the feudal lords: "All under Heaven jointly enthroned Emperor Yi, and we served him as sovereign.

manualTranslations.zh: 今項羽放殺義帝，大逆無道，寡人親爲發喪，兵皆縞素。
manualTranslations.literal: Now Xiang Yu cast aside and killed Emperor Yi—great rebellion and devoid of the Way. I personally hold mourning; the troops all wear white mourning."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now Xiang Yu cast aside and murdered Emperor Yi—great treason. I personally hold mourning, and the troops all wear white."

manualTranslations.zh: 」自天子蒙塵，蒙，冒也。
manualTranslations.literal: Since the Son of Heaven suffered dust on the road—meng means to suffer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since the emperor fell into exile—meng means to suffer hardship.

manualTranslations.zh: 左傳臧文仲曰：「天子蒙塵於外，敢不奔問官守。
manualTranslations.literal: Zang Wenzhong in the Zuo Commentary said: "The Son of Heaven suffers dust abroad—how dare we not rush to inquire after official duty?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zang Wenzhong said in the Zuo Commentary: "When the Son of Heaven suffers exile abroad, who would not rush to serve?"

manualTranslations.zh: 」將軍首唱義兵，徒以山東擾亂，未遑遠赴，雖禦難於外，乃心無不在王室。
manualTranslations.literal: The General was first to raise the righteous army, but only because the east of the mountains was in turmoil had he no leisure to go far in haste; though defending against calamity abroad, his heart was never absent from the royal house.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You were first to raise the righteous banner, but turmoil in the east kept you from going to his aid; though you fought enemies abroad, your heart never left the royal house.

manualTranslations.zh: 《尚書》曰：「雖爾身在外，乃心無不在王室。
manualTranslations.literal: The Documents says: "Though your person is abroad, your heart is never absent from the royal house."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Documents says: "Though your body is abroad, your heart never leaves the royal house."

manualTranslations.zh: 」乃，汝也。
manualTranslations.literal: Nai means you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Nai means "you."

manualTranslations.zh: 今鑾駕旋軫，鄭玄注《周禮》曰：「軫，輿後橫木也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the imperial carriage turns back its wheels—Zheng Xuan annotates the Rites of Zhou: "Zhen is the crossbeam behind the carriage."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the imperial carriage is turning homeward—Zheng Xuan glosses zhen as the rear crossbeam of the carriage.

manualTranslations.zh: 」東京榛蕪，義士有存本之思，兆人懷感舊之哀。
manualTranslations.literal: The Eastern Capital is overgrown with weeds; men of righteousness harbor thoughts of preserving the root; the myriad people cherish grief for the old.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Luoyang lies in ruins, loyal men yearn to restore the dynasty, and the people mourn the capital they have lost.

manualTranslations.zh: 誠因此時奉主上以從人望，大順也；
manualTranslations.literal: Truly to take this moment, uphold the sovereign above to follow the people's hopes—this is the great accord;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you seize this moment to receive the emperor and satisfy the people's hopes, you will align with the greatest mandate;

manualTranslations.zh: 秉至公以服天下，大略也；
manualTranslations.literal: to hold utmost fairness to bring all under Heaven to submission—this is the great strategy;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: hold yourself to utmost fairness and win the realm—that is the grand strategy;

manualTranslations.zh: 扶弘義以致英俊，大德也。
manualTranslations.literal: to uphold expansive righteousness to draw men of excellence—this is the great virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and uphold righteous purpose to gather the talented—that is supreme virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 四方雖有逆節，其何能爲？
manualTranslations.literal: Though the four quarters have rebellious conduct, what can they accomplish?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rebels may stir in the provinces, but what can they achieve?

manualTranslations.zh: 韓暹、楊奉，安足恤哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Han Xian and Yang Feng—how are they worth worrying over!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Xian and Yang Feng are hardly worth your concern!

manualTranslations.zh: 若不時定，使豪桀生心，後雖爲慮，亦無及矣。
manualTranslations.literal: If you do not settle matters in timely fashion and let heroes and champions take heart, afterward even if you take thought, it will be too late.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you delay, ambitious rivals will take heart; even if you reconsider later, it will be too late.

manualTranslations.zh: 」操從之。
manualTranslations.literal: Cao Cao followed his advice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao accepted his counsel.

時論者多欲復肉刑。融乃建議曰：「古者敦庬，善否不別，《左傳》楚申叔時曰：「人生敦庬。」杜預注：「庬，厚大也。」吏端刑清，端，直也。政無過失。百姓有罪，皆自取之。末世陵遲，風化壞亂，政撓其俗，法害其人。故曰上失其道，民散乆矣。而欲繩之以古刑，投之以殘弃，殘其支體而弃廢之。非所謂與時消息者也。《易》曰：「天地盈虛，與時消息。」紂斮朝涉之脛，天下謂爲無道。《尚書》曰：「紂斮朝涉之脛。」孔安國注曰：「冬日見朝涉水者，謂其脛耐寒，斮而視之。」夫九牧之地，千八百君，《前書》賈山曰：「昔者周蓋千八百國，以九州之人養千八百君也。」若各刖一人，是下常有千八百紂也。求俗休和，弗可得已。且被刑之人，慮不念生，志在思死，類多趨惡，莫復歸正。夙沙亂齊，左傳曰，靈公廢太子光，立公子牙，使高厚傅牙，夙沙衞爲少傅。崔杼逆光而立之，是爲莊公。莊公以夙沙衞易己，衞奔高唐以叛。伊戾禍宋，《左傳》，楚客聘于晉，過宋，太子痤知之，請野享之。公使往，伊戾請從，遣之。至則欿用牲，加書徵之，騁而告曰：「太子將爲亂，旣與楚客盟矣。」公使視之，則信有焉。公囚太子，太子縊死。公徐聞其無罪，乃亨伊戾。趙高、英布爲世大患。《史記》，胡亥謂李斯曰：「高，故宮人也。」遂專信任之。後殺李斯，劫殺胡亥，卒亡秦也。《前書》，英布坐法黥，論輸驪山，亡之江中爲羣盜。及屬項羽，常爲先鋒陷陣。後歸漢，爲九江王。謀反，誅之。不能止人遂爲非也，適足絕人還爲善耳。雖忠如鬻拳，左傳：「初，鬻拳彊諫，楚子弗從。臨之以兵，懼而從之。拳曰：『吾懼君以兵，罪莫大焉。』遂自刖。楚人以爲大閽。君子曰：『鬻拳可謂愛君矣。諫以自納於刑，刑猶不忘納君於善。』」信如卞和，《韓子》曰：「楚人和氏得璞玉於楚山之中，獻之武王。武王使玉人相之，曰：『石也。』王以和爲謾己，刖其左足。及文王即位，和又奉其璞，玉人又曰：『石也。』又刖其右足。文王薨，成王即位，和乃抱其璞而哭於楚山之下，三日三夜，泣盡而繼以血。王使玉人攻璞而得寶焉。」琴操曰：「荊王封和爲陵陽侯，和辭不就而去。乃作怨歌曰：『進寶得刑，足離分兮。去封立信，守休芸兮。斷者不續，豈不冤兮！』」智如孫臏，史記，孫臏與龐涓學兵法，涓事魏惠王爲將軍，自以能不及臏，陰使召臏，斷其兩足而黥之。臏後入齊，威王問兵法，以爲師。魏與趙攻韓，齊使田忌將而往。龐涓聞，去韓而歸。臏謂田忌曰：「三晉之兵素悍勇而輕齊。軍半至。使齊軍入魏地爲十萬竈，明日爲五萬竈，明日爲二萬竈。」龐涓行三日，大喜曰：「我固知齊卒怯，入吾地三日，士卒亡者過半矣。」乃棄其步兵，與其輕銳倍日并行逐之。孫子度其行，暮當至馬陵。馬陵道狹，旁多險阻，可伏兵，乃斫大樹白而書之曰「龐涓死於此木下」。於是令齊軍曰：「善射者萬弩，夾道而伏，期日莫見火舉而俱發。」涓夜至斫木下，見白書，乃攢火燭之，讀書未畢，齊軍萬弩俱發，魏軍大亂相失。龐涓自知智窮兵敗，遂自剄。曰：「遂成豎子之名矣。」冤如巷伯，毛萇注詩云：「巷伯，內小臣也。掌王后之命於宮中，故謂之巷伯。」伯被讒將刑，寺人孟子傷而作詩，以刺幽王也。才如史遷，李陵爲匈奴敗，馬遷明陵當必立功以報漢，遂被下蠶室宮刑，後乃著史記。達如子政，劉向字子政。宣帝時，上言黃金可成。上令典尚方鑄作事，費甚多，方不驗，乃下吏，當死。上竒其材，得踰冬減論。班固云：「向博物洽聞，通達古今。」一離刀鋸，沒世不齒。《國語》「中刑用刀鋸」也。是太甲之思庸，《尚書》：「太甲旣立，不明，伊尹放諸桐。三年，復歸於亳。思庸。」孔注曰：「念常道也。」穆公之霸秦，秦穆使孟明、白乙等伐鄭，蹇叔諫，不從。晉襄公敗諸崤，囚孟明等，後歸之。穆公曰：「孤之罪也，夫子何罪！」復使爲政，遂霸西戎。事見《左傳》。南睢之骨立，衞武之初筵，《韓詩》曰：「賔之初筵，衞武公飲酒悔過也。言賔客初就筵之時，賔主秩秩然，俱謹敬也。賔旣醉止，載號載呶，不知其爲惡也。」陳湯之都賴，《前書》，湯字子公。遷西域副校尉，矯制發諸國兵，斬郅支單于於都賴水上。魏尚之守邊，文帝時，尚爲雲中守，坐上首虜差六級，下吏削爵。趙人馮唐爲郎，爲言文帝，赦尚復爲雲中守也。無所復施也。漢開改惡之路，凡爲此也。故明德之君，遠度深惟，弃短就長，不苟革其政者也。」朝廷善之，卒不改焉。是時荊州牧劉表不供職貢，多行僭僞，遂乃郊祀天地，擬斥乘輿。斥，指也。詔書班下其事。融上疏曰：「竊聞領荊州牧劉表桀逆放恣，所爲不軌，至乃郊祭天地，擬儀社稷。雖昏僭惡極，罪不容誅，至於國體，宜且諱之。體謂國家之大體也。何者？萬乘至重，天王至尊，身爲聖躬，國爲神器，《老子》曰：「天下神器，不可爲也。」陛級縣遠，祿位限絕，賈誼曰：「人主之尊譬如堂，羣臣如陛，衆庶如地。故陛乃九級上，廉遠地則堂高也。」猶天之不可階，日月之不可踰也。《論語》曰：「夫子之不可及也，猶天之不可階而升也。」又曰：「仲尼如日月，無得而踰焉。」每有一豎臣，輒云圖之，若形之四方，形，見也。非所以杜塞邪萌。愚謂雖有重戾，必宜隱忍。賈誼所謂『擲鼠忌器』，蓋謂此也。《前書》賈誼曰：「里諺云『欲投鼠而忌器』，此善諭也。鼠近於器，尚憚不投，恐傷其器，況乎貴臣之近主乎？」是以齊兵次楚，唯責包茅；《左傳》，齊桓伐楚，責以「苞茅不入，王祭不供，無以縮酒」。杜預注曰：「包，裹束也。茅，菁茅也。束茅而灌之以酒，爲縮酒也。」王師敗績，不書晉人。《公羊傳》：「成公元年秋，王師敗績于貿戎。孰敗之？蓋晉敗之。曷爲不言晉敗之？王者無敵，莫敢當也。」前以露袁術之罪，今復下劉表之事，是使跛牂欲闚高岸，天險可得而登也。史記李斯曰：「故城高五丈，而樓季不輕犯也；太山之高百仞，而跛牂牧其上。夫樓季而難五丈之限，豈跛牂而易百仞之高哉？峭漸之埶異也。」爾雅曰：「羊牝曰牂。」易曰：「天險不可昇，地險山川丘陵也。」案表跋扈，擅誅列侯，遏絕詔命，斷盜貢篚，鄭玄注儀禮曰：「篚，竹器如筐也。」書曰：「厥篚玄纁璣組。」招呼元惡，以自營衞，專爲羣逆，主萃淵藪。」孔注曰：「天下罪人逃亡者，而紂爲魁主，窟聚泉府藪澤也。」郜鼎在廟，章孰甚焉！左傳：「取郜大鼎于宋，戊申納于太廟。臧哀伯諫曰：『君人者，昭德塞違，以臨照百官，百官於是乎戒懼。郜鼎在廟，彰孰甚焉！』」郜鼎，郜國所作也。桑落瓦解，其埶可見。詩曰：「桑之落矣，其黃而隕。」臣愚以爲宜隱郊祀之事，以崇國防。」五年，南陽王馮、東海王祗薨，並獻帝子。帝傷其早歿，欲爲脩四時之祭，以訪於融。融對曰：「聖恩敦睦，感時增思，悼二王之靈，發哀愍之詔，稽度前典，以正禮制。竊觀故事，前梁懷王、臨江愍王、齊哀王、臨淮懷王並薨無後，同產昆弟，即景、武、昭、明四帝是也，梁懷王揖，景帝弟也，立十年薨。臨江閔王榮，武帝兄也，爲皇太子，四歲廢爲王，坐侵廟壖地自殺。齊懷王閎，武帝子，昭帝異母兄，立八年薨。臣賢案：齊哀王，悼惠王之子，高帝之孫，非昭帝兄弟，當爲懷王，作「哀」者誤也。臨淮公衡，明帝弟，建武十五年立，未及進爵爲王而薨。融家傳及本傳皆作「公」，此爲「王」者，亦誤也。未聞前朝修立祭祀。若臨時所施，則不列傳紀。臣愚以爲諸在冲齔，聖慈哀悼，禮同成人，加以號謚者，宜稱上恩，稱音尺證反。祭祀禮畢，而後絕之。至於一歲之限，不合禮意，又違先帝已然之法，所未敢處。」處猶安也。

manualTranslations.zh: 時論者多欲復肉刑。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time many in public debate wished to restore corporal mutilation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time many officials wanted to restore corporal mutilation.

manualTranslations.zh: 融乃建議曰：「古者敦庬，善否不別，《左傳》楚申叔時曰：「人生敦庬。
manualTranslations.literal: Kong Rong thereupon submitted a proposal, saying: "In high antiquity they were simple and vast; good and evil were not distinguished—the Zuo Commentary, Chu's Shen Shushi said: 'Human life is simple and vast.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kong Rong argued: "In antiquity life was plain and simple; good and evil were not sharply divided. Shen Shushi of Chu said in the Zuo Commentary: 'Human life is simple and vast.'

manualTranslations.zh: 」杜預注：「庬，厚大也。
manualTranslations.literal: Du Yu annotates: 'Kuang means thick and great.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Yu glosses kuang as thick and great.

manualTranslations.zh: 」吏端刑清，端，直也。
manualTranslations.literal: Clerks were upright and punishments were clear—duan means upright.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Officials were upright and punishments were clear—duan means upright.

manualTranslations.zh: 政無過失。
manualTranslations.literal: Government had no errors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Government ran without fault.

manualTranslations.zh: 百姓有罪，皆自取之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the common people had guilt they all brought it on themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When commoners sinned, they brought it on themselves.

manualTranslations.zh: 末世陵遲，風化壞亂，政撓其俗，法害其人。
manualTranslations.literal: In declining ages slopes slip; customs spoil and disorder; government bends custom; law injures the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later ages decay: morale frays, institutions warp until policy twists customs and statutes harm the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 故曰上失其道，民散乆矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore it is said: when those above lose the Way, the people scatter—long ago.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence the saying that once rulers abandon the Way, their subjects drift beyond recall.

manualTranslations.zh: 而欲繩之以古刑，投之以殘弃，殘其支體而弃廢之。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet wishing to tie them to ancient punishments and cast them away as wreckage—mutilating their limbs and casting them off as ruined.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet you would bind them to ancient mutilations, maim their limbs, and cast them aside as ruined bodies.

manualTranslations.zh: 非所謂與時消息者也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is not what is called ebbing and flowing with the age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That is not what it means to breathe with the times.

manualTranslations.zh: 《易》曰：「天地盈虛，與時消息。
manualTranslations.literal: The Changes says: "Heaven and earth wax and wane, ebbing and flowing with the age."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "Heaven and earth wax and wane with the seasons."

manualTranslations.zh: 」紂斮朝涉之脛，天下謂爲無道。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhou cut the shin of a man wading the ford at dawn—the realm called him devoid of the Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Zhou cut the shins of a man wading at dawn, and the realm judged him devoid of the Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 《尚書》曰：「紂斮朝涉之脛。
manualTranslations.literal: The Documents says: "Zhou cut the shin of a man wading at dawn."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Documents says: "Zhou cut the shin of a man wading at dawn."

manualTranslations.zh: 」孔安國注曰：「冬日見朝涉水者，謂其脛耐寒，斮而視之。
manualTranslations.literal: Kong Anguo annotates: "In winter he saw a man wading at dawn, judged his shins able to endure cold, cut them and looked."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo glosses: "In winter he saw a man wading at dawn, thought his shins must resist cold, cut them, and looked."

manualTranslations.zh: 」夫九牧之地，千八百君，《前書》賈山曰：「昔者周蓋千八百國，以九州之人養千八百君也。
manualTranslations.literal: Across the Nine Pastures' lands were eighteen hundred lords—the Former Documents, Jia Shan said: "Formerly Zhou had roughly eighteen hundred states; the people of the Nine Provinces nourished eighteen hundred lords."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Across the Nine Pastures were eighteen hundred lords. Jia Shan said in the Former Documents: "Zhou once had some eighteen hundred states; the people of the Nine Provinces fed eighteen hundred rulers."

manualTranslations.zh: 」若各刖一人，是下常有千八百紂也。
manualTranslations.literal: If each severed one foot, below there would constantly be eighteen hundred Zhous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If each lord amputated one man, the land would forever harbor eighteen hundred tyrants like Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 求俗休和，弗可得已。
manualTranslations.literal: Seeking customs at rest and harmony cannot be achieved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Peace and harmony could never be achieved.

manualTranslations.zh: 且被刑之人，慮不念生，志在思死，類多趨惡，莫復歸正。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover those who have suffered punishment do not plan on living; their hearts dwell on death; most incline toward evil and never return to rectitude.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The branded stop investing in survival; hope dies, recidivism rises, and rehabilitation falters.

manualTranslations.zh: 夙沙亂齊，左傳曰，靈公廢太子光，立公子牙，使高厚傅牙，夙沙衞爲少傅。
manualTranslations.literal: Su Sha threw Qi into chaos—the Zuo Commentary says Duke Ling deposed Crown Prince Guang, enthroned Prince Ya, made Gao Hou tutor to Ya, and Su Sha Wei junior tutor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Su Sha threw Qi into chaos. The Zuo Commentary says Duke Ling deposed Crown Prince Guang, enthroned Prince Ya, made Gao Hou tutor to Ya, and Su Sha Wei junior tutor.

manualTranslations.zh: 崔杼逆光而立之，是爲莊公。
manualTranslations.literal: Cui Shu restored Guang and enthroned him—this was Duke Zhuang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cui Shu restored Guang and enthroned him as Duke Zhuang.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊公以夙沙衞易己，衞奔高唐以叛。
manualTranslations.literal: Duke Zhuang because Su Sha Wei had replaced him—Wei fled to Gaotang and rebelled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Duke Zhuang resented Su Sha Wei for having replaced him; Wei fled to Gaotang and rebelled.

manualTranslations.zh: 伊戾禍宋，《左傳》，楚客聘于晉，過宋，太子痤知之，請野享之。
manualTranslations.literal: Yi Li harmed Song—the Zuo Commentary: a guest of Chu was on mission to Jin and passed through Song; Crown Prince Zuo learned of it and asked for an outdoor feast.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi Li brought disaster on Song. A Chu envoy bound for Jin passed through Song; Crown Prince Zuo learned of it and asked for an outdoor feast.

manualTranslations.zh: 公使往，伊戾請從，遣之。
manualTranslations.literal: The duke sent him; Yi Li asked to accompany and was dispatched.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The duke sent the prince; Yi Li asked to go along and was sent.

manualTranslations.zh: 至則欿用牲，加書徵之，騁而告曰：「太子將爲亂，旣與楚客盟矣。
manualTranslations.literal: On arrival he improperly used sacrificial victims, added a written summons, and galloped back to report: "The crown prince is about to rebel—he has already allied with the Chu guest."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On arrival he improperly sacrificed, added a written summons, and galloped back to report: "The crown prince is plotting rebellion and has already allied with the Chu envoy."

manualTranslations.zh: 」公使視之，則信有焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The duke sent men to look—sure enough there was evidence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The duke sent men to investigate and found apparent proof.

manualTranslations.zh: 公囚太子，太子縊死。
manualTranslations.literal: The duke imprisoned the crown prince; the crown prince hanged himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The duke imprisoned the crown prince, who hanged himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 公徐聞其無罪，乃亨伊戾。
manualTranslations.literal: The duke slowly learned he was innocent and then boiled Yi Li.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The duke slowly learned the prince was innocent and boiled Yi Li alive.

manualTranslations.zh: 趙高、英布爲世大患。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao Gao and Ying Bu became great scourges to the age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao and Ying Bu became great scourges of their age.

manualTranslations.zh: 《史記》，胡亥謂李斯曰：「高，故宮人也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Records: Hu Hai said to Li Si, "Gao is a former palace man."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Records says Hu Hai told Li Si: "Gao is a former palace eunuch."

manualTranslations.zh: 」遂專信任之。
manualTranslations.literal: He thereupon trusted him exclusively.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hu Hai then trusted him exclusively.

manualTranslations.zh: 後殺李斯，劫殺胡亥，卒亡秦也。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he killed Li Si, coerced and killed Hu Hai, and in the end destroyed Qin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He later killed Li Si, forced Hu Hai's death, and in the end destroyed Qin.

manualTranslations.zh: 《前書》，英布坐法黥，論輸驪山，亡之江中爲羣盜。
manualTranslations.literal: The Former Documents: Ying Bu by law was tattooed, sentenced and sent to Mount Li, fled to the river and became a bandit chief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Former Documents says Ying Bu was tattooed by law, sent to Mount Li, fled to the rivers, and became a bandit chief.

manualTranslations.zh: 及屬項羽，常爲先鋒陷陣。
manualTranslations.literal: When he came under Xiang Yu he was constantly vanguard breaking formations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Xiang Yu he often led the vanguard in breaking enemy lines.

manualTranslations.zh: 後歸漢，爲九江王。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he returned to Han and became king of Jiujiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He later joined Han and became king of Jiujiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 謀反，誅之。
manualTranslations.literal: He plotted rebellion and was executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rebelled and was executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 不能止人遂爲非也，適足絕人還爲善耳。
manualTranslations.literal: They cannot stop others from thus doing wrong—they only suffice to cut people off from returning to good.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Corporal shame does not deter crime; it simply bars redemption.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖忠如鬻拳，左傳：「初，鬻拳彊諫，楚子弗從。
manualTranslations.literal: Though loyal like Yu Quan—the Zuo Commentary: "At first Yu Quan strongly remonstrated; the ruler of Chu would not follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men as loyal as Yu Quan—the Zuo Commentary: "At first Yu Quan strongly remonstrated; the Chu ruler would not listen.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨之以兵，懼而從之。
manualTranslations.literal: He confronted him with troops; in fear the ruler followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He confronted the ruler with troops; in fear the ruler yielded.

manualTranslations.zh: 拳曰：『吾懼君以兵，罪莫大焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Quan said: 'I frightened the ruler with troops—no crime is greater.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Quan said: "I frightened my ruler with troops—no crime is greater."

manualTranslations.zh: 』遂自刖。
manualTranslations.literal: He thereupon cut off his own foot.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then cut off his own foot.

manualTranslations.zh: 楚人以爲大閽。
manualTranslations.literal: The people of Chu made him grand gatekeeper.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people of Chu made him grand gatekeeper.

manualTranslations.zh: 君子曰：『鬻拳可謂愛君矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The gentleman said: 'Yu Quan may be called one who loved his ruler.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The gentleman said: "Yu Quan truly loved his ruler.

manualTranslations.zh: 諫以自納於刑，刑猶不忘納君於善。
manualTranslations.literal: He remonstrated and submitted himself to punishment; even in punishment he did not forget to bring the ruler to good.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He remonstrated and submitted himself to punishment; even under punishment he sought to bring his ruler to good."

manualTranslations.zh: 』」信如卞和，《韓子》曰：「楚人和氏得璞玉於楚山之中，獻之武王。
manualTranslations.literal: Trustworthy like Bian He—the Han Feizi says: "He of the Bian clan in Chu obtained raw jade in the mountains of Chu and presented it to King Wu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Trustworthy like Bian He—the Han Feizi says: "Bian He of Chu found raw jade in the Chu mountains and presented it to King Wu.

manualTranslations.zh: 武王使玉人相之，曰：『石也。
manualTranslations.literal: King Wu had a jade appraiser examine it; he said: 'It is stone.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Wu had a jade appraiser examine it; the man said: "It is stone."

manualTranslations.zh: 』王以和爲謾己，刖其左足。
manualTranslations.literal: The king thought He had deceived him and cut off his left foot.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The king thought He had deceived him and cut off his left foot.

manualTranslations.zh: 及文王即位，和又奉其璞，玉人又曰：『石也。
manualTranslations.literal: When King Wen took the throne, He again presented his raw jade; the jade appraiser again said: 'It is stone.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When King Wen took the throne, He again presented the jade; the appraiser again said: "It is stone."

manualTranslations.zh: 』又刖其右足。
manualTranslations.literal: They again cut off his right foot.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They again cut off his right foot.

manualTranslations.zh: 文王薨，成王即位，和乃抱其璞而哭於楚山之下，三日三夜，泣盡而繼以血。
manualTranslations.literal: When King Wen died and King Cheng took the throne, He then embraced his raw jade and wept at the foot of the Chu mountains for three days and three nights; tears exhausted, blood followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When King Wen died and King Cheng took the throne, He embraced the jade and wept at the Chu mountains for three days and three nights until tears gave way to blood.

manualTranslations.zh: 王使玉人攻璞而得寶焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The king sent the jade appraiser to work the raw jade and obtained a treasure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The king had the jade worked and obtained a treasure.

manualTranslations.zh: 」琴操曰：「荊王封和爲陵陽侯，和辭不就而去。
manualTranslations.literal: The Qincao says: "The king of Jing enfeoffed He as Marquis of Lingyang; He declined and would not accept, and left.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Qincao says: "The king of Jing enfeoffed He as Marquis of Lingyang; He declined and left.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃作怨歌曰：『進寶得刑，足離分兮。
manualTranslations.literal: He then composed a song of grievance: 'Presenting treasure yet receiving punishment—feet parted and divided!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He composed a lament: "Presenting treasure yet punished—feet torn apart!

manualTranslations.zh: 去封立信，守休芸兮。
manualTranslations.literal: Declining enfeoffment yet keeping faith—guarding rest amid fields!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Declining rank yet keeping faith—guarding honor amid fields!

manualTranslations.zh: 斷者不續，豈不冤兮！
manualTranslations.literal: What is severed cannot be joined—is this not injustice!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What is severed cannot be joined—is this not injustice!"

manualTranslations.zh: 』」智如孫臏，史記，孫臏與龐涓學兵法，涓事魏惠王爲將軍，自以能不及臏，陰使召臏，斷其兩足而黥之。
manualTranslations.literal: Wise like Sun Bin—the Records: Sun Bin and Pang Juan studied military methods together; Juan served King Hui of Wei as general, judged his ability inferior to Bin's, secretly had Bin summoned, cut off both his feet and tattooed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wise like Sun Bin—the Records: Sun Bin and Pang Juan studied military arts; Juan served Wei as general, envied Bin, had him summoned, cut off both feet, and tattooed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 臏後入齊，威王問兵法，以爲師。
manualTranslations.literal: Later Bin entered Qi; King Wei asked about military methods and made him teacher.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bin later entered Qi; King Wei questioned him on strategy and made him his teacher.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏與趙攻韓，齊使田忌將而往。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei and Zhao attacked Han; Qi sent Tian Ji to lead troops and go.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wei and Zhao attacked Han, Qi sent Tian Ji to command the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 龐涓聞，去韓而歸。
manualTranslations.literal: Pang Juan heard and left Han to return.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pang Juan heard and hurried back from Han.

manualTranslations.zh: 臏謂田忌曰：「三晉之兵素悍勇而輕齊。
manualTranslations.literal: Bin told Tian Ji: "The troops of the Three Jin are by nature fierce and brave and look down on Qi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bin told Tian Ji: "The Three Jin armies are fierce and despise Qi.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍半至。
manualTranslations.literal: Half the army arrives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Half the army will arrive.

manualTranslations.zh: 使齊軍入魏地爲十萬竈，明日爲五萬竈，明日爲二萬竈。
manualTranslations.literal: Have the Qi army enter Wei territory and make one hundred thousand cooking pits; tomorrow make fifty thousand; the next day make twenty thousand.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Have the Qi army enter Wei and make one hundred thousand cooking pits; the next day fifty thousand; the day after twenty thousand.

manualTranslations.zh: 」龐涓行三日，大喜曰：「我固知齊卒怯，入吾地三日，士卒亡者過半矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Pang Juan marched three days and said in great joy: "I knew all along the Qi soldiers were cowards—three days in our territory and more than half the troops have fled."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pang Juan marched three days and exulted: "I knew Qi soldiers were cowards—three days in our land and more than half have fled."

manualTranslations.zh: 」乃棄其步兵，與其輕銳倍日并行逐之。
manualTranslations.literal: He then abandoned his infantry and with his light elite troops marched double days in parallel pursuit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He abandoned his infantry and with light elite troops pursued at double speed.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫子度其行，暮當至馬陵。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Bin calculated their march—they would reach Maling at dusk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Bin calculated their march and knew they would reach Maling at dusk.

manualTranslations.zh: 馬陵道狹，旁多險阻，可伏兵，乃斫大樹白而書之曰「龐涓死於此木下」。
manualTranslations.literal: The Maling road was narrow with many obstacles beside it—good for ambush; he cut a large tree bare and wrote on it: "Pang Juan dies beneath this tree."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Maling road was narrow and treacherous—ideal for ambush. He stripped a tree and wrote: "Pang Juan dies beneath this tree."

manualTranslations.zh: 於是令齊軍曰：「善射者萬弩，夾道而伏，期日莫見火舉而俱發。
manualTranslations.literal: He then ordered the Qi army: "Good archers with ten thousand crossbows lie in ambush along the road; at dusk when you see fire raised, all release together."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He ordered: "Ten thousand crossbowmen lie in ambush along the road; at dusk when fire is raised, release together."

manualTranslations.zh: 」涓夜至斫木下，見白書，乃攢火燭之，讀書未畢，齊軍萬弩俱發，魏軍大亂相失。
manualTranslations.literal: Juan by night reached the cut tree, saw the bare writing, gathered fire to illuminate it; before he finished reading, ten thousand Qi crossbows released together and the Wei army fell into great disorder and lost one another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Juan reached the tree at night, lit a torch to read, and before he finished ten thousand crossbows fired; the Wei army collapsed in chaos.

manualTranslations.zh: 龐涓自知智窮兵敗，遂自剄。
manualTranslations.literal: Pang Juan knew his stratagems were exhausted and his army defeated, and cut his own throat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pang Juan knew he was beaten and cut his own throat.

manualTranslations.zh: 曰：「遂成豎子之名矣。
manualTranslations.literal: He said: "Thus the stripling's name is made."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He said: "Thus the stripling wins fame."

manualTranslations.zh: 」冤如巷伯，毛萇注詩云：「巷伯，內小臣也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wronged like the Lane Uncle—Mao Chang annotates the Odes: "The Lane Uncle is an inner petty official.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wronged like the Lane Uncle—Mao Chang glosses the Odes: "The Lane Uncle was an inner palace official.

manualTranslations.zh: 掌王后之命於宮中，故謂之巷伯。
manualTranslations.literal: He transmitted the queen's commands within the palace, hence he is called the Lane Uncle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He carried the queen's commands within the palace, hence the name Lane Uncle."

manualTranslations.zh: 」伯被讒將刑，寺人孟子傷而作詩，以刺幽王也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Uncle was slandered and about to be punished; the eunuch Mengzi grieved and composed an ode to satirize King You.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Slandered and facing execution, the eunuch Mengzi grieved and composed an ode satirizing King You.

manualTranslations.zh: 才如史遷，李陵爲匈奴敗，馬遷明陵當必立功以報漢，遂被下蠶室宮刑，後乃著史記。
manualTranslations.literal: Talented like Sima Qian—Li Ling was defeated by the Xiongnu; Ma Qian knew Ling would surely establish merit to repay Han, yet was cast into the silkworm chamber and suffered palace punishment; afterward he wrote the Records.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Talented like Sima Qian—when Li Ling was defeated by the Xiongnu, Sima Qian knew he would repay Han with merit, yet Sima Qian was cast into the silkworm chamber and mutilated; afterward he wrote the Records.

manualTranslations.zh: 達如子政，劉向字子政。
manualTranslations.literal: Penetrating like Zizheng—Liu Xiang, courtesy name Zizheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Penetrating like Liu Xiang, courtesy name Zizheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣帝時，上言黃金可成。
manualTranslations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he submitted that gold could be made.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he claimed gold could be transmuted.

manualTranslations.zh: 上令典尚方鑄作事，費甚多，方不驗，乃下吏，當死。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor ordered the Director of the Imperial Workshop to cast and test; expenses were great and the method failed; he was handed to officials and deserved death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the imperial workshop to test it; costs mounted, the method failed, and he was sentenced to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 上竒其材，得踰冬減論。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor admired his talent and was able to reduce the sentence after passing winter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his talent and reduced the sentence after winter.

manualTranslations.zh: 班固云：「向博物洽聞，通達古今。
manualTranslations.literal: Ban Gu said: "Xiang was broadly learned and well informed, penetrating past and present.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ban Gu said: "Xiang was broadly learned and penetrating in past and present."

manualTranslations.zh: 」一離刀鋸，沒世不齒。
manualTranslations.literal: Once they meet knife and saw, they are spurned forever.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once mutilated by blade and saw, they are spurned forever.

manualTranslations.zh: 《國語》「中刑用刀鋸」也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Discourses of the States: "Intermediate punishments use knife and saw."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Discourses of the States says intermediate punishments use knife and saw.

manualTranslations.zh: 是太甲之思庸，《尚書》：「太甲旣立，不明，伊尹放諸桐。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore Taijia's reflection on the common man—the Documents: "After Taijia was enthroned he was unenlightened; Yi Yin banished him to Tong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men like Taijia who reflected on the common Way—the Documents: "Taijia was enthroned but unenlightened; Yi Yin banished him to Tong.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，復歸於亳。
manualTranslations.literal: After three years he returned to Bo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After three years he returned to Bo.

manualTranslations.zh: 思庸。
manualTranslations.literal: Reflection on the common man.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He reflected on the common Way."

manualTranslations.zh: 」孔注曰：「念常道也。
manualTranslations.literal: Kong's annotation: "Thinking on the constant Way."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kong's gloss: "Thinking on the constant Way."

manualTranslations.zh: 」穆公之霸秦，秦穆使孟明、白乙等伐鄭，蹇叔諫，不從。
manualTranslations.literal: Duke Mu's hegemony of Qin—Duke Mu of Qin sent Meng Ming, Bai Yi, and others to attack Zheng; Jian Shu remonstrated and was not followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Duke Mu's hegemony of Qin—Duke Mu sent Meng Ming and Bai Yi against Zheng; Jian Shu remonstrated in vain.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉襄公敗諸崤，囚孟明等，後歸之。
manualTranslations.literal: Duke Xiang of Jin defeated them at Xiao and imprisoned Meng Ming and the others; later he returned them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang of Jin defeated them at Xiao, imprisoned them, and later released them.

manualTranslations.zh: 穆公曰：「孤之罪也，夫子何罪！
manualTranslations.literal: Duke Mu said: "My fault alone—what fault have you, sir!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Duke Mu said: "The fault is mine—what fault is yours?

manualTranslations.zh: 」復使爲政，遂霸西戎。
manualTranslations.literal: He again employed them in government and thus hegemonized the Western Rong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He restored them to office and hegemonized the Western Rong."

manualTranslations.zh: 事見《左傳》。
manualTranslations.literal: The affair is seen in the Zuo Commentary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The affair appears in the Zuo Commentary.

manualTranslations.zh: 南睢之骨立，衞武之初筵，《韓詩》曰：「賔之初筵，衞武公飲酒悔過也。
manualTranslations.literal: Nan Sui's bones standing bare, Duke Wu of Wei's first feast—the Han Odes says: "When guests first take their places—Duke Wu of Wei drank wine and repented of faults.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Nan Sui wasted to bone, Duke Wu of Wei repented at the first feast—the Han Odes says: "At the guests' first seating, Duke Wu of Wei drank and repented."

manualTranslations.zh: 言賔客初就筵之時，賔主秩秩然，俱謹敬也。
manualTranslations.literal: It speaks of when guests first take their seats—host and guest orderly and all reverent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When guests first sat, host and guest were orderly and reverent.

manualTranslations.zh: 賔旣醉止，載號載呶，不知其爲惡也。
manualTranslations.literal: When guests were drunk they shouted and clamored, not knowing it was evil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once drunk they shouted and clamored, not knowing it was wrong."

manualTranslations.zh: 」陳湯之都賴，《前書》，湯字子公。
manualTranslations.literal: Chen Tang at Du Lai—the Former Documents: Tang, courtesy name Zigong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Tang at Du Lai—the Former Documents: Tang, courtesy name Zigong.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷西域副校尉，矯制發諸國兵，斬郅支單于於都賴水上。
manualTranslations.literal: Promoted to deputy colonel of the Western Regions, he by forged edict mobilized the states' troops and beheaded Zhizhi Chanyu on the Du Lai River.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As deputy colonel of the Western Regions he forged an edict, mobilized allied troops, and beheaded Zhizhi Chanyu on the Du Lai River.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏尚之守邊，文帝時，尚爲雲中守，坐上首虜差六級，下吏削爵。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei Shang guarding the frontier—in the time of Emperor Wen, Shang was administrator of Yunzhong; for falling six head short in captives he was handed to officials and stripped of rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei Shang guarding the frontier—as Yunzhong administrator he fell six enemy heads short and was stripped of rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 趙人馮唐爲郎，爲言文帝，赦尚復爲雲中守也。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng Tang of Zhao was a gentleman; he spoke to Emperor Wen and Shang was pardoned and restored as Yunzhong administrator.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng Tang of Zhao pleaded to Emperor Wen, and Shang was pardoned and restored.

manualTranslations.zh: 無所復施也。
manualTranslations.literal: None could again apply their talents.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: None could again apply their talents.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢開改惡之路，凡爲此也。
manualTranslations.literal: Han opened a path to reform the wicked—generally for this reason.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han deliberately created alternatives to mutilation for exactly these humane reasons.

manualTranslations.zh: 故明德之君，遠度深惟，弃短就長，不苟革其政者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore a ruler of bright virtue, measuring far and pondering deep, discards the short-term and embraces the long-term and does not rashly alter his institutions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wise sovereigns weigh distant consequences and refuse cosmetic cruelty."

manualTranslations.zh: 」朝廷善之，卒不改焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The court approved his view and in the end made no change.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court approved Kong Rong's view and dropped the proposal.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時荊州牧劉表不供職貢，多行僭僞，遂乃郊祀天地，擬斥乘輿。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time Governor of Jingzhou Liu Biao did not submit tribute and duties and practiced many usurpations; he then performed suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and imitated pointing at the imperial carriage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At this time Jingzhou governor Liu Biao withheld tribute, practiced usurpation, performed suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, and imitated imperial rites.

manualTranslations.zh: 斥，指也。
manualTranslations.literal: Chi means to point.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chi means to point or designate.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔書班下其事。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict was promulgated announcing the matter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict was issued announcing the matter.

manualTranslations.zh: 融上疏曰：「竊聞領荊州牧劉表桀逆放恣，所爲不軌，至乃郊祭天地，擬儀社稷。
manualTranslations.literal: Kong Rong submitted a memorial, saying: "I have heard that Governor of Jingzhou Liu Biao is arrogant, rebellious, and unrestrained; his conduct is irregular—he has even performed suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and imitated the rites of the altars of soil and grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kong Rong memorialized: "I hear that Jingzhou governor Liu Biao is arrogant and rebellious, his conduct irregular—even performing suburban sacrifices and imitating the rites of the altars of soil and grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖昏僭惡極，罪不容誅，至於國體，宜且諱之。
manualTranslations.literal: Though his folly and usurpation are extreme and his crimes deserve execution, as to the body politic it is fitting to conceal it for the time being.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though his folly and usurpation deserve execution, for the sake of the state it is fitting to conceal it for now.

manualTranslations.zh: 體謂國家之大體也。
manualTranslations.literal: Ti means the great body of the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ti means the great body of the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 何者？
manualTranslations.literal: Why?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why?

manualTranslations.zh: 萬乘至重，天王至尊，身爲聖躬，國爲神器，《老子》曰：「天下神器，不可爲也。
manualTranslations.literal: The ten-thousand-carriage state is of utmost weight; the Son of Heaven is supreme; the person is the sacred body, the state is the sacred vessel—the Laozi says: "The sacred vessel of all under Heaven cannot be handled."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The imperial throne is weight beyond measure; the Son of Heaven is supreme; the person is the sacred body and the state the sacred vessel. The Laozi says: "The sacred vessel of all under Heaven must not be grasped."

manualTranslations.zh: 」陛級縣遠，祿位限絕，賈誼曰：「人主之尊譬如堂，羣臣如陛，衆庶如地。
manualTranslations.literal: The steps of the throne are distant and suspended; rank and emolument are bounded and severed—Jia Yi said: "The ruler's dignity is like a hall; ministers are like steps; the multitude is like the ground.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The throne steps are distant; rank and emolument are bounded. Jia Yi said: "The ruler's dignity is like a hall; ministers like steps; the people like the ground.

manualTranslations.zh: 故陛乃九級上，廉遠地則堂高也。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore when the steps are nine tiers high and the ground is far below, the hall is high."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the steps are nine tiers high and the ground far below, the hall stands high."

manualTranslations.zh: 」猶天之不可階，日月之不可踰也。
manualTranslations.literal: It is like Heaven that cannot be climbed by steps, or sun and moon that cannot be crossed over.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It is like Heaven that cannot be climbed or sun and moon that cannot be crossed.

manualTranslations.zh: 《論語》曰：「夫子之不可及也，猶天之不可階而升也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Analects says: "The Master cannot be reached—it is like Heaven that cannot be climbed by steps."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Analects says: "The Master cannot be reached—it is like Heaven that cannot be climbed by steps."

manualTranslations.zh: 」又曰：「仲尼如日月，無得而踰焉。
manualTranslations.literal: It also says: "Zhongni is like sun and moon—none can cross over him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It also says: "Confucius is like sun and moon—none can cross over him."

manualTranslations.zh: 」每有一豎臣，輒云圖之，若形之四方，形，見也。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever there is a petty minister, they immediately say they will plot against him—as if the form were visible on four sides—xing means visible.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever some petty minister appears, men immediately say they will plot against him—as if the plot were visible on four sides—xing means visible.

manualTranslations.zh: 非所以杜塞邪萌。
manualTranslations.literal: This is not the way to block the sprouting of evil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That is not how to choke off evil at its root.

manualTranslations.zh: 愚謂雖有重戾，必宜隱忍。
manualTranslations.literal: I hold that though the offense is grave, forbearance is necessary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I hold that though the offense is grave, forbearance is necessary.

manualTranslations.zh: 賈誼所謂『擲鼠忌器』，蓋謂此也。
manualTranslations.literal: What Jia Yi called "throwing at a rat yet fearing the vessel"—this is what is meant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What Jia Yi called "throwing at a rat yet fearing the vessel" applies here.

manualTranslations.zh: 《前書》賈誼曰：「里諺云『欲投鼠而忌器』，此善諭也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Former Documents, Jia Yi said: "A village saying runs, 'Wishing to strike a rat yet fearing the vessel'—this is a fine analogy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Yi said in the Former Documents: "A village saying runs, 'Wishing to strike a rat yet fearing the vessel'—this is a fine analogy.

manualTranslations.zh: 鼠近於器，尚憚不投，恐傷其器，況乎貴臣之近主乎？
manualTranslations.literal: When the rat is near the vessel one still fears to strike, lest the vessel be harmed—how much more when a great minister is near the ruler?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the rat is near the vessel one still fears to strike lest the vessel be harmed—how much more when a great minister is near the ruler?"

manualTranslations.zh: 」是以齊兵次楚，唯責包茅；
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore when Qi's troops halted at Chu they only demanded bundled thatch;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore when Qi's troops halted at Chu they only demanded bundled thatch;

manualTranslations.zh: 《左傳》，齊桓伐楚，責以「苞茅不入，王祭不供，無以縮酒」。
manualTranslations.literal: The Zuo Commentary: Duke Huan of Qi attacked Chu and charged them: "Bundled thatch was not sent in; the king's sacrifices were not supplied—there was nothing with which to filter the wine."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary: Duke Huan of Qi attacked Chu and charged: "Bundled thatch was not sent; the king's sacrifices lacked wine-filtration rites."

manualTranslations.zh: 杜預注曰：「包，裹束也。
manualTranslations.literal: Du Yu annotates: "Bao means wrapped and bound.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Yu glosses: "Bao means wrapped and bound.

manualTranslations.zh: 茅，菁茅也。
manualTranslations.literal: Mao is fine thatch.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mao is fine thatch.

manualTranslations.zh: 束茅而灌之以酒，爲縮酒也。
manualTranslations.literal: Binding thatch and pouring wine through it is filtering wine."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Binding thatch and pouring wine through it filters the wine."

manualTranslations.zh: 」王師敗績，不書晉人。
manualTranslations.literal: The royal army suffered defeat, yet the Jin people were not recorded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The royal army suffered defeat, yet the Jin people were not named.

manualTranslations.zh: 《公羊傳》：「成公元年秋，王師敗績于貿戎。
manualTranslations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary: "In autumn of the first year of Duke Cheng, the royal army suffered defeat at Mao Rong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary: "In autumn of Duke Cheng's first year, the royal army suffered defeat at Mao Rong.

manualTranslations.zh: 孰敗之？
manualTranslations.literal: Who defeated it?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Who defeated it?

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋晉敗之。
manualTranslations.literal: It was Jin that defeated it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin defeated it.

manualTranslations.zh: 曷爲不言晉敗之？
manualTranslations.literal: Why does it not say Jin defeated it?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why does it not say Jin defeated it?

manualTranslations.zh: 王者無敵，莫敢當也。
manualTranslations.literal: The king has no enemy—none dare withstand him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The king has no enemy—none dare withstand him."

manualTranslations.zh: 」前以露袁術之罪，今復下劉表之事，是使跛牂欲闚高岸，天險可得而登也。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier Yuan Shu's crimes were exposed; now Liu Biao's affair is again promulgated—this is like making a lame ewe wish to peer over a high bank; Heaven's barrier could be climbed and ascended.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuan Shu's crimes were exposed; now Liu Biao's affair is promulgated again—this is like letting a lame ewe peer over a high bank as if Heaven's barrier could be climbed.

manualTranslations.zh: 史記李斯曰：「故城高五丈，而樓季不輕犯也；
manualTranslations.literal: The Records, Li Si said: "Therefore though a wall is five ren high, Lou Ji does not lightly violate it;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Si said in the Records: "Though a wall is five ren high, Lou Ji does not lightly scale it;

manualTranslations.zh: 太山之高百仞，而跛牂牧其上。
manualTranslations.literal: Mount Tai is a hundred ren high, yet a lame ewe grazes upon it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mount Tai is a hundred ren high, yet a lame ewe grazes on it.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫樓季而難五丈之限，豈跛牂而易百仞之高哉？
manualTranslations.literal: If Lou Ji finds five ren difficult, how can a lame ewe find a hundred ren easy?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Lou Ji finds five ren difficult, how can a lame ewe find a hundred ren easy?

manualTranslations.zh: 峭漸之埶異也。
manualTranslations.literal: The steepness of the gradient differs."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The steepness of the slope differs."

manualTranslations.zh: 」爾雅曰：「羊牝曰牂。
manualTranslations.literal: The Erya says: "A female sheep is called zang."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Erya says: "A female sheep is called zang."

manualTranslations.zh: 」易曰：「天險不可昇，地險山川丘陵也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Changes says: "Heaven's barrier cannot be ascended; earth's barrier is mountains, rivers, hills, and mounds."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "Heaven's barrier cannot be ascended; earth's barrier is mountains, rivers, hills, and mounds."

manualTranslations.zh: 」案表跋扈，擅誅列侯，遏絕詔命，斷盜貢篚，鄭玄注儀禮曰：「篚，竹器如筐也。
manualTranslations.literal: Examining Biao's case: he is overbearing, executes marquises on his own authority, blocks imperial edicts, cuts off and steals tribute baskets—Zheng Xuan annotates the Ceremonial: "Fei is a bamboo vessel like a basket.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Examining Biao: he is overbearing, executes marquises on his own authority, blocks edicts, and steals tribute baskets—Zheng Xuan glosses the Ceremonial: "Fei is a bamboo vessel like a basket.

manualTranslations.zh: 」書曰：「厥篚玄纁璣組。
manualTranslations.literal: The Documents says: "Their baskets hold black and crimson silk with embroidered clasps."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Documents says: "Their baskets hold black and crimson silk with embroidered clasps."

manualTranslations.zh: 」招呼元惡，以自營衞，專爲羣逆，主萃淵藪。
manualTranslations.literal: He summons chief villains to guard himself, devotes himself to the company of rebels, and hosts the gathering of the deep pool and marsh."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He summons chief villains as guards, devotes himself to rebels, and hosts outlaws in deep pools and marshes."

manualTranslations.zh: 」孔注曰：「天下罪人逃亡者，而紂爲魁主，窟聚泉府藪澤也。
manualTranslations.literal: Kong's annotation: "Fugitives and criminals of all under Heaven—and Zhou as their chief leader, gathering in caves, treasuries, marshes, and lakes."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kong's gloss: "Fugitives of all under Heaven—and Zhou as their chief, gathering in caves, treasuries, marshes, and lakes."

manualTranslations.zh: 」郜鼎在廟，章孰甚焉！
manualTranslations.literal: The great cauldron of Gao in the ancestral temple—what display could be more glaring!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The great cauldron of Gao in the ancestral temple—what display could be more glaring!

manualTranslations.zh: 左傳：「取郜大鼎于宋，戊申納于太廟。
manualTranslations.literal: The Zuo Commentary: "They took the great cauldron of Gao from Song; on day wushen it was placed in the Grand Temple.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary: "They took the great cauldron of Gao from Song and on wushen placed it in the Grand Temple.

manualTranslations.zh: 臧哀伯諫曰：『君人者，昭德塞違，以臨照百官，百官於是乎戒懼。
manualTranslations.literal: Zang Aibo remonstrated: 'A ruler should display virtue and block transgression to oversee the hundred officials—then the hundred officials will be on guard and in fear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zang Aibo remonstrated: "A ruler should display virtue and block transgression to oversee officials—then officials will be on guard and in fear.

manualTranslations.zh: 郜鼎在廟，彰孰甚焉！
manualTranslations.literal: The cauldron of Gao in the temple—what display could be more glaring!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The cauldron of Gao in the temple—what display could be more glaring!

manualTranslations.zh: 』」郜鼎，郜國所作也。
manualTranslations.literal: The cauldron of Gao was made by the state of Gao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The cauldron of Gao was made by the state of Gao.

manualTranslations.zh: 桑落瓦解，其埶可見。
manualTranslations.literal: Mulberry leaves fall and structures collapse—the trend can be seen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mulberry leaves fall and structures collapse—the trend is plain.

manualTranslations.zh: 詩曰：「桑之落矣，其黃而隕。
manualTranslations.literal: The Odes says: "The mulberry is falling, yellow and dropping."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Odes says: "The mulberry is falling, yellow and dropping."

manualTranslations.zh: 」臣愚以爲宜隱郊祀之事，以崇國防。
manualTranslations.literal: I hold that the suburban sacrifice affair should be concealed to uphold the state's defenses."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I hold the suburban sacrifice affair should be concealed to uphold the state's defenses."

manualTranslations.zh: 」五年，南陽王馮、東海王祗薨，並獻帝子。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year Prince Feng of Nanyang and Prince Zhi of Donghai died—both were sons of Emperor Xian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Prince Feng of Nanyang and Prince Zhi of Donghai died—both sons of Emperor Xian.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝傷其早歿，欲爲脩四時之祭，以訪於融。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor grieved their early deaths and wished to establish seasonal sacrifices for them; he consulted Kong Rong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved their early deaths and wished to establish seasonal sacrifices; he consulted Kong Rong.

manualTranslations.zh: 融對曰：「聖恩敦睦，感時增思，悼二王之靈，發哀愍之詔，稽度前典，以正禮制。
manualTranslations.literal: Kong Rong replied: "The sacred grace is warm in kinship; moved by the season you increase your thoughts, mourn the spirits of the two princes, and issue a decree of pity and compassion—examining former canons to set right ritual institutions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kong Rong replied: "Your sacred grace is warm in kinship; mourning the two princes you issue a decree of compassion and examine former canons to set ritual right.

manualTranslations.zh: 竊觀故事，前梁懷王、臨江愍王、齊哀王、臨淮懷王並薨無後，同產昆弟，即景、武、昭、明四帝是也，梁懷王揖，景帝弟也，立十年薨。
manualTranslations.literal: Privately observing precedents: former Princes Huai of Liang, Min of Linjiang, Ai of Qi, and Huai of Linhuai all died without heirs—they were full brothers of Emperors Jing, Wu, Zhao, and Ming respectively. Prince Huai of Liang, Yi, was Emperor Jing's younger brother; enthroned ten years then died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Precedents show Princes Huai of Liang, Min of Linjiang, Ai of Qi, and Huai of Linhuai all died without heirs—they were full brothers of Emperors Jing, Wu, Zhao, and Ming. Prince Huai of Liang, Yi, was Emperor Jing's brother and died after ten years.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨江閔王榮，武帝兄也，爲皇太子，四歲廢爲王，坐侵廟壖地自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Prince Min of Linjiang, Rong, was Emperor Wu's elder brother; he was crown prince, deposed after four years to be a prince, and killed himself for encroaching on temple precinct land.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prince Min of Linjiang, Rong, was Emperor Wu's elder brother, crown prince for four years before deposition; he killed himself for encroaching on temple land.

manualTranslations.zh: 齊懷王閎，武帝子，昭帝異母兄，立八年薨。
manualTranslations.literal: Prince Huai of Qi, Hong, was Emperor Wu's son and Emperor Zhao's elder half-brother; enthroned eight years then died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Qi, Hong, was Emperor Wu's son and Emperor Zhao's elder half-brother; he died after eight years.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣賢案：齊哀王，悼惠王之子，高帝之孫，非昭帝兄弟，當爲懷王，作「哀」者誤也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Xian notes: Prince Ai of Qi was Prince Daohui's son and the High Emperor's grandson—not Emperor Zhao's brother; it should read Prince Huai; writing "Ai" is an error.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commentator Xian notes: Prince Ai of Qi was Prince Daohui's son and the High Emperor's grandson—not Emperor Zhao's brother; "Huai" is correct and "Ai" is an error.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨淮公衡，明帝弟，建武十五年立，未及進爵爲王而薨。
manualTranslations.literal: Duke Heng of Linhuai was Emperor Ming's younger brother; established in Jianwu 15, he died before advancing in rank to prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Duke Heng of Linhuai was Emperor Ming's brother, established in Jianwu 15, and died before advancing to princely rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 融家傳及本傳皆作「公」，此爲「王」者，亦誤也。
manualTranslations.literal: Kong Rong's family biography and this biography both read "duke"; writing "prince" here is also an error.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kong Rong's family biography and this biography both read "duke"; "prince" here is also an error.

manualTranslations.zh: 未聞前朝修立祭祀。
manualTranslations.literal: I have not heard that former dynasties established sacrifices for them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have not heard that former dynasties established sacrifices for such cases.

manualTranslations.zh: 若臨時所施，則不列傳紀。
manualTranslations.literal: If it were a temporary measure it would not be entered in the annals.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Temporary measures are not entered in the annals.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣愚以爲諸在冲齔，聖慈哀悼，禮同成人，加以號謚者，宜稱上恩，稱音尺證反。
manualTranslations.literal: I hold that for those still in infancy, though the sacred compassion mourns them and ritual equals an adult with posthumous title added, it should be called an expression of imperial grace—cheng is read chi-zheng fan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For those still in infancy, though imperial compassion mourns them and ritual equals an adult with posthumous title, it should be called an expression of imperial grace—cheng is read chi-zheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 祭祀禮畢，而後絕之。
manualTranslations.literal: Once sacrificial rites are complete, then cease them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once sacrificial rites are complete, then cease them.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於一歲之限，不合禮意，又違先帝已然之法，所未敢處。
manualTranslations.literal: As for a limit of one year, it does not accord with ritual intent and also violates methods already established by the former emperor—I dare not settle it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A limit of one year does not accord with ritual and violates methods already established by the former emperor—I dare not approve it.

manualTranslations.zh: 」處猶安也。
manualTranslations.literal: Chu means to settle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chu means to settle or approve.

localRange.text: 校勘記二二五七頁三行司農觿之曾孫也按：「曾孫」當作「玄孫」。泰弟渾，魏志有傳，雲高祖父觿，則泰乃觿之玄孫也。二二五八頁一一行將各*(基)**[潟]*峙刊誤謂案文「基」當作「潟」，謂如潟不動。按：王先謙謂魏志鄭渾傳注引張璠漢紀作「潟峙」。今據改。二二五八頁一二行婦女猶戴戟操矛按：王先謙謂戟不能戴，魏志鄭渾傳注引張璠漢紀作「載戟」。二二五八頁一三行百姓所畏者有並涼之人按：刊誤謂案文多一「有」字。二二五九頁一五行說菀曰汲本、殿本「菀」作「苑」。按：菀苑通。二二五九頁一五行聲響動天按：「響」原斗「向」，逕改正。二二六０頁一０行景帝*(二)**[三]*年反據殿本改。二二六０頁一四行年四十一汲本、殿本作「四十二」。按：魏志鄭渾傳注作「四十一」，盧弼校雲宋本作「四十二」。二二六一頁三行霸字次*(孺)**[儒]*據汲本、殿本改，與前書合。二二六一頁七行太中大夫陳煒按：袁紀「煒」作「禕」。二二六一頁九行將不早惠乎殿本「惠」作「慧」，冊府元龜七七三卷同。按：惠慧通。二二六一頁九行高明必為偉器按：王先謙謂世說注引續漢書，「高明」上有「長大」二字，似不可少。二二六二頁一行年十三喪父按：校補引沉銘彝說，謂融父宙卒於桓帝延熹六年正月己未，見孔宙碑，以融卒年計之，則宙卒時，融年十一，非十三也。二二六二頁三行時融年十六按：校補引侯康說，謂詔捕張儉事在建寧二年，融年十七矣。二二六三頁六行拜中軍候刊誤謂漢官無中軍候，惟有北軍中候耳，明字有脫誤。按：校補引錢大昭說，謂魏志崔琰傳注云「累遷北軍中候」此作「中軍候」，誤。二二六五頁一六行*(及)**[反]*魯□之侵地刊誤謂案公羊傳本文，「及」當作「反」。今據改。按：以下注所引公羊傳文與今本多不合，然意義無大出入。二二六六頁一０行善否不別按：御覽六四八引續漢書，「不別」作「區別」。二二六六頁一三行是下常有千八百紂也按：刊誤謂「是」下少一「天」字。二二六八頁七行軍半至刊誤謂案史記，彼文更有他語，故未云「軍半至」，今既節取，不宜長此三字。今按：史記作「兵法，百里而趣利者蹶上將，五十里而趣利者軍半至。二二六八頁一０行於是令齊軍曰按：史記無「曰」字。二二六八頁一０行期日莫見火舉而俱發按：史記「日」作「曰」。二二七０頁九行苞茅不入汲本、殿本「苞」作「包」。按：阮元謂「包茅不入」之「包」，原從艸作「苞」，自石經始去艸頭，後人往往從之。二二七０頁九行包裡束也按：「裡」原斗「裡」，逕改正。二二七一頁八行並獻帝子按：校補謂以融所對聖恩敦睦及同產昆弟之說證之，實皆獻帝之諸弟，而靈帝子耳。疑此注本作「並靈帝子」，淺人妄改為「獻」。二二七二頁一０行單于徙北海上按：張森楷校勘記謂「徙」下疑有「之」字。二二七四頁二行獻帝嘗時見慮按：刊誤謂案文「時」當作「特」。二二七四頁一五行令宗欽馮愔守栒邑按：集解引周壽昌說，謂案鄧禹傳，「宗欽」作「宗歆」。二二七六頁一三行令信出跨下汲本、殿本「跨」作「胯」。按：跨胯同。二二七七頁一行酒酸*(者)*據今本韓非子刪。二二七七頁一行*(二人)**[倩]*曰汝狗猛耶據今本韓非子改。二二七七頁五行*[曰然谷]*將□之按：韓非子作「曰然谷將棄之」，此脫「曰然谷」三字，今據補。二二七八頁八行譬如寄物燦中按：殿本「燦」作「瓶」。二二七九頁二行燦缶也按：沈家本謂按說文，缾，□也，瓶缾或從□。此注言缶也，疑傳寫奪爛其半耳。「瓶」字本或作「燦」者誤，說文無燦字也。二二八０頁三行豈有員□委屈可以每其生哉汲本「有員」作「其負」。校補謂負，恃也，恃員道以為委屈也。□可通員，作「員□」於義為窒，似誤。今按：員□委屈，相對成文，古人自有復語耳，作「負」者鬥，校補說非。二二八一頁一一行亢父*[縣]*屬梁國據汲本、殿本補。二二八一頁一五行彧明有意數按：刊誤謂「明」上當有一「聰」字。二二八二頁一行明年又為操鎮東司馬按：集解引錢大昕說，謂此初平二年之明年也。據魏志，操為鎮東將軍在建安元年，則初平三年安得便稱鎮東司馬乎？魏志彧傳本雲明年太祖領兗州牧，後為鎮東將軍，常以司馬從。然則領兗州在此年，而除鎮東不在此年也。范史刪去領兗州句，遂誤以鎮東司馬為是年事矣。二二八二頁六行宜亟供軍實按：集解引惠棟說，謂「實」魏志作「食」。二二八三頁六行而將軍之關河也按：集解引錢大昕說，謂「關河」當依魏志彧傳作「關中河內」，蓋上言高祖保關中，光武據河內，皆深根固本，以制天下，故以兗州比關中、河內。范史刪去二字，未當。二二八三頁一五行東郡守按：刊誤謂案文少一「太」字。二二八六頁八行*[書]*與彧議據殿本補。按：下文云「彧報曰」，則此當有「書」字。二二八九頁二行各規利人百其勇也按：「各」原斗「名」，逕改正。二二八九頁七行發[縱]指示功人也據汲本補。二二九０頁五行國之*(望)**[重]*臣據汲本、殿本改。

sourceRange.text: 興平元年，操東擊陶謙，使彧守甄城，縣名，屬濟陰郡，今濮州縣也。「甄」今作「鄄」，音絹。任以留事。會張邈、陳宮以兖州反操，《典略》「宮字公臺，東郡人。剛直烈壯，少與海內知名之士皆相連結」也。而潛迎呂布。布旣至，諸城悉應之。邈乃使人譎彧曰：譎，詐也。「呂將軍來助曹使君擊陶謙，宜亟供軍實。」彧知邈有變，即勒兵設備，故邈計不行。豫州刺史郭貢率兵數萬來到城下，求見彧。彧將往，東郡太守夏侯惇等止之。《魏志》曰：「惇字元讓，沛國人。」曰：「何知貢不與呂布同謀，而輕欲見之。今君爲一州之鎮，往必危也。」彧曰：「貢與邈等分非素結，今來速者，計必未定，及其猶豫，宜時說之，縱不爲用，可使中立。不令其有去就也。若先懷疑嫌，彼將怒而成謀，不如往也。」貢旣見彧無懼意，知城不可攻，遂引而去。彧乃使程昱說范、東阿，魏志：「昱字仲德，東郡東阿人。」范，縣，屬東郡，今濮陽縣也。東阿，縣，屬東郡，今濟州縣也。使固其守，卒全三城以待操焉。三城謂甄、范、東阿也。

manualTranslations.zh: 興平元年，操東擊陶謙，使彧守甄城，縣名，屬濟陰郡，今濮州縣也。
manualTranslations.literal: In Xingping 1 Cao Cao marched east against Tao Qian and left Xun Yu to hold Zhen city—a county seat in Jiyin commandery, present-day Puzhou county.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xingping 1 (194 CE) Cao Cao marched east against Tao Qian and left Xun Yu to hold Juancheng, a county seat in Jiyin commandery, in present-day Puzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 「甄」今作「鄄」，音絹。
manualTranslations.literal: "Zhen" is now written "Juan," pronounced juan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Zhen" is now written Juan, pronounced juan.

manualTranslations.zh: 任以留事。
manualTranslations.literal: He was entrusted with affairs left behind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao entrusted him with affairs at home.

manualTranslations.zh: 會張邈、陳宮以兖州反操，《典略》「宮字公臺，東郡人。
manualTranslations.literal: Just then Zhang Miao and Chen Gong rebelled against Cao Cao in Yan Province—the Dianlüe says: "Gong, courtesy name Gongtai, was a man of Dong commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that moment Zhang Miao and Chen Gong turned Yan Province against Cao Cao. The Dianlüe says Chen Gong, courtesy name Gongtai, came from Dong commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 剛直烈壯，少與海內知名之士皆相連結」也。
manualTranslations.literal: Upright, stern, and bold; from youth he was linked with famous men throughout the realm."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was upright and bold, and from youth had ties with famous men throughout the realm."

manualTranslations.zh: 而潛迎呂布。
manualTranslations.literal: They secretly welcomed Lü Bu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They secretly welcomed Lü Bu.

manualTranslations.zh: 布旣至，諸城悉應之。
manualTranslations.literal: Once Bu arrived, all the cities responded to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Lü Bu arrived, cities throughout the province declared for him.

manualTranslations.zh: 邈乃使人譎彧曰：譎，詐也。
manualTranslations.literal: Miao then sent someone to deceive Xun Yu, saying—jie means to deceive:
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Miao then sent a man to trick Xun Yu—jie means to deceive:

manualTranslations.zh: 「呂將軍來助曹使君擊陶謙，宜亟供軍實。
manualTranslations.literal: "General Lü has come to aid Lord Cao in attacking Tao Qian—you should urgently supply military stores."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "General Lü has come to help Lord Cao attack Tao Qian. You should urgently supply military provisions."

manualTranslations.zh: 」彧知邈有變，即勒兵設備，故邈計不行。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun Yu knew Miao had turned traitor and at once mustered troops and made preparations, so Miao's plan failed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Yu knew Miao had turned traitor, mustered troops, and made preparations, so the plot failed.

manualTranslations.zh: 豫州刺史郭貢率兵數萬來到城下，求見彧。
manualTranslations.literal: Inspector of Yuzhou Guo Gong led several tens of thousands of troops to the foot of the city walls and asked to see Xun Yu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yuzhou Guo Gong marched tens of thousands of men to the city and asked to meet Xun Yu.

manualTranslations.zh: 彧將往，東郡太守夏侯惇等止之。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun Yu was about to go when Dong commandery Administrator Xiahou Dun and others stopped him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Yu was about to go when Dong commandery Administrator Xiahou Dun and others stopped him.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏志》曰：「惇字元讓，沛國人。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Records says: "Dun, courtesy name Yuanrang, was a man of Pei."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei Records says: "Dun, courtesy name Yuanrang, came from Pei."

manualTranslations.zh: 」曰：「何知貢不與呂布同謀，而輕欲見之。
manualTranslations.literal: They said: "How do you know Gong is not in league with Lü Bu, yet you lightly wish to see him?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They said: "How do you know Guo Gong is not in league with Lü Bu, yet you would go to meet him so lightly?

manualTranslations.zh: 今君爲一州之鎮，往必危也。
manualTranslations.literal: You are now the pillar of a whole province; if you go you will surely be in danger."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You are the linchpin of the province—if you go, you will be in mortal danger."

manualTranslations.zh: 」彧曰：「貢與邈等分非素結，今來速者，計必未定，及其猶豫，宜時說之，縱不爲用，可使中立。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun Yu said: "Gong and Miao and the others are not old allies by nature. He has come quickly, so his plans cannot yet be settled. While he is still hesitating I should persuade him; even if he will not be used by us, we can make him remain neutral.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Yu replied: "Guo Gong is no longtime ally of Miao and the rest. He arrived in haste, so his plans cannot be firm yet. If I speak to him before he decides, I may not win him over—but I can at least keep him neutral.

manualTranslations.zh: 不令其有去就也。
manualTranslations.literal: We must not let him choose sides.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We must not let him commit to either side.

manualTranslations.zh: 若先懷疑嫌，彼將怒而成謀，不如往也。
manualTranslations.literal: If we show suspicion first, he will grow angry and settle on a plan—it is better to go."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If we show suspicion first, he will take offense and commit to their side—it is better to go."

manualTranslations.zh: 」貢旣見彧無懼意，知城不可攻，遂引而去。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gong saw that Xun Yu showed no fear, he knew the city could not be taken and led his troops away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Guo Gong saw that Xun Yu showed no fear, he decided the city would not fall easily and withdrew.

manualTranslations.zh: 彧乃使程昱說范、東阿，魏志：「昱字仲德，東郡東阿人。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun Yu then sent Cheng Yu to persuade Fan and Dong'e—the Wei Records: "Yu, courtesy name Zhongde, was a man of Dong'e in Dong commandery."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Yu then sent Cheng Yu to rally Fan and Dong'e. The Wei Records says: "Yu, courtesy name Zhongde, came from Dong'e in Dong commandery."

manualTranslations.zh: 」范，縣，屬東郡，今濮陽縣也。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan is a county in Dong commandery, present-day Puyang county.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan was a county in Dong commandery, in present-day Puyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 東阿，縣，屬東郡，今濟州縣也。
manualTranslations.literal: Dong'e is a county in Dong commandery, present-day Jizhou county.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong'e was a county in Dong commandery, in present-day Jizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 使固其守，卒全三城以待操焉。
manualTranslations.literal: He made them hold firm in their defense and in the end preserved all three cities to await Cao Cao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He secured their defenses and in the end preserved all three cities until Cao Cao returned.

manualTranslations.zh: 三城謂甄、范、東阿也。
manualTranslations.literal: The three cities mean Zhen, Fan, and Dong'e.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The three cities were Juancheng, Fan, and Dong'e.

sourceRange.text: 時年飢兵興，操表制酒禁，融頻書爭之，多侮慢之辭。融集與操書云：「酒之爲德乆矣。古先哲王，類帝禋宗，和神定人，以濟萬國，非酒莫以也。故天垂酒星之燿，地列酒泉之郡，人著旨酒之德。堯不千鍾，無以建太平。孔非百觚，無以堪上聖。樊噲解戹鴻門，非豕肩鍾酒，無以奮其怒。趙之廝養，東迎其王，非引巵酒，無以激其氣。高祖非醉斬白蛇，無以暢其靈。景帝非醉幸唐姬，無以開中興。袁盎非醇醪之力，無以脫其命。定國不酣飲一斛，無以決其法。故酈生以高陽酒徒，著功於漢；屈原不餔醩歠醨，取困於楚。由是觀之，酒何負於政哉？」又書曰：「昨承訓荅，陳二代之禍，及衆人之敗，以酒亡者，實如來誨。雖然，徐偃王行仁義而亡，今令不絕仁義；燕噲以讓失社稷，今令不禁謙退；魯因儒而損，今令不棄文學；夏、商亦以婦人失天下，今令不斷婚姻。而將酒獨急者，疑但惜穀耳，非以亡王爲戒也。」旣見操雄詐漸著，數不能堪，故發辭偏宕，偏邪跌宕，不拘正理。多致乖忤。又甞奏宜準古王畿之制，千里寰內，不以封建諸侯。《周禮》：「方千里曰國畿，其外五百里侯畿。」鄭玄注：「畿，限也。」操疑其所論建漸廣，益憚之。然以融名重天下，外相容忍，而潛忌正議，慮鯁大業。山陽郗慮承望風旨，續漢書：「慮字鴻豫，山陽高平人，少受學於鄭玄。」虞浦《江表傳》曰：「獻帝甞時見慮及少府孔融。問融曰：『鴻豫何所優長？』融曰：『可與適道，未可與權。』慮舉笏曰：『融昔宰北海，政散人流，其權安在？』遂與融互相長短，以至不穆。曹操以書和解之。」慮從光祿勳遷御史大夫。以微法奏免融官。因顯明讎怨，操故書激厲融曰：「蓋聞唐虞之朝，有克讓之臣，《尚書》曰，舜以伯禹爲司空，禹讓稷、契暨皐陶。以益爲朕虞，益讓于朱虎、熊羆。以伯夷爲秩宗，伯夷讓于夔龍。故麟鳳來而頌聲作也。史記曰：「於是禹興九韶之樂，致異物，鳳皇來儀。」後世德薄，猶有殺身爲君，若齊孟陽代君居床以待賊，西漢紀信乘黃屋誑楚之類也。破家爲國。若要離焚妻子以徇吳，李通誅宗族以從漢之類也。及至其敝，睚眦之怨必讎，一餐之惠必報。史記，范雎一餐之德必償，睚眦之怨必報。故鼂錯念國，遘禍於袁盎；景帝時，錯爲御史大夫，以諸侯國大，請削其土。吳楚七國反，以誅錯爲名。袁盎素與錯不相善，盎乃進說，請斬錯以謝七國，景帝遂斬錯也。屈平悼楚，受譖於椒、蘭；屈平楚懷王時爲三閭大夫。秦昭王使張儀譎詐懷王，令絕齊交，又誘請會武關，平諫，王不聽其言，卒客死於秦。懷王子子椒、子蘭讒之於襄王，而放逐之。見史記。彭寵傾亂，起自朱浮；朱浮與寵不相能，數譖之光武，寵遂反。鄧禹威損，失於宗、馮。鄧禹征赤眉，令宗欽、馮愔守栒邑。二人爭權相攻，遂殺欽，因反擊禹。今流俗本「宗」誤作「宋」也。由此言之，喜怒怨愛，禍福所因，可不慎與！音余。昔廉、藺小國之臣，猶能相下；趙惠文王與秦昭王會黽池，歸，拜藺相如爲上卿，位在廉頗右。頗曰；「吾不忍爲之下，必辱之。」相如每朝，常避之。頗聞之，肉袒負荊謝之，相與爲刎頸之友。事見《史記》。寇、賈倉卒武夫，屈節崇好；光武不問伯升之怨；齊侯不疑射鉤之虜。公子糾與桓公爭立，管仲射桓公中鉤。後桓公即位，以管仲爲相也。夫立大操者，豈累細故哉！往聞二君有執法之平，以爲小介，介猶蔕芥也。公法雖平，私情爲蔕芥者也。當收舊好；而怨毒漸積，志相危害，聞之憮然，憮音舞。憮，失意貌也。中夜而起。昔國家東遷，文舉盛歎鴻豫名實相副，綜達經學，出於鄭玄，又明司馬法，史記，齊威王使大夫追論古者司馬法。其法論田及兵之法也。鴻豫亦稱文舉竒逸博聞，誠怪今者與始相違。孤與文舉旣非舊好，又於鴻豫亦無恩紀，然願人之相美，不樂人之相傷，是以區區思協歡好。又知二君羣小所搆，孤爲人臣，進不能風化海內，退不能建德和人，然撫養戰士，殺身爲國，破浮華交會之徒，計有餘矣。」融報曰：「猥惠書敎，猥，曲也。

localRange.text: 融報曰：「猥惠書敎，〈猥，曲也。
