manualTranslations.idiomatic: Black: water spirits levy tribute, rivers burst, and bandits rise everywhere.”

manualTranslations.zh: 韓揚占曰：「其象若竹彗、樹木條，長短無常。
manualTranslations.literal: Han Yang’s prognostication says: “Its form is like a bamboo broom or tree branches—length and shortness are irregular.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Yang’s canon says: “Its form resembles a bamboo broom or tree branches—length varies without rule.

manualTranslations.zh: 其長大見久，災深；
manualTranslations.literal: If large and long and visible for long, the disaster is deep;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Large and long-lived, the disaster runs deep;

manualTranslations.zh: 短小見不久，災狹。
manualTranslations.literal: if small and short and visible briefly, the disaster is narrow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: small and brief, the disaster is narrow.”

manualTranslations.zh: 」晏子春秋曰：「齊景公睹彗星，使伯常騫攘之。
manualTranslations.literal: ” The Spring and Autumn of Master Yan says: “Duke Jing of Qi saw a comet and sent Bo Changqian to expel it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Yanzi Chunqiu records: “Duke Jing of Qi saw a comet and sent Bo Changqian to drive it away.

manualTranslations.zh: 晏子曰：『不可。
manualTranslations.literal: Yanzi said: “It cannot be done.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yanzi said, “No.

manualTranslations.zh: 此天教也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is Heaven’s instruction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is Heaven’s instruction.

manualTranslations.zh: 日月之氣，風雨不時，彗星之出，天為民之亂見之。
manualTranslations.literal: The qi of sun and moon is out of season, wind and rain are untimely—the comet’s appearance is Heaven showing the people’s disorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When sun and moon lose their season and wind and rain fail, a comet appears because Heaven displays the people’s disorder.

manualTranslations.zh: 』」又一曰：「景公彗星出而泣，晏子問之。
manualTranslations.literal: ”’” Another account says: “When the comet appeared Duke Jing wept; Yanzi asked him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: ”’” Another version says: “When the comet appeared Duke Jing wept. Yanzi asked why.

manualTranslations.zh: 公曰：『寡人聞之，彗星出，其所向之國君當之。
manualTranslations.literal: The duke said: “I have heard that when a comet appears, the ruler of the state it faces must bear it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The duke said, “I have heard that when a comet appears, the ruler of the state it faces must bear the omen.

manualTranslations.zh: 今彗星出而向吾國，我是以悲。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the comet faces our state—that is why I grieve.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now it faces our state—that is why I grieve.

manualTranslations.zh: 』晏子曰：『君之行義〔回邪〕，無德於國。
manualTranslations.literal: ” Yanzi said: “Your lordship’s conduct is perverse and crooked; you have no virtue for the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: ” Yanzi said, “Your lordship’s conduct is crooked; you have no virtue for the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 穿〔陂〕池，則欲其深以廣也，為臺榭則欲其高且大也。
manualTranslations.literal: When digging pools you want them deep and wide; when building terraces and pavilions you want them high and large.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You dig pools deep and wide; you build terraces high and vast.

manualTranslations.zh: 賦斂如撝奪，誅戮如仇讎。
manualTranslations.literal: Taxes are levied like plunder; executions are like settling scores with enemies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taxes are seized like plunder; executions fall like vengeance on enemies.

manualTranslations.zh: 自是觀之，孛又將出。
manualTranslations.literal: Viewed from this, a broom star will appear again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, a broom star will appear again.

manualTranslations.zh: 彗星之出，庸何〔懼〕乎？
manualTranslations.literal: When a comet appears, what is there to fear?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When a comet appears, what is there to fear?

manualTranslations.zh: 』」案：如晏子之言，孛之與彗，如似匪同。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: ”’ Commentary: as Yanzi suggests, broom stars and comets are not quite the same thing.

sourceRange.text: 星經曰：「歲星主泰山，徐州、青州、兗州。熒惑主霍山，楊州、荊州、交州。鎮星主嵩高山，豫州。太白主華陰山，涼州、雍州、益州。辰星主恆山，冀州、幽州、并州。歲星主角、亢、氐、房、心、尾、箕。熒惑主輿鬼、柳、七星、張、翼、軫。鎮星主東井。太白主奎、婁、胃、昴、畢、觜、參。辰星主斗、牛、女、虛、危、室、壁。琁、璣者，謂北極星也。玉衡者，謂斗九星也。玉衡第一星主徐州，常以五子日候之，甲子為東海，丙子為琅邪，戊子為彭城，庚子為下邳，壬子為廣陵，凡五郡。第二星主益州，常以五亥日候之，乙亥為漢中，丁亥為永昌，己亥為巴郡、蜀郡、牂牁，辛亥為廣漢，癸亥為犍為，凡七郡。第三星主冀州，常以五戌日候之，甲戌為魏郡、勃海，丙戌為安平，戊戌為鉅鹿、河閒，庚戌為清河、趙國，壬戌為恆山，凡八郡。第四星主荊州，常以五卯日候之，乙卯為南陽，己卯為零陵，辛卯為桂陽，癸卯為長沙，丁卯為武陵，凡五郡。第五星主兗州，常以五辰日候之，甲辰為東郡、陳留，丙辰為濟北，戊辰為山陽、泰山，庚辰為濟陰，壬辰為東平、任城，凡八郡。第六星主揚州，常以五巳日候之，乙巳為豫章，辛巳為丹陽，己巳為廬江，丁巳為吳郡、會稽，癸巳為九江，凡六郡。第七星為豫州，常以五午日候之，甲午為潁川，壬午為梁國，丙午為汝南，戊午為沛國，庚午為魯國，凡五郡。第八星主幽州，常以五寅日候之，甲寅為玄菟，丙寅為遼東、遼西、漁陽，庚寅為上谷、代郡，壬寅為廣陽，戊寅為涿郡，凡八郡。第九星主并州，常以五申日候之，甲申為五原、鴈門，丙申為朔方、雲中，戊申為西河，庚申為太原、定襄，壬申為上黨，凡八郡。琁、璣、玉衡占色，春青黃，夏赤黃，秋白黃，冬黑黃。此是常明；不如此者，所向國有兵殃起。凡有六十郡，九州所領，自有分而名焉。」三皇邁化，協神醇朴，謂五星如連珠，日月若合璧。化由自然，民不犯慝。至於書契之興，五帝是作。軒轅始受《河圖斗苞授》，規日月星辰之象，故星官之書自黄帝始。至高陽氏，使南正重司天，北正黎司地。唐、虞之時，羲仲、和仲，尚書曰：「帝在琁璣玉衡，以齊七政。」孔安國曰：「在，察也。琁，美玉也。璣衡，王者正天文之器，可運轉者。七政，日月五星各異政。舜察天文，齊七政也。」夏有昆吾，湯則巫咸，周之史佚、萇弘，宋之子韦，楚之唐蔑，魯之梓慎，鄭之裨竈，魏石中夫，或云石申父。齐国甘公，皆掌天文之官。仰占俯視，以佐時政；步變擿微，通洞密至；採禍福之原，覩成敗之勢。秦燔《詩》、《書》，以愚百姓，六經典籍，殘為灰炭，星官之書，全而不毁。故《秦史》書始皇之時，彗孛大角，大角以亡，有大星與小星斗於宫中，是其廢亡之征。至漢興，景、武之際，司馬談，談子遷，以世黎氏之后，為太史令，遷著《史记》，作《天官書》。成帝時，中垒校尉劉向，广《洪范》灾条作五纪皇极之论，以参往行之事。孝明帝使班固叙《漢書》，而馬續述《天文志》。謝沈書曰：「蔡邕撰建武已後，星驗著明，以續前志，譙周接繼其下者。」今紹《漢書》作《天文志》，起王莽居摄元年，迄孝獻帝建安二十五年，二百一十五載。言其時星辰之變，表象之應，以顯天戒，明王事焉。臣昭以張衡天文之妙，冠絕一代。所著靈憲、渾儀，略具辰燿之本，今寫載以備其理焉。靈憲曰：「昔在先王，將步天路，用〔定〕靈軌，尋緒本元。先準之于渾體，是為正儀立度，而皇極有逌建也，樞運有逌稽也。乃建乃稽，斯經天常。聖人無心，因茲以生心，故靈憲作興。曰：太素之前，幽清玄靜，寂漠冥默，不可為象，厥中惟虛，厥外惟無。如是者永久焉，斯謂溟涬，蓋乃道之根也。道根既建，自無生有。太素始萌，萌而未兆，并氣同色，渾沌不分。故道志之言云：『有物渾成，先天地生。』其氣體固未可得而形，其遲速固未可得而紀也。如是者又永久焉，斯為庬鴻，蓋乃道之幹也。道幹既育，有物成體。於是元氣剖判，剛柔始分，清濁異位。天成於外，地定於內。天體於陽，故圓以動；地體於陰，故平以靜。動以行施，靜以合化，堙鬱構精，時育庶類，斯謂太元，蓋乃道之實也。在天成象，在地成形。天有九位，地有九域；天有三辰，地有三形；有象可效，有形可度。情性萬殊，旁通感薄，自然相生，莫之能紀。於是人之精者作聖。實始紀綱而經緯之。八極之維，徑二億三萬二千三百里，南北則短減千里，東西則廣增千里。自地至天，半於八極，則地之深亦如之。通而度之，則是渾已。將覆其數，用重鉤股，懸天之景，薄地之義，皆移千里而差一寸得之。過此而往者，未之或知也。未之或知者，宇宙之謂也。宇之表無極，宙之端無窮。天有兩儀，以儛道中。其可睹，樞星是也，謂之北極。在南者不著，故聖人弗之名焉。其世之遂，九分而減二。陽道左迴，故天運左行。有驗於物，則人氣左羸，形左繚也。天以陽迴，地以陰淳。是故天致其動，稟氣舒光；地致其靜，承施候明。天以順動，不失其中，則四序順至，寒暑不減，致生有節，故品物用生。地以靈靜，作合承天，清化致養，四時而後育，故品物用成。凡至大莫如天，至厚莫若地。（地）至質者曰地而已。至多莫若水，水精為漢，漢用於天而無列焉，思次質也。地有山獄，以宣其氣，精種為星。星也者，體生於地，精成於天，列居錯跱，各有逌屬。紫宮為皇極之居，太微為五帝之廷。明堂之房，大角有席，天巿有坐。蒼龍連蜷於左，白虎猛據於右，朱雀奮翼於前，靈龜圈首於後，黃神軒轅於中。六擾既畜，而狼蚖魚鱉罔有不具。在野象物，在朝象官，在人象事，於是備矣。懸象著明，莫大乎日月。其徑當天周七百三十六分之一，地廣二百四十二分之一。日者，陽精之宗。積而成鳥，象烏而有三趾。陽之類，其數奇。月者，陰精之宗。積而成獸，象兔。陰之類，其數耦。其後有馮焉者。羿請無死之藥於西王母，姮娥竊之以奔月。將往，枚筮之於有黃，有黃占之曰：『吉。翩翩歸妹，獨將西行，逢天晦芒，毋驚毋恐，後其大昌。』姮娥遂託身于月，是為蟾蠩。夫日譬猶火，月譬猶水，火則外光，水則含景。故月光生於日之所照，魄生於日之所蔽，當日則光盈，就日則光盡也。眾星被燿，因水轉光。當日之衝，光常不合者，蔽於〔地〕也。是謂闇虛。在星星微，月過則食。日之薄地，其明也。繇暗視明，明無所屈，是以望之若火。方於中天，天地同明。繇明瞻暗，暗還自奪，故望之若水。火當夜而揚光，在晝則不明也。月之於夜，與日同而差微。星則不然，強弱之差也。眾星列布，其以神著，有五列焉，是為三十五名。一居中央，謂之北斗。動變挺占，寔司王命。四布於方，為二十八宿。日月運行，歷示吉凶，五緯經次，用告禍福，則天心於是見矣。中外之官，常明者百有二十四，可名者三百二十，為星二千五百，而海人之占未存焉。微星之數，蓋萬一千五百二十。庶物蠢蠢，咸得繫命。不然，何以總而理諸！夫三光同形，有似珠玉，神守精存，麗其職而宣其明；及其衰，神歇精斁，於是乎有隕星。然則奔星之所墜，至〔地〕則石〔矣〕。文曜麗乎天，其動者七，日、月、五星是也。周旋右回。天道者，貴順也。近天則遲，遠天則速，行則屈，屈則留回，留回則逆，逆則遲，迫於天也。行遲者覿于東，覿于東屬陽，行速者覿于西，覿于西屬陰，日與月此配合也。攝提、熒惑、地候見晨，附于日也。太白、辰星見昏，附于月也。二陰三陽，參天兩地，故男女取焉。方星巡鎮，必因常度，苟或盈縮，不逾於次。故有列司作使，曰老子四星，周伯、王逢、芮各一，錯乎五緯之閒，其見無期，其行無度，寔妖經星之所，然後吉凶宣周，其祥可盡。」蔡邕表志曰：「言天體者有三家：一曰周髀，二曰宣夜，三曰渾天。宣夜之學絕無師法。周髀數術具存，考驗天狀，多所違失，故史官不用。唯渾天者近得其情，今史官所用候臺銅儀，則其法也。立八尺圓體之度，而具天地之象，以正黃道，以察發斂，以行日月，以步五緯。精微深妙，萬世不易之道也。官有其器而無本書，前志亦闕而不論。臣求其舊文，連年不得。在東觀，以治律未竟，未及成書，案略求索。竊不自量，卒欲寢伏儀下，思惟精意，案度成數，扶以文義，潤以道術，著成篇章。罪惡無狀，投畀有北，灰滅雨絕，世路無由。宜博問群臣，下及巖穴，知渾天之意者，使述其義，以裨天文志。撰建武以來星變彗孛占驗著明者續其後。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Saturn governs Eastern Well.

manualTranslations.zh: 太白主奎、婁、胃、昴、畢、觜、參。
manualTranslations.literal: The Metal Star governs Legs, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Turtle Beak, and Three Stars.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Venus governs Legs, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Turtle Beak, and Three Stars.

manualTranslations.zh: 辰星主斗、牛、女、虛、危、室、壁。
manualTranslations.literal: The Water Star governs Dipper, Ox, Girl, Emptiness, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mercury governs Dipper, Ox, Girl, Emptiness, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall.

manualTranslations.zh: 琁、璣者，謂北極星也。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan and Ji mean the Pole Star.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuan and Ji refer to the circumpolar pivot.

manualTranslations.zh: 玉衡者，謂斗九星也。
manualTranslations.literal: Jade Balance means the nine stars of the Dipper.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jade Balance denotes the nine stars of the Big Dipper.

manualTranslations.zh: 玉衡第一星主徐州，常以五子日候之，甲子為東海，丙子為琅邪，戊子為彭城，庚子為下邳，壬子為廣陵，凡五郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The first star of Jade Balance governs Xu Region; one regularly watches it on the five zi days: jiazi is Donghai, bingzi is Langye, wuzi is Pengcheng, gengzi is Xiapi, and renzi is Guangling—five commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The first Jade Balance star presides over Xu Region and is watched on the five zi days: jiazi marks Donghai, bingzi Langye, wuzi Pengcheng, gengzi Xiapi, and renzi Guangling—five commanderies altogether.

manualTranslations.zh: 第二星主益州，常以五亥日候之，乙亥為漢中，丁亥為永昌，己亥為巴郡、蜀郡、牂牁，辛亥為廣漢，癸亥為犍為，凡七郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The second star governs Yi Region; one regularly watches it on the five hai days: yihai is Hanzhong, dinghai is Yongchang, jihai is Ba, Shu, and Zangke, xinhai is Guanghan, and guihai is Jianwei—seven commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The second star presides over Yi Region and is watched on the five hai days: yihai marks Hanzhong, dinghai Yongchang, jihai Ba, Shu, and Zangke, xinhai Guanghan, and guihai Jianwei—seven commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 第三星主冀州，常以五戌日候之，甲戌為魏郡、勃海，丙戌為安平，戊戌為鉅鹿、河閒，庚戌為清河、趙國，壬戌為恆山，凡八郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The third star governs Ji Region; one regularly watches it on the five xu days: jiaxu is Wei and Bohai, bingxu is Anping, wuxu is Julu and Hejian, gengxu is Qinghe and Zhao, and renxu is Hengshan—eight commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The third star presides over Ji Region and is watched on the five xu days: jiaxu marks Wei and Bohai, bingxu Anping, wuxu Julu and Hejian, gengxu Qinghe and Zhao, and renxu Hengshan—eight commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 第四星主荊州，常以五卯日候之，乙卯為南陽，己卯為零陵，辛卯為桂陽，癸卯為長沙，丁卯為武陵，凡五郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The fourth star governs Jing Region; one regularly watches it on the five mao days: yimao is Nanyang, jimao is Lingling, xinmao is Guiyang, guimao is Changsha, and dingmao is Wuling—five commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The fourth star presides over Jing Region and is watched on the five mao days: yimao marks Nanyang, jimao Lingling, xinmao Guiyang, guimao Changsha, and dingmao Wuling—five commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 第五星主兗州，常以五辰日候之，甲辰為東郡、陳留，丙辰為濟北，戊辰為山陽、泰山，庚辰為濟陰，壬辰為東平、任城，凡八郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The fifth star governs Yan Region; one regularly watches it on the five chen days: jiachen is Dong and Chenliu, bingchen is Jibei, wuchen is Shanyang and Taishan, gengchen is Jiyin, and renchen is Dongping and Rencheng—eight commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The fifth star presides over Yan Region and is watched on the five chen days: jiachen marks Dong and Chenliu, bingchen Jibei, wuchen Shanyang and Taishan, gengchen Jiyin, and renchen Dongping and Rencheng—eight commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 第六星主揚州，常以五巳日候之，乙巳為豫章，辛巳為丹陽，己巳為廬江，丁巳為吳郡、會稽，癸巳為九江，凡六郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The sixth star governs Yang Region; one regularly watches it on the five si days: yisi is Yuzhang, xinsi is Danyang, jisi is Lujiang, dingsi is Wu and Kuaiji, and guisi is Jiujiang—six commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sixth star presides over Yang Region and is watched on the five si days: yisi marks Yuzhang, xinsi Danyang, jisi Lujiang, dingsi Wu and Kuaiji, and guisi Jiujiang—six commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 第七星為豫州，常以五午日候之，甲午為潁川，壬午為梁國，丙午為汝南，戊午為沛國，庚午為魯國，凡五郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The seventh star is Yu Region; one regularly watches it on the five wu days: jiawu is Yingchuan, renwu is Liang, bingwu is Runan, wuwu is Pei, and gengwu is Lu—five commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The seventh star marks Yu Region and is watched on the five wu days: jiawu marks Yingchuan, renwu Liang, bingwu Runan, wuwu Pei, and gengwu Lu—five commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 第八星主幽州，常以五寅日候之，甲寅為玄菟，丙寅為遼東、遼西、漁陽，庚寅為上谷、代郡，壬寅為廣陽，戊寅為涿郡，凡八郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The eighth star governs You Region; one regularly watches it on the five yin days: jiayin is Xuantu, bingyin is Liaodong, Liaoxi, and Yuyang, gengyin is Shanggu and Dai, renyin is Guangyang, and wuyin is Zhuo—eight commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The eighth star presides over You Region and is watched on the five yin days: jiayin marks Xuantu, bingyin Liaodong, Liaoxi, and Yuyang, gengyin Shanggu and Dai, renyin Guangyang, and wuyin Zhuo—eight commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 第九星主并州，常以五申日候之，甲申為五原、鴈門，丙申為朔方、雲中，戊申為西河，庚申為太原、定襄，壬申為上黨，凡八郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The ninth star governs Bing Region; one regularly watches it on the five shen days: jiashen is Wuyuan and Yanmen, bingshen is Shuofang and Yunzhong, wushen is Xihe, gengshen is Taiyuan and Dingxiang, and renshen is Shangdang—eight commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The ninth star presides over Bing Region and is watched on the five shen days: jiashen marks Wuyuan and Yanmen, bingshen Shuofang and Yunzhong, wushen Xihe, gengshen Taiyuan and Dingxiang, and renshen Shangdang—eight commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 琁、璣、玉衡占色，春青黃，夏赤黃，秋白黃，冬黑黃。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan, Ji, and Jade Balance are judged by color: in spring, green-yellow; in summer, red-yellow; in autumn, white-yellow; in winter, black-yellow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The colors of Xuan, Ji, and Jade Balance are read seasonally: green-yellow in spring, red-yellow in summer, white-yellow in autumn, and black-yellow in winter.

manualTranslations.zh: 此是常明；
manualTranslations.literal: This is their normal brightness;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That is their normal brilliance;

manualTranslations.zh: 不如此者，所向國有兵殃起。
manualTranslations.literal: when they are not like this, in the direction toward which they turn, the states will see military disaster arise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they depart from this pattern, the regions they face will suffer war and calamity.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡有六十郡，九州所領，自有分而名焉。
manualTranslations.literal: In all there are sixty commanderies, under the Nine Regions, each with its own allotment and name.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sixty commanderies in all fall under the Nine Regions, each with its own allotment and designation.

manualTranslations.zh: 」三皇邁化，協神醇朴，謂五星如連珠，日月若合璧。
manualTranslations.literal: "The Three Sovereigns advanced in transformation, harmonizing with the spirits in pure simplicity; it is said that the five stars were like linked pearls and the sun and moon like joined jade disks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "In the age of the Three Sovereigns, transformation moved in harmony with the spirits in pristine simplicity; the five stars stood like pearls on a string and sun and moon like paired jade disks.

manualTranslations.zh: 化由自然，民不犯慝。
manualTranslations.literal: Transformation came from nature, and the people did not commit wickedness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Change arose naturally, and the people did not turn to evil.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於書契之興，五帝是作。
manualTranslations.literal: When writing and tallies arose, the Five Thearchs were the ones who made them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When writing and record-keeping arose, the Five Thearchs were their makers.

manualTranslations.zh: 軒轅始受《河圖斗苞授》，規日月星辰之象，故星官之書自黄帝始。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuanyuan first received the River Chart and Dipper Bud Transmission, laid out the images of sun, moon, stars, and asterisms, and therefore the books of star-offices begin with the Yellow Thearch.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuanyuan first received the River Chart and Dipper Bud Transmission, mapped the forms of sun, moon, stars, and asterisms, and so the star-office canon begins with the Yellow Emperor.

manualTranslations.zh: 至高陽氏，使南正重司天，北正黎司地。
manualTranslations.literal: Down to the house of Gaoyang, he made the Southern Rectifier Chong oversee Heaven and the Northern Rectifier Li oversee Earth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the house of Gaoyang, the Southern Rectifier Chong was charged with Heaven and the Northern Rectifier Li with Earth.

manualTranslations.zh: 唐、虞之時，羲仲、和仲，尚書曰：「帝在琁璣玉衡，以齊七政。
manualTranslations.literal: In the time of Tang and Yu, Xi Zhong and He Zhong—the Documents says: "The emperor was at Xuanji and Jade Balance to align the Seven Regulators.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the age of Tang and Yu, Xi Zhong and He Zhong—the Book of Documents says: "The emperor observed from the Xuanji and Jade Balance to harmonize the Seven Regulators.

manualTranslations.zh: 」孔安國曰：「在，察也。
manualTranslations.literal: "Kong Anguo says: "Zai means to observe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Kong Anguo says: "'At' means to observe.

manualTranslations.zh: 琁，美玉也。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan is fine jade.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuan is fine jade.

manualTranslations.zh: 璣衡，王者正天文之器，可運轉者。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji and Balance are the instruments by which the king rectifies astronomy, and they can be turned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji and Balance are the revolving instruments by which the king sets the heavens aright.

manualTranslations.zh: 七政，日月五星各異政。
manualTranslations.literal: The Seven Regulators are the sun, moon, and five stars, each with its distinct governance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Seven Regulators are sun, moon, and the five planets, each with its own office.

manualTranslations.zh: 舜察天文，齊七政也。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun observed the astronomy of Heaven and aligned the Seven Regulators."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun observed Heaven and harmonized the Seven Regulators."

manualTranslations.zh: 」夏有昆吾，湯則巫咸，周之史佚、萇弘，宋之子韦，楚之唐蔑，魯之梓慎，鄭之裨竈，魏石中夫，或云石申父。
manualTranslations.literal: "In Xia there was Kunwu; under Tang, Wuxian; in Zhou, Shi Yi and Chang Hong; in Song, Zi Wei; in Chu, Tang Mie; in Lu, Zishen; in Zheng, Pizao; in Wei, Shi Zhongfu—or some say Shi Shenfu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Xia had Kunwu; Tang had Wuxian; Zhou had Shi Yi and Chang Hong; Song had Zi Wei; Chu had Tang Mie; Lu had Zishen; Zheng had Pizao; Wei had Shi Zhongfu—or, by another account, Shi Shenfu.

manualTranslations.zh: 齐国甘公，皆掌天文之官。
manualTranslations.literal: In Qi there was Gan Gong—all were officials in charge of astronomy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qi had Gan Gong—all were officers charged with astronomy.

manualTranslations.zh: 仰占俯視，以佐時政；
manualTranslations.literal: Looking up they divined, looking down they surveyed, to assist the governance of the age;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They looked up to read the sky and down to survey the earth, aiding the governance of their time;

manualTranslations.zh: 步變擿微，通洞密至；
manualTranslations.literal: tracking changes and plucking out the subtle, penetrating to the densest depths;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: tracking shifts and extracting the subtle, penetrating to the finest detail;

manualTranslations.zh: 採禍福之原，覩成敗之勢。
manualTranslations.literal: gathering the sources of calamity and blessing, and seeing the momentum of success and failure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: tracing the sources of fortune and disaster and discerning the tide of success and ruin.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦燔《詩》、《書》，以愚百姓，六經典籍，殘為灰炭，星官之書，全而不毁。
manualTranslations.literal: Qin burned the Odes and Documents to keep the common people ignorant; the texts of the Six Classics were reduced to ash and charcoal, but the books of the star-offices remained whole and were not destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qin burned the Odes and Documents to benight the people; the Six Classics were reduced to ash, but the star-office books survived intact.

manualTranslations.zh: 故《秦史》書始皇之時，彗孛大角，大角以亡，有大星與小星斗於宫中，是其廢亡之征。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore the Qin Annals record that in the time of the First Thearch a comet broomed the Great Horn, and the Great Horn thereby perished; a great star and a small star battled in the palace—signs of its overthrow and ruin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence the Qin Annals record that under the First Emperor a comet swept the Great Horn and the Great Horn fell; a great star and a small star clashed in the palace—omens of overthrow and ruin.

manualTranslations.zh: 至漢興，景、武之際，司馬談，談子遷，以世黎氏之后，為太史令，遷著《史记》，作《天官書》。
manualTranslations.literal: When Han arose, in the time of Jing and Wu, there were Sima Tan and Tan's son Qian; as descendants by marriage of the Li clan, they served as Grand Astrologer; Qian wrote the Records of the Grand Historian and composed the Treatise on the Celestial Offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Han rose, in the reigns of Jing and Wu, Sima Tan and his son Qian—descendants by marriage of the Li clan—held the post of Grand Astrologer; Qian wrote the Records and composed the Treatise on Celestial Offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 成帝時，中垒校尉劉向，广《洪范》灾条作五纪皇极之论，以参往行之事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the time of Emperor Cheng, Central Rampart Commandant Liu Xiang expanded the calamity entries of the Great Plan and wrote a discourse on the Five Regulators and the Grand Pivot, to compare with events of the past.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng, Central Rampart Commandant Liu Xiang expanded the calamity articles of the Great Plan and wrote on the Five Regulators and Grand Pivot to test them against past events.

manualTranslations.zh: 孝明帝使班固叙《漢書》，而馬續述《天文志》。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming had Ban Gu compile the Book of Han, and Ma Xu composed the Treatise on Astronomy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered Ban Gu to compile the Book of Han, and Ma Xu wrote the Treatise on Astronomy.

manualTranslations.zh: 謝沈書曰：「蔡邕撰建武已後，星驗著明，以續前志，譙周接繼其下者。
manualTranslations.literal: The book of Xie Shen says: "Cai Yong compiled what came after Jianwu, with star-verifications clearly set forth, to continue the earlier treatise; Qiao Zhou carried on below him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xie Shen's book says: "Cai Yong compiled verified star records from Jianwu onward to continue the earlier treatise; Qiao Zhou carried the work on after him.

manualTranslations.zh: 」今紹《漢書》作《天文志》，起王莽居摄元年，迄孝獻帝建安二十五年，二百一十五載。
manualTranslations.literal: "Now, continuing the Book of Han, we compose the Treatise on Astronomy, from the first year of Wang Mang's regency down to the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an of Emperor Xiaoxian—two hundred fifteen years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "This treatise continues the Book of Han's astronomy from Wang Mang's first regency year through Jian'an 25 of Emperor Xian—two hundred fifteen years.

manualTranslations.zh: 言其時星辰之變，表象之應，以顯天戒，明王事焉。
manualTranslations.literal: It tells of the changes of stars and asterisms in that time and the responses of outward signs, to display Heaven's warnings and clarify the affairs of kings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It records the stellar changes and outward responses of that age to reveal Heaven's warnings and clarify royal affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣昭以張衡天文之妙，冠絕一代。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Zhao holds that Zhang Heng's mastery of astronomy surpassed a whole generation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your servant Zhao holds that Zhang Heng's astronomical mastery stood unmatched in his age.

manualTranslations.zh: 所著靈憲、渾儀，略具辰燿之本，今寫載以備其理焉。
manualTranslations.literal: What he wrote, the Spiritual Constitution and the Armillary Sphere, briefly sets forth the roots of the star-lights; they are now copied and recorded here to complete its principles.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His Spiritual Constitution and Armillary Sphere sketch the foundations of the star-lights; they are copied here to preserve his reasoning.

manualTranslations.zh: 靈憲曰：「昔在先王，將步天路，用〔定〕靈軌，尋緒本元。
manualTranslations.literal: The Spiritual Constitution says: "In former times the early kings, about to pace the road of Heaven, used [to fix] the numinous track and traced the thread of the primal origin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Spiritual Constitution says: "In antiquity the early kings, preparing to measure Heaven's path, fixed the numinous track and traced the thread of primordial origin.

manualTranslations.zh: 先準之于渾體，是為正儀立度，而皇極有逌建也，樞運有逌稽也。
manualTranslations.literal: First they matched it to the spherical body; this was to establish the upright instrument and set the degrees, so that the Grand Pivot had its distant founding and the pivot's motion had its distant reckoning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: First they calibrated it against the celestial sphere, establishing the upright instrument and setting degrees so the Grand Pivot could be founded afar and the pivot's motion reckoned afar.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃建乃稽，斯經天常。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus founding and thus reckoning—this is the constant of Heaven's warp.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By founding and reckoning alike, they fixed Heaven's constant pattern.

manualTranslations.zh: 聖人無心，因茲以生心，故靈憲作興。
manualTranslations.literal: The sage has no mind of his own; because of this he gives birth to mind—therefore the Spiritual Constitution arose.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sage has no private intent; from this he gives rise to intent—hence the Spiritual Constitution was composed.

manualTranslations.zh: 曰：太素之前，幽清玄靜，寂漠冥默，不可為象，厥中惟虛，厥外惟無。
manualTranslations.literal: It says: Before Grand Simplicity, dark, pure, abstruse, and still—silent, dim, and mute, nothing could be imaged; within was only void, without was only nothing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It says: Before Grand Simplicity, all was dark, pure, abstruse, and still—silent and imageless; within was void alone, without was nothing alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 如是者永久焉，斯謂溟涬，蓋乃道之根也。
manualTranslations.literal: Being so for long ages, this is called primeval chaos—this is the root of the Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Remaining so for ages without end, this is called primeval chaos—the root of the Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 道根既建，自無生有。
manualTranslations.literal: Once the root of the Way was established, from nothing being arose.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once the Way's root was set, being arose from nonbeing.

manualTranslations.zh: 太素始萌，萌而未兆，并氣同色，渾沌不分。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Simplicity first sprouted; it sprouted but had not yet shown signs; qi merged and colors were one; chaos was undivided.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand Simplicity first stirred; it stirred but showed no sign; breaths merged and colors were one; chaos remained undivided.

manualTranslations.zh: 故道志之言云：『有物渾成，先天地生。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore the words of the Way's records say: 'There was a thing formed in chaos, born before Heaven and Earth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence the Way's records say: 'There was a thing formed in chaos, born before Heaven and Earth.

manualTranslations.zh: 』其氣體固未可得而形，其遲速固未可得而紀也。
manualTranslations.literal: 'Its qi-body indeed could not yet be given form; its slowness and speed indeed could not yet be recorded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 'Its breath-body could not yet be shaped; its motion could not yet be measured.

manualTranslations.zh: 如是者又永久焉，斯為庬鴻，蓋乃道之幹也。
manualTranslations.literal: Being so again for long ages, this is called vast obscurity—this is the trunk of the Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Remaining so again for ages without end, this is called vast obscurity—the trunk of the Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 道幹既育，有物成體。
manualTranslations.literal: Once the trunk of the Way had nourished, things formed bodies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once the Way's trunk had ripened, things took bodily form.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是元氣剖判，剛柔始分，清濁異位。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon primal qi was split and distinguished; hard and soft first divided; clear and turbid took different positions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then primal breath was divided; hard and soft parted; clear and turbid took separate stations.

manualTranslations.zh: 天成於外，地定於內。
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven formed on the outside; Earth was fixed within.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven took shape without; Earth was fixed within.

manualTranslations.zh: 天體於陽，故圓以動；
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven's body belongs to yang, therefore it is round and moves;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven belongs to yang, hence it is round and in motion;

manualTranslations.zh: 地體於陰，故平以靜。
manualTranslations.literal: Earth's body belongs to yin, therefore it is flat and still.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earth belongs to yin, hence it is flat and still.

manualTranslations.zh: 動以行施，靜以合化，堙鬱構精，時育庶類，斯謂太元，蓋乃道之實也。
manualTranslations.literal: Motion acts to distribute; stillness joins in transformation; buried and pent-up, it constructs essence and in season nourishes the myriad kinds—this is called Grand Origin, and is the substance of the Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Motion distributes; stillness joins transformation; pent-up essence builds and in season nourishes the myriad kinds—this is Grand Origin, the Way's substance.

manualTranslations.zh: 在天成象，在地成形。
manualTranslations.literal: In Heaven images are formed; on Earth forms are shaped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Heaven images take shape; on Earth forms are molded.

manualTranslations.zh: 天有九位，地有九域；
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven has nine positions; Earth has nine domains;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven has nine stations; Earth has nine regions;

manualTranslations.zh: 天有三辰，地有三形；
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven has the three luminaries; Earth has the three forms;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven has the three lights; Earth has the three shapes;

manualTranslations.zh: 有象可效，有形可度。
manualTranslations.literal: there are images that can be modeled and forms that can be measured.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: images can be modeled and forms can be measured.

manualTranslations.zh: 情性萬殊，旁通感薄，自然相生，莫之能紀。
manualTranslations.literal: Natures and temperaments are myriad and diverse; they reach one another and are stirred and pressed; naturally they generate one another, and none can record them all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Natures and temperaments differ endlessly; they reach and stir one another and naturally generate one another beyond all reckoning.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是人之精者作聖。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon the refined among men became sages.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then the most refined among men became sages.

manualTranslations.zh: 實始紀綱而經緯之。
manualTranslations.literal: Truly they first laid out the warp and woof and threaded them through.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They first set the warp and woof and threaded the pattern through.

manualTranslations.zh: 八極之維，徑二億三萬二千三百里，南北則短減千里，東西則廣增千里。
manualTranslations.literal: The girth of the Eight Poles is two hundred thirty-two thousand three hundred li in diameter; north and south it is shorter by one thousand li, east and west wider by one thousand li.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The girth of the Eight Poles measures two hundred thirty-two thousand three hundred li in diameter, one thousand li shorter north and south and one thousand li wider east and west.

manualTranslations.zh: 自地至天，半於八極，則地之深亦如之。
manualTranslations.literal: From Earth to Heaven is half the Eight Poles; the depth of Earth is likewise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Earth to Heaven is half the Eight Poles; Earth's depth is the same.

manualTranslations.zh: 通而度之，則是渾已。
manualTranslations.literal: Measured through and through, this is already a sphere.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Measured through and through, the cosmos is already a sphere.

manualTranslations.zh: 將覆其數，用重鉤股，懸天之景，薄地之義，皆移千里而差一寸得之。
manualTranslations.literal: To verify its numbers, using doubled hook-and-leg measures, the shadow cast by Heaven suspended and the principle of nearness to Earth—each shift of one thousand li yields a difference of one inch.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To verify its measure, using doubled gnomon-and-base triangles, the suspended shadow of Heaven and nearness to Earth all show that each thousand li shifts the reading by one inch.

manualTranslations.zh: 過此而往者，未之或知也。
manualTranslations.literal: Beyond this point, none has ever known.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Beyond this, none has ever known.

manualTranslations.zh: 未之或知者，宇宙之謂也。
manualTranslations.literal: What none has ever known is what is called cosmos.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What none can know is called the cosmos.

manualTranslations.zh: 宇之表無極，宙之端無窮。
manualTranslations.literal: Outside space there is no limit; at time's end there is no exhaustion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Space has no outer bound; time has no final end.

manualTranslations.zh: 天有兩儀，以儛道中。
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven has two pivots, dancing in the middle of the Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven has two pivots, wheeling along the central path.

manualTranslations.zh: 其可睹，樞星是也，謂之北極。
manualTranslations.literal: What can be seen is the Pivot Star—this is called the North Pole.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What can be seen is the Pivot Star, called the North Pole.

manualTranslations.zh: 在南者不著，故聖人弗之名焉。
manualTranslations.literal: What lies to the south is not visible, so the sage does not name it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The southern pivot is not visible, so the sage gives it no name.

manualTranslations.zh: 其世之遂，九分而減二。
manualTranslations.literal: Its generational depth is nine parts with two subtracted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Its depth through the ages is reckoned as nine parts minus two.

manualTranslations.zh: 陽道左迴，故天運左行。
manualTranslations.literal: The yang path turns left, therefore Heaven's motion goes leftward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The yang path wheels leftward, so Heaven's motion runs to the left.

manualTranslations.zh: 有驗於物，則人氣左羸，形左繚也。
manualTranslations.literal: Verified in things, human breath is weaker on the left and the form coils leftward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This shows in things: human breath is weaker on the left and the body coils leftward.

manualTranslations.zh: 天以陽迴，地以陰淳。
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven turns by yang; Earth is dense by yin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven wheels by yang; Earth compacts by yin.

manualTranslations.zh: 是故天致其動，稟氣舒光；
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore Heaven brings forth its motion, receiving qi and spreading light;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence Heaven achieves motion, receiving breath and spreading light;

manualTranslations.zh: 地致其靜，承施候明。
manualTranslations.literal: Earth brings forth its stillness, receiving and applying, awaiting brightness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earth achieves stillness, receiving and applying, awaiting illumination.

manualTranslations.zh: 天以順動，不失其中，則四序順至，寒暑不減，致生有節，故品物用生。
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven, moving in accord, does not miss its center; then the four seasons arrive in order, cold and heat are not diminished, generation has its seasons, and therefore the myriad kinds are enabled to live.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven moves in accord without losing its center; the four seasons come in order, cold and heat hold steady, generation keeps its seasons, and the myriad kinds are enabled to live.

manualTranslations.zh: 地以靈靜，作合承天，清化致養，四時而後育，故品物用成。
manualTranslations.literal: Earth, numinous and still, joins in union to receive Heaven, clear transformation brings nourishment, and after the four seasons it nurtures; therefore the myriad kinds are enabled to mature.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earth, numinous and still, joins Heaven, clear transformation nourishes, and after the four seasons it brings things to maturity; hence the myriad kinds are enabled to ripen.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡至大莫如天，至厚莫若地。
manualTranslations.literal: Of all that is greatest, none is like Heaven; of all that is thickest, none is like Earth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Nothing is greater than Heaven; nothing is thicker than Earth.

manualTranslations.zh: 地）
manualTranslations.literal: Earth)
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earth)

manualTranslations.zh: 至質者曰地而已。
manualTranslations.literal: What is most substantial is called Earth, and that is all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What is most substantial is simply called Earth.

manualTranslations.zh: 至多莫若水，水精為漢，漢用於天而無列焉，思次質也。
manualTranslations.literal: Of all that is most abundant, none is like water; the essence of water becomes the Han River; the Han is used in Heaven but has no fixed array—consider the next in substance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Nothing is more abundant than water; water's essence becomes the Celestial River; the River serves in Heaven but has no fixed array—think next of substance.

manualTranslations.zh: 地有山獄，以宣其氣，精種為星。
manualTranslations.literal: Earth has mountains and marshes to release its qi; the seed of essence becomes stars.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earth has mountains and marshes to release its breath; the seed of essence becomes stars.

manualTranslations.zh: 星也者，體生於地，精成於天，列居錯跱，各有逌屬。
manualTranslations.literal: Stars are bodies born from Earth and essences perfected in Heaven; arrayed and set in staggered positions, each has its distant affiliation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Stars are bodies born from Earth and essences perfected in Heaven; arrayed in staggered stations, each has its distant affiliation.

manualTranslations.zh: 紫宮為皇極之居，太微為五帝之廷。
manualTranslations.literal: The Purple Palace Enclosure is the dwelling of the Grand Pivot; the Supreme Palace Enclosure is the court of the Five Thearchs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Purple Palace Enclosure is the Grand Pivot's dwelling; the Supreme Palace Enclosure is the court of the Five Thearchs.

manualTranslations.zh: 明堂之房，大角有席，天巿有坐。
manualTranslations.literal: In the chambers of the Bright Hall, the Great Horn has its seat; in the Celestial Market there is a throne.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Bright Hall chambers the Great Horn has its seat; in the Celestial Market there is a throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 蒼龍連蜷於左，白虎猛據於右，朱雀奮翼於前，靈龜圈首於後，黃神軒轅於中。
manualTranslations.literal: The Azure Dragon coils on the left; the White Tiger fiercely holds the right; the Vermilion Bird spreads its wings in front; the Spirit Tortoise circles its head behind; the Yellow Spirit Xuanyuan is in the center.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Azure Dragon coils on the left, the White Tiger holds the right, the Vermilion Bird spreads its wings before, the Spirit Tortoise circles behind, and the Yellow Spirit Xuanyuan stands at the center.

manualTranslations.zh: 六擾既畜，而狼蚖魚鱉罔有不具。
manualTranslations.literal: Once the six domestic beasts were gathered, wolf, snake, fish, and turtle—none was not complete.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once the six domestic beasts were gathered, wolf, snake, fish, and turtle were all present.

manualTranslations.zh: 在野象物，在朝象官，在人象事，於是備矣。
manualTranslations.literal: In the wilds they image things; at court they image offices; in men they image affairs—then all was complete.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fields they mirror things; at court they mirror offices; in men they mirror affairs—then the pattern was complete.

manualTranslations.zh: 懸象著明，莫大乎日月。
manualTranslations.literal: Of the suspended images that shine bright, none is greater than sun and moon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Of the bright suspended images, none surpass sun and moon.

manualTranslations.zh: 其徑當天周七百三十六分之一，地廣二百四十二分之一。
manualTranslations.literal: Their diameter equals one seven-hundred-thirty-sixth of Heaven's circumference and one two-hundred-forty-second of Earth's breadth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Their diameter is one seven-hundred-thirty-sixth of Heaven's circuit and one two-hundred-forty-second of Earth's breadth.

manualTranslations.zh: 日者，陽精之宗。
manualTranslations.literal: The sun is the ancestor of yang essence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sun is the sovereign of yang essence.

manualTranslations.zh: 積而成鳥，象烏而有三趾。
manualTranslations.literal: Massed together it becomes a bird, imaged as a crow with three toes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Massed together it becomes a bird, imaged as a three-toed crow.

manualTranslations.zh: 陽之類，其數奇。
manualTranslations.literal: Things of the yang kind have odd numbers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Things of yang kind count by odd numbers.

manualTranslations.zh: 月者，陰精之宗。
manualTranslations.literal: The moon is the ancestor of yin essence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The moon is the sovereign of yin essence.

manualTranslations.zh: 積而成獸，象兔。
manualTranslations.literal: Massed together it becomes a beast, imaged as a hare.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Massed together it becomes a beast, imaged as a rabbit.

manualTranslations.zh: 陰之類，其數耦。
manualTranslations.literal: Things of the yin kind have even numbers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Things of yin kind count by even numbers.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後有馮焉者。
manualTranslations.literal: Later there was one named Feng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later there was a man named Feng.

manualTranslations.zh: 羿請無死之藥於西王母，姮娥竊之以奔月。
manualTranslations.literal: Yi requested the deathless drug from the Queen Mother of the West; Chang'e stole it and fled to the moon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi asked the Queen Mother of the West for the elixir of immortality; Chang'e stole it and fled to the moon.

manualTranslations.zh: 將往，枚筮之於有黃，有黃占之曰：『吉。
manualTranslations.literal: About to go, she had Mei divined by You Huang; You Huang divined and said: 'Auspicious.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before she went, she had Mei divined with You Huang, who read the omen: 'Auspicious.

manualTranslations.zh: 翩翩歸妹，獨將西行，逢天晦芒，毋驚毋恐，後其大昌。
manualTranslations.literal: Gracefully returning maiden, alone about to travel west; meeting Heaven dim and vast—do not startle, do not fear; afterward great prosperity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gracefully returning maiden, traveling west alone; you will meet Heaven dim and vast—do not startle, do not fear; afterward comes great prosperity.

manualTranslations.zh: 』姮娥遂託身于月，是為蟾蠩。
manualTranslations.literal: 'Chang'e then entrusted her body to the moon and became the toad.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 'Chang'e then entrusted herself to the moon and became the moon toad.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫日譬猶火，月譬猶水，火則外光，水則含景。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the sun is like fire and the moon like water; fire shines outward, water holds reflected light.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sun is like fire and the moon like water: fire shines outward, water holds reflected light.

manualTranslations.zh: 故月光生於日之所照，魄生於日之所蔽，當日則光盈，就日則光盡也。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore moonlight is born where the sun shines; the dark part is born where the sun is blocked; when opposite the sun, light is full; when near the sun, light is exhausted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence moonlight arises where the sun shines; the dark portion arises where the sun is blocked; at full opposition light is full, and near the sun light is spent.

manualTranslations.zh: 眾星被燿，因水轉光。
manualTranslations.literal: The host of stars are covered with radiance and, through water, turn the light.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The host of stars are bathed in radiance and, through water, turn the light.

manualTranslations.zh: 當日之衝，光常不合者，蔽於〔地〕也。
manualTranslations.literal: At the sun's opposition, the light often does not meet because it is blocked by [Earth].
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At full moon the light often fails to meet because it is blocked by Earth.

manualTranslations.zh: 是謂闇虛。
manualTranslations.literal: This is called the dark void.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is called the dark void.

manualTranslations.zh: 在星星微，月過則食。
manualTranslations.literal: Among the stars the star is faint; when the moon passes, there is an eclipse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among the stars the star is faint; when the moon passes it, there is an eclipse.

manualTranslations.zh: 日之薄地，其明也。
manualTranslations.literal: When the sun nears Earth, that is its brightness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the sun nears Earth, that is when it appears bright.

manualTranslations.zh: 繇暗視明，明無所屈，是以望之若火。
manualTranslations.literal: Looking from darkness toward brightness, brightness has nothing to bend it; therefore gazing at it, it seems like fire.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Looking from darkness toward brightness, brightness is unbent; hence it looks like fire.

manualTranslations.zh: 方於中天，天地同明。
manualTranslations.literal: When squarely at mid-heaven, Heaven and Earth share the same brightness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At mid-heaven, Heaven and Earth share the same brightness.

manualTranslations.zh: 繇明瞻暗，暗還自奪，故望之若水。
manualTranslations.literal: Looking from brightness toward darkness, darkness in turn steals from itself; therefore gazing at it, it seems like water.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Looking from brightness toward darkness, darkness steals from itself; hence it looks like water.

manualTranslations.zh: 火當夜而揚光，在晝則不明也。
manualTranslations.literal: Fire raises its light at night; in daytime it is not bright.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fire raises its light at night; by day it is not bright.

manualTranslations.zh: 月之於夜，與日同而差微。
manualTranslations.literal: The moon at night is like the sun but with a slight difference.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The moon at night resembles the sun but with a slight difference.

manualTranslations.zh: 星則不然，強弱之差也。
manualTranslations.literal: Stars are not so; the difference is one of strong and weak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Stars are not so; the difference lies in strength and weakness.

manualTranslations.zh: 眾星列布，其以神著，有五列焉，是為三十五名。
manualTranslations.literal: The host of stars are arrayed and spread; those distinguished by spirit have five ranks—this makes thirty-five names.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The host of stars are arrayed; those distinguished by numinous power form five ranks—thirty-five names in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 一居中央，謂之北斗。
manualTranslations.literal: One occupies the center—this is called the Northern Dipper.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One occupies the center—the Northern Dipper.

manualTranslations.zh: 動變挺占，寔司王命。
manualTranslations.literal: In motion, change, and upright divination, it truly presides over the king's mandate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In motion, change, and upright divination, it truly governs the royal mandate.

manualTranslations.zh: 四布於方，為二十八宿。
manualTranslations.literal: Four spread to the quarters, making the twenty-eight lodges.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Four spread to the quarters, forming the twenty-eight lodges.

manualTranslations.zh: 日月運行，歷示吉凶，五緯經次，用告禍福，則天心於是見矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun and moon move in their courses, passing through to show good and ill; the five cords traverse in sequence, used to announce calamity and blessing—then the heart of Heaven is seen here.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun and moon run their courses to show fortune and misfortune; the five cords traverse in sequence to announce calamity and blessing—then Heaven's intent appears.

manualTranslations.zh: 中外之官，常明者百有二十四，可名者三百二十，為星二千五百，而海人之占未存焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Among the inner and outer offices, those constantly bright are one hundred twenty-four; those that can be named are three hundred twenty; stars number two thousand five hundred—and the divinations of the sea peoples are not preserved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among the inner and outer offices, one hundred twenty-four are constantly bright, three hundred twenty can be named, and stars number two thousand five hundred—while the sea peoples' divinations are not preserved.

manualTranslations.zh: 微星之數，蓋萬一千五百二十。
manualTranslations.literal: The number of faint stars is roughly eleven thousand five hundred twenty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Faint stars number roughly eleven thousand five hundred twenty.

manualTranslations.zh: 庶物蠢蠢，咸得繫命。
manualTranslations.literal: The myriad things, teeming and restless, all have their lives tied to it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The myriad teeming things all have their lives bound to it.

manualTranslations.zh: 不然，何以總而理諸！
manualTranslations.literal: If not so, how could one gather and order them all!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how could one gather and order them all!

manualTranslations.zh: 夫三光同形，有似珠玉，神守精存，麗其職而宣其明；
manualTranslations.literal: Now the Three Luminaries share one form, like pearls and jade; spirit guards and essence is preserved, beautifying their offices and displaying their brightness;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Three Luminaries share one form, like pearls and jade; spirit guards and essence endures, adorning their offices and displaying their light;

manualTranslations.zh: 及其衰，神歇精斁，於是乎有隕星。
manualTranslations.literal: when they decline, spirit rests and essence is spent—then there are falling stars.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they decline, spirit rests and essence fails—then falling stars appear.

manualTranslations.zh: 然則奔星之所墜，至〔地〕則石〔矣〕。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus where running stars fall, when they reach [Earth] they become stone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus where shooting stars fall, upon reaching Earth they become stone.

manualTranslations.zh: 文曜麗乎天，其動者七，日、月、五星是也。
manualTranslations.literal: Patterned lights adorn Heaven; those that move are seven—sun, moon, and the five stars.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Patterned lights adorn Heaven; seven move—sun, moon, and the five planets.

manualTranslations.zh: 周旋右回。
manualTranslations.literal: They wheel and turn rightward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They wheel and turn rightward.

manualTranslations.zh: 天道者，貴順也。
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven's Way values accord.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way values accord.

manualTranslations.zh: 近天則遲，遠天則速，行則屈，屈則留回，留回則逆，逆則遲，迫於天也。
manualTranslations.literal: Near Heaven it is slow; far from Heaven it is fast; in motion it bends; when bent it stays and turns; when staying and turning it reverses; when reversed it is slow—pressed by Heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Near Heaven it slows; far from Heaven it quickens; in motion it bends; bent, it halts and turns; halted and turning, it reverses; reversed, it slows—constrained by Heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 行遲者覿于東，覿于東屬陽，行速者覿于西，覿于西屬陰，日與月此配合也。
manualTranslations.literal: Those moving slowly appear in the east; appearing in the east belongs to yang; those moving swiftly appear in the west; appearing in the west belongs to yin—sun and moon pair in this way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Slow movers appear in the east, and eastern appearance belongs to yang; swift movers appear in the west, and western appearance belongs to yin—sun and moon pair accordingly.

manualTranslations.zh: 攝提、熒惑、地候見晨，附于日也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sheti, Flaming Radiance, and Earth-Emissary appear at dawn, attached to the sun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sheti, Mars, and Earth-Emissary appear at dawn, attached to the sun.

manualTranslations.zh: 太白、辰星見昏，附于月也。
manualTranslations.literal: Metal Star and Water Star appear at dusk, attached to the moon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Venus and Mercury appear at dusk, attached to the moon.

manualTranslations.zh: 二陰三陽，參天兩地，故男女取焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Two yin and three yang, thrice Heaven and twice Earth—therefore male and female are taken from this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Two yin and three yang, thrice Heaven and twice Earth—hence male and female are modeled on this.

manualTranslations.zh: 方星巡鎮，必因常度，苟或盈縮，不逾於次。
manualTranslations.literal: When the square stars patrol and anchor, they must follow regular degrees; if they swell or shrink, they do not pass beyond their sequence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the square stars patrol and anchor, they follow regular degrees; even if they swell or shrink, they do not pass their station.

manualTranslations.zh: 故有列司作使，曰老子四星，周伯、王逢、芮各一，錯乎五緯之閒，其見無期，其行無度，寔妖經星之所，然後吉凶宣周，其祥可盡。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore there are arrayed officers acting as envoys—called the four stars of Laozi, Zhou Bo, Wang Feng, and Rui, one each—straying among the five cords; their appearance has no fixed season, their motion no fixed measure; they are truly the place of portentous classic stars, and only then are good and ill proclaimed roundly and omens fully displayed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence there are arrayed officers serving as envoys—the four stars of Laozi, Zhou Bo, Wang Feng, and Rui, one each—straying among the five cords; their appearances are untimed and their motions unmeasured; they are truly the domain of portentous classic stars, by which fortune and misfortune are fully proclaimed and omens fully displayed.

manualTranslations.zh: 」蔡邕表志曰：「言天體者有三家：一曰周髀，二曰宣夜，三曰渾天。
manualTranslations.literal: "Cai Yong's memorial treatise says: "Those who speak of the celestial body are of three schools: first, Gnomon and Leg; second, Declare the Night; third, Spherical Heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Cai Yong's memorial treatise says: "Writers on the celestial body fall into three schools: the Gnomon and Leg, Declare the Night, and Spherical Heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣夜之學絕無師法。
manualTranslations.literal: The learning of Declare the Night is utterly without transmitted masters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Declare the Night school has no surviving transmission.

manualTranslations.zh: 周髀數術具存，考驗天狀，多所違失，故史官不用。
manualTranslations.literal: The numbers and methods of Gnomon and Leg are fully preserved, but when tested against the state of Heaven, many fail; therefore the historiographers do not use them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Gnomon and Leg numbers and methods survive intact, but tested against Heaven's state they fail in many ways, so historiographers do not use them.

manualTranslations.zh: 唯渾天者近得其情，今史官所用候臺銅儀，則其法也。
manualTranslations.literal: Only Spherical Heaven nearly gets the reality; the bronze instrument of the observation platform now used by historiographers is its method.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only Spherical Heaven nearly captures the truth; the bronze armillary on the observation platform now used by historiographers follows its method.

manualTranslations.zh: 立八尺圓體之度，而具天地之象，以正黃道，以察發斂，以行日月，以步五緯。
manualTranslations.literal: It sets up an eight-foot measure of the round body and fully presents the images of Heaven and Earth, to rectify the Yellow Path, to observe waxing and waning, to track sun and moon, and to pace the five cords.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It erects an eight-foot measure of the celestial sphere and presents the images of Heaven and Earth, to fix the Yellow Path, observe waxing and waning, track sun and moon, and pace the five cords.

manualTranslations.zh: 精微深妙，萬世不易之道也。
manualTranslations.literal: Subtle, refined, deep, and wondrous—it is a Way unchanged for ten thousand generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Subtle, refined, deep, and wondrous—a Way unchanged for ten thousand generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 官有其器而無本書，前志亦闕而不論。
manualTranslations.literal: The office has its instrument but not the original book; the earlier treatise also omits it and does not discuss it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The office has the instrument but not the original book; the earlier treatise also omits and does not discuss it.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣求其舊文，連年不得。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant sought its old text for years without obtaining it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your servant sought the old text for years without success.

manualTranslations.zh: 在東觀，以治律未竟，未及成書，案略求索。
manualTranslations.literal: At the Eastern Pavilion, because work on the pitch-pipes was not finished, he had not yet completed the book and only searched out a brief outline.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Pavilion, because work on the pitch-pipes was unfinished, he had not yet completed the book and only pursued a brief outline.

manualTranslations.zh: 竊不自量，卒欲寢伏儀下，思惟精意，案度成數，扶以文義，潤以道術，著成篇章。
manualTranslations.literal: Presuming beyond his measure, he finally wished to lie hidden beneath the instrument, think through its refined intent, work out the numbers by degrees, support them with literary meaning, polish them with the methods of the Way, and compose them into chapters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Presuming beyond his measure, he finally wished to work beneath the instrument, ponder its refined intent, derive the numbers by degrees, support them with literary meaning, polish them with Way-craft, and compose chapters.

manualTranslations.zh: 罪惡無狀，投畀有北，灰滅雨絕，世路無由。
manualTranslations.literal: His guilt was beyond description; cast out to the northern wilds, ashes extinguished and rain cut off—there was no path left in the world.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His guilt was beyond description; cast out to the northern wilds, ashes extinguished and rain cut off—no path remained in the world.

manualTranslations.zh: 宜博問群臣，下及巖穴，知渾天之意者，使述其義，以裨天文志。
manualTranslations.literal: It is fitting to question broadly among the ministers and down to the cliff caves; whoever knows the intent of Spherical Heaven should be made to set forth its meaning to supplement the Treatise on Astronomy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court should question ministers broadly and even recluses in cliff caves; whoever understands Spherical Heaven should set forth its meaning to supplement the Treatise on Astronomy.

manualTranslations.zh: 撰建武以來星變彗孛占驗著明者續其後。
manualTranslations.literal: Compile verified records of star changes and comets from Jianwu onward that are clearly set forth, and continue them afterward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Compile clearly verified records of stellar changes and comets from Jianwu onward to continue the treatise.

sourceRange.text: 古今注曰：「其年七月丁丑，月犯昴頭兩星。八月辛酉，水見東方翼分。九月甲午，火犯輿鬼。十月丁卯，大星流，有光，發東井西行，聲隆隆。十三年二月乙卯，火犯輿鬼西北。」黃帝占曰：「熒惑守輿鬼，大人憂。」一曰貴人當之。巫咸曰：「水見翼，多火災。」石氏曰：「為旱。」郗萌占曰：「流星出東井，所之國大水。」十五年正月丁未，彗星見昴，炎長三丈。韓揚占曰：「在昴，大國起兵也。」稍西北行，入营室，犯离宫，韓揚占曰：「彗出營室、東壁之閒，為兵起也。」三月乙未，至東壁滅，見四十九日。

sourceRange.text: 古今注曰：「四月乙亥，月入南斗魁中。八月己亥，熒惑出入太微端門。」三年正月庚戌，月犯心后星。河圖曰：「亂臣在旁。」己亥，太白入斗中。古今注曰：「三月壬寅，熒惑入輿鬼中。五月丙寅，太白入畢中。」石氏經曰；「太白守畢，國多任刑也。」十二月，彗星起天菀南，東北指，長六七尺，色苍白。太白昼見，爲强臣。前志曰：「太白晝見，強國弱，小國強，女主昌。」是時，鄧氏方盛，月犯心后星，不利子。心爲宋。五月丁酉，沛王正薨。太白入斗中，爲貴相凶。臣昭案：楊厚對曰「以為諸王子多在京師，容有非常，宜亟發遣還本國」，太后從之，星尋滅不見。以斯而言，太白入之，災在貴相。天菀爲外軍，彗星出其南爲外兵。是后使羌、氐討賊李貴，又使烏桓擊鮮卑，又使中郎將任尚、護羌校尉馬贤擊羌，皆降。四年古今注曰：「二月丙寅，月犯軒轅大星。」六月甲子，客星大如李，苍白，芒氣長二尺，西南指上階星。

manualTranslations.zh: 三年正月庚戌，月犯心后星。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year, in the first month, on the day gengxu, the moon offended the posterior star of Heart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengxu in the first month of the third Yongchu year the moon crossed the posterior star of Heart.

manualTranslations.zh: 己亥，太白入斗中。
manualTranslations.literal: On jihai, Great White entered the Dipper.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jihai Venus entered the Dipper.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月，彗星起天菀南，東北指，長六七尺，色苍白。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month, a comet rose south of the Celestial Park, pointing northeast, six or seven feet long, pale white in color.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month a pale comet six or seven feet long rose south of the Celestial Park with its train aimed northeast.

manualTranslations.zh: 太白昼見，爲强臣。
manualTranslations.literal: Great White seen by day means overbearing ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Daylight Venus marked ministers grown too strong for the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，鄧氏方盛，月犯心后星，不利子。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time the Deng clan was at its height; the moon offending the posterior star of Heart was ill for sons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Deng were then at the height of power; the moon’s trespass on Heart’s posterior star boded ill for imperial sons.

manualTranslations.zh: 心爲宋。
manualTranslations.literal: Heart is Song.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heart corresponds to the domain of Song.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月丁酉，沛王正薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day dingyou, Prince Zheng of Pei passed away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingyou in the fifth month Prince Zheng of Pei died.

manualTranslations.zh: 太白入斗中，爲貴相凶。
manualTranslations.literal: Great White entering the Dipper means misfortune for exalted ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Venus in the Dipper foretold calamity for high ministers.

manualTranslations.zh: 天菀爲外軍，彗星出其南爲外兵。
manualTranslations.literal: The Celestial Park is armies from without; a comet issuing south from it means foreign troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Celestial Park governs armies abroad; a comet rising south from it augured foreign war.

manualTranslations.zh: 是后使羌、氐討賊李貴，又使烏桓擊鮮卑，又使中郎將任尚、護羌校尉馬贤擊羌，皆降。
manualTranslations.literal: Afterward the court sent Qiang and Di to punish the bandit Li Gui, also sent Wuhuan to strike Xianbei, and also sent General of the Gentlemen of the Household Ren Shang and Protector of the Qiang Ma Xian to strike the Qiang; all submitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court then sent Qiang and Di forces against the rebel Li Gui, dispatched Wuhuan against the Xianbei, and sent Household General Ren Shang and Protector of the Qiang Ma Xian against the Qiang; all enemies submitted.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年六月甲子，客星大如李，苍白，芒氣長二尺，西南指上階星。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year, in the sixth month, on the day jiazi: a guest star as large as a plum, pale white, with a rayed aura two feet long, pointed southwest toward the Upper Steps star.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiazi in the sixth month of Yongchu 4, a plum-sized guest star shone pale white with a two-foot coma aimed southwest at the Upper Steps.

sourceRange.text: 五年古今注曰：「正月甲戌，月乘歲星。」四月癸巳，太白、熒惑、辰星俱在東井。巫咸曰：「太白守井，五穀不成。」黃帝經曰：「五星及客星守井，皆為水。」石氏曰：「為旱。」又曰：「太白入東井，留一日以上乃占，大臣當之，期三月，若一年，遠五年。」古今注曰：「木在輿鬼。」七月壬午，歲星犯軒轅大星。九月，金在南斗魁中。為水。石氏曰：「為旱。」火犯房北第一星。東井，秦地，爲法。三星合，内外有兵，又爲法令及水。金入斗口中，爲大將將死。火犯房北第一星，爲將相。其六年正月，司徒丁鸿薨。古今注曰：「六年六月丁亥，金在東井。閏月己丑，流星大如桃，起參北，西至參肩南，稍有光。」七月水，大漂殺人民，傷五谷。許侯馬光有罪自殺。九月，行車騎將軍事鄧鸿、越騎校尉馮柱發左右羽林、北軍五校士及八郡迹射、烏桓、鮮卑，合四万騎，與度遼將軍朱徵、護烏桓校尉任尚、中郎將杜崇征叛胡。十二月，車騎將軍鸿坐追虏失利，下獄死；度遼將軍徵、中郎將崇皆抵罪。七年正月丁未，有流星起天津，入紫宫中滅。色青黄，有光。二月癸酉，金、火俱在参。巫咸占曰：「熒惑守參，多火災。」海中占曰：「為旱。太白守參，國有反臣。」郗萌曰「有攻戰伐國」也。戊寅，金、火俱在東井。郗萌曰：「熒惑守井，百川皆滿。太白又從舍，蓋二十日流國。」又曰：「雜糴貴。又將相死。」八月甲寅，水、土、金俱在軫。春秋緯曰：「五星有入軫者，皆為兵大起。」巫咸占曰：「五星入軫者，司其出日而數之，期二十日皆為兵發。司始入處之率一日期，十日軍罷。」石氏星經曰：「辰星守軫，歲水。」郗萌曰：「鎮星出入留舍軫六十日不下，必有大喪。」春秋緯曰：「太白入軫，兵大起。」郗萌曰：「太白守軫，必有死王。」十一月甲戌，金、火俱在心。雒書曰：「太白守心，後九年大飢。」十二月己卯，有流星起文昌，入紫宫消。丙辰，火、金、水俱在斗。流星入紫宫，金、火在心，皆爲大喪。三星合軫，爲白衣之會，金、火俱在参、東井，皆爲外兵，有死將。三星俱在斗，有戮將，若有死相。八年四月乐成王黨，七月乐成王宗皆薨。將兵長史吳棽坐事征下獄誅。古今注曰：「八年九月辛丑，夜有流星，大如拳，起婁。」十月，北海王威自殺。十二月，陳王羡薨。其九年閏月，皇太后竇氏崩。遼東鮮卑反，太守祭参不追虏，征下獄誅。九月，司徒劉方坐事免官，自殺。陇西羌反，遣执金吾劉尚行征西將軍事，越騎校尉节鄉侯趙世發北軍五校、黎陽、雍营及邊胡兵三万騎，征西羌。

manualTranslations.zh: 五年四月癸巳，太白、熒惑、辰星俱在東井。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year, in the fourth month, on the day guisi, Great White, Mars, and the Morning Star were all in Eastern Well.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guisi in the fourth month of the fifth Yongyuan year Venus, Mars, and Mercury all stood in Eastern Well.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月壬午，歲星犯軒轅大星。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month, on the day renwu, Jupiter offended the great star of the Chariot Shaft.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renwu in the seventh month Jupiter crossed the principal star of the Chariot Shaft.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月，金在南斗魁中。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month, metal was in the Dipper’s head.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Venus stood within the head of the Southern Dipper.

manualTranslations.zh: 火犯房北第一星。
manualTranslations.literal: Fire offended the first northern star of Room.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mars trespassed on the first northern star of Room.

manualTranslations.zh: 東井，秦地，爲法。
manualTranslations.literal: Eastern Well is the Qin quarter and stands for law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Eastern Well corresponds to Qin and governs legal affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 三星合，内外有兵，又爲法令及水。
manualTranslations.literal: Three stars joined: troops within and without, and also statutes and water.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The conjunction of three stars augured war at home and abroad, legal turmoil, and flood.

manualTranslations.zh: 金入斗口中，爲大將將死。
manualTranslations.literal: Metal entering the mouth of the Dipper means a great general will die.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Venus in the Dipper’s gap foretold the death of a field marshal.

manualTranslations.zh: 火犯房北第一星，爲將相。
manualTranslations.literal: Fire offending the first northern star of Room means generals and ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mars on Room’s northern star betokened peril for generals and ministers.

manualTranslations.zh: 其六年正月，司徒丁鸿薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth year’s first month, Minister over the Masses Ding Hong passed away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year Minister over the Masses Ding Hong died.

manualTranslations.zh: 七月水，大漂殺人民，傷五谷。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month water rose, flooding greatly and killing the people and injuring the five grains.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month floods drowned the people and ruined the harvest.

manualTranslations.zh: 許侯馬光有罪自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Marquis Xu Ma Guang, guilty of a crime, killed himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Marquis Ma Guang of Xu, convicted of a crime, took his own life.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月，行車騎將軍事鄧鸿、越騎校尉馮柱發左右羽林、北軍五校士及八郡迹射、烏桓、鮮卑，合四万騎，與度遼將軍朱徵、護烏桓校尉任尚、中郎將杜崇征叛胡。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month, acting chariot-and-cavalry general Deng Hong and colonel of rapid cavalry Feng Zhu mobilized the Left and Right Forest guards, the Five Colonies of the Northern Army, marksmen from eight commanderies, Wuhuan, and Xianbei—forty thousand horsemen in all—with trans-Liao general Zhu Zheng, Protector of the Wuhuan Ren Shang, and General of the Gentlemen of the Household Du Chong to campaign against rebel Hu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Deng Hong as acting chariot-and-cavalry general and Rapid Cavalry Colonel Feng Zhu raised the imperial guards, the Five Colonies, marksmen from eight commanderies, and Wuhuan and Xianbei allies—forty thousand horse in all—and with Zhu Zheng as trans-Liao general, Ren Shang as Protector of the Wuhuan, and Du Chong as household general marched against rebel Hu forces.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月，車騎將軍鸿坐追虏失利，下獄死。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month, chariot-and-cavalry general Hong, for failing in pursuit of the enemy, was imprisoned and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Hong was jailed and died for bungling the pursuit.

manualTranslations.zh: 度遼將軍徵、中郎將崇皆抵罪。
manualTranslations.literal: Trans-Liao general Zheng and household general Chong were both punished according to their crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zheng and Du Chong were sentenced for their failures.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年正月丁未，有流星起天津，入紫宫中滅。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh year, in the first month, on the day dingwei, a meteor rose from the Celestial Ford and was extinguished entering the Purple Palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the first month of the seventh year a meteor rose at the Celestial Ford and vanished within the Purple Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 色青黄，有光。
manualTranslations.literal: Its color was green-yellow and luminous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It shone green-yellow with a steady glow.

manualTranslations.zh: 二月癸酉，金、火俱在参。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month, on the day guiyou, metal and fire were both in Shen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the second month Venus and Mars shared Orion (Shen).

manualTranslations.zh: 戊寅，金、火俱在東井。
manualTranslations.literal: On wuyin, metal and fire were both in Eastern Well.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On wuyin Venus and Mars both stood in Eastern Well.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月甲寅，水、土、金俱在軫。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jiayin, water, earth, and metal were all in Axletree.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the eighth month Mercury, Saturn, and Venus converged in Axletree.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一月甲戌，金、火俱在心。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jiaxu, metal and fire were both in Heart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiaxu in the eleventh month Venus and Mars shared Heart.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月己卯，有流星起文昌，入紫宫消。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jimao, a meteor rose from Prosperity Literature and was extinguished entering the Purple Palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jimao in the twelfth month a meteor rose at Prosperity Literature and died out in the Purple Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙辰，火、金、水俱在斗。
manualTranslations.literal: On bingchen, fire, metal, and water were all in the Dipper.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingchen Mars, Venus, and Mercury all stood in the Dipper.

manualTranslations.zh: 流星入紫宫，金、火在心，皆爲大喪。
manualTranslations.literal: A meteor entering the Purple Palace; metal and fire in Heart—all mean great mourning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A meteor into the Purple Palace and Venus and Mars in Heart all presaged a state bereavement.

manualTranslations.zh: 三星合軫，爲白衣之會，金、火俱在参、東井，皆爲外兵，有死將。
manualTranslations.literal: Three stars joining in Axletree means a gathering in white; metal and fire together in Shen and Eastern Well both mean foreign troops and a dead general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Three stars in Axletree foretold a great funeral; Venus and Mars in Shen and Eastern Well augured foreign war and a general’s death.

manualTranslations.zh: 三星俱在斗，有戮將，若有死相。
manualTranslations.literal: Three stars all in the Dipper: executed generals, or perhaps a dead minister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Three stars in the Dipper betokened executed commanders or the fall of a chief minister.

manualTranslations.zh: 八年四月乐成王黨，七月乐成王宗皆薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth year, in the fourth month Prince Dang of Lecheng; in the seventh month Prince Zong of Lecheng—both passed away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Prince Dang of Lecheng died in the fourth month and Prince Zong of Lecheng in the seventh.

manualTranslations.zh: 將兵長史吳棽坐事征下獄誅。
manualTranslations.literal: Chief clerk of the general-in-command Wu Sen, summoned for an offense, was imprisoned and executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu Sen, chief clerk to the campaigning general, was recalled, jailed, and executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 十月，北海王威自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month, Prince Wei of Beihai killed himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Prince Wei of Beihai took his own life.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月，陳王羡薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month, Prince Xian of Chen passed away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Prince Xian of Chen died.

manualTranslations.zh: 其九年閏月，皇太后竇氏崩。
manualTranslations.literal: In the intercalary month of the ninth year, Empress Dowager Dou passed away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month of the ninth year Empress Dowager Dou died.

manualTranslations.zh: 遼東鮮卑反，太守祭参不追虏，征下獄誅。
manualTranslations.literal: Liaodong Xianbei rebelled; governor Ji Can did not pursue the enemy and was summoned, imprisoned, and executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Liaodong Xianbei rose, Governor Ji Can failed to pursue them and was recalled, jailed, and executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月，司徒劉方坐事免官，自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month, Minister over the Masses Liu Fang, for an offense, was removed from office and killed himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Minister of Works Liu Fang was dismissed for misconduct and committed suicide.

manualTranslations.zh: 陇西羌反，遣执金吾劉尚行征西將軍事，越騎校尉节鄉侯趙世發北軍五校、黎陽、雍营及邊胡兵三万騎，征西羌。
manualTranslations.literal: The Longxi Qiang rebelled; the court sent Bearer of the Golden Mace Liu Shang as acting general on a western campaign, and Rapid Cavalry Colonel Marquis of Jiexiang Zhao Shi mobilized the Five Colonies of the Northern Army, the Liyang and Yong camps, and thirty thousand border Hu cavalry to campaign against the western Qiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Longxi Qiang rebelled, Liu Shang was sent with the golden mace as acting western commander, and Zhao Shi, Rapid Cavalry Colonel and marquis of Jiexiang, raised the Five Colonies, the Liyang and Yong garrisons, and thirty thousand frontier horsemen against the western Qiang.

sourceRange.text: 孝章建初元年，正月丁巳，太白在昴西一尺。八月庚寅，彗星出天市，長二尺所，稍行入牽牛三度，积四十日稍滅。太白在昴爲邊兵，彗星出天市爲外軍，牽牛爲吳、越。是時，蛮夷陳纵等及哀牢王類牢反，攻巂唐城。永昌太守王尋走奔楪榆，安夷長宋延爲羌所殺。以武威太守傅育领護羌校尉，馬防行車騎將軍，征西羌。又，阜陵王延與子男魴謀反，大逆无道，得不誅，廢爲侯。二年九月古今注曰：「甲申，金入斗魁。」甲寅，流星過紫宫中，長數丈，散爲三，滅。

localRange.text: 二年九月甲寅，流星過紫宫中，長數丈，散爲三，滅。

context.beforeSource: 其八月壬子，孝明帝崩。

manualTranslations.zh: 孝章建初元年，正月丁巳，太白在昴西一尺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jianchu of Emperor Zhang the Filial and Enlightened, in the first month, on the day dingsi, Great White stood one foot west of Hairy Head.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the first month of Jianchu 1 (76 CE) of Emperor Zhang, Venus stood one foot west of the Hairy Head asterism.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月庚寅，彗星出天市，長二尺所，稍行入牽牛三度，积四十日稍滅。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day gengyin, a comet emerged from the Celestial Market, about two feet long, gradually traveling into Herdboy three degrees; after forty days it gradually faded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengyin in the eighth month a comet rose from the Celestial Market, roughly two feet in train, drifted three degrees into Herdboy, and waned away over forty days.

manualTranslations.zh: 太白在昴爲邊兵，彗星出天市爲外軍，牽牛爲吳、越。
manualTranslations.literal: Great White in Hairy Head means frontier troops; a comet issuing from the Celestial Market means armies from without; Herdboy means Wu and Yue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Venus in the Hairy Head betokened border war; a comet from the Celestial Market, armies abroad; Herdboy, the lands of Wu and Yue.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，蛮夷陳纵等及哀牢王類牢反，攻巂唐城。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time the barbarians Chen Zong and others and Ailao king Lei Lao rebelled and attacked Qitang city.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then Chen Zong of the southern tribes and King Lei Lao of Ailao rose in revolt and stormed Qitang.

manualTranslations.zh: 永昌太守王尋走奔楪榆，安夷長宋延爲羌所殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Yongchang governor Wang Xun fled to Dieyu; Anyi chief Song Yan was killed by the Qiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yongchang’s governor Wang Xun fled toward Dieyu, and Anyi chief Song Yan was slain by Qiang raiders.

manualTranslations.zh: 以武威太守傅育领護羌校尉，馬防行車騎將軍，征西羌。
manualTranslations.literal: Fu Yu, governor of Wuwei, was appointed acting Protector of the Qiang; Ma Fang served as acting chariot-and-cavalry general to campaign against the western Qiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wuwei governor Fu Yu took the post of Protector of the Qiang, and Ma Fang acted as chariot-and-cavalry general in a western Qiang campaign.

manualTranslations.zh: 又，阜陵王延與子男魴謀反，大逆无道，得不誅，廢爲侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Further Prince Yan of Fuling and his son Nan Fang plotted rebellion, a capital crime without principle; he was spared execution and demoted to marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prince Yan of Fuling and his son Nan Fang also plotted treason; though guilty of a capital offense, Yan was spared death and reduced to marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年九月甲寅，流星過紫宫中，長數丈，散爲三，滅。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year, in the ninth month, on the day jiayin: a meteor passed through the Purple Palace, several rods long, scattered into three, and was extinguished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the ninth month of the second Jianchu year (77 CE), a meteor several zhang long crossed the Purple Palace, split into three fragments, and died out.

sourceRange.text: 臣昭案：郎顗傳，陽嘉元年，太白與歲星合於房、心。二年，熒惑失度，盈縮往來，涉歷輿鬼，環繞軒轅。古今注曰：「二年四月壬寅，太白晝見，五月癸巳，又晝見，十一月辛未，又晝見。十二月壬寅，月犯太白。三年十二月辛未，太白晝見。四月乙卯，太白、熒惑入輿鬼。永和元年正月丁卯，太白犯牽牛大星。

sourceRange.text: 古今注曰：「永建元年二月甲午，客星入太微。五月甲子，月入斗。」李氏家書曰：「時天有變氣，李郃上書諫曰：『臣聞天不言，縣象以示吉凶，挺災變異以為譴誡。昔齊桓公遭虹貫牛、斗之變，納管仲之謀，令齊去婦，無近妃宮。桓公聽用，齊以大安。趙有尹史，見月生齒，齕畢大星，占有兵變。趙君曰：「天下共一畢，知為何國也？」下史於獄。其後公子牙謀弒君，血書端門，如史所言。乃月十三日，有客星氣象彗孛，歷天巿、梗河、招搖、槍、棓，十六日入紫宮，迫北辰，十七日復過文昌、泰陵，至天船、積水閒，稍微不見。客星一占曰：「魯星歷天巿者為穀貴，梗河三星備非常，泰陵八星為凶喪，紫宮、北辰為至尊。」如占，恐宮廬之內有兵喪之變，千里之外有非常暴逆之憂。魯星不得過歷尊宿，行度從疾，應非一端，恐復有如王阿母母子賤妾之欲居帝旁耗亂政事者。誠令有之，宜當抑遠，饒足以財。王者權柄及爵祿，人天所重慎，誠非阿妾所宜干豫，天故挺變，明以示人。如不承慎，禍至變成，悔之靡及也。

context.beforeSource: 皆奸人强臣狂乱王室，其于死亡誅戮，兵起宫中，是其應。
context.afterSource: 』」孝順永建二年二月癸未，太白昼見三十九日。

sourceRange.text: 六年二月丁巳，彗星見東方，長六七尺，色青白，西南指营室及坟墓里。郗萌占曰：「彗星出而中營室，天下亂，易政，以五色占之吉凶。」丁丑，彗星在奎一度，長六尺；癸未，昏見，河圖曰：「彗星出貫奎，庫兵悉出，禍在強侯、外夷，胡應逆首謀也。」西北歷昂、畢；甲申，在東井，遂歷輿鬼、柳、七星、張，光炎及三台，至軒轅中滅。古今注曰：「五月庚寅，太白晝見。十一月甲午，太白晝見。」营室者，天子常宫。坟墓主死。彗星起而在营室、坟墓，不出五年，天下有大喪。后四年，孝順帝崩。昂爲邊兵，又爲趙。羌周馬父子后遂爲寇。又劉文劫清河相射暠，欲立王蒜爲天子，暠不听，殺暠，王閉門距文，官兵捕誅文，蒜以恶人所劫，廢爲尉氏侯，又徙爲犍陽都鄉侯，薨，国绝。歷東井、輿鬼爲秦，皆羌所攻抄。炎及三台，爲三公。是時，太尉杜乔及故太尉李固爲梁冀所陷入，坐文書死。及至注、張爲周，滅于軒轅中爲后宫。其后懿献后以憂死，梁氏被誅，是其應也。漢安二年古今注曰：「元年二月壬午，歲星在太微中。八月癸丑，月犯南斗，入魁中。」正月己亥，太白昼見。

localRange.text: 漢安二年正月己亥，太白昼見。
