sourceRange.text: 金曹主貨幣、鹽、鐵事。倉曹主倉穀事。黃閤主簿錄省衆事。應劭《漢官儀》曰：「世祖詔：『方今選舉，賢佞朱紫錯用。丞相故事，四科取士。一曰德行高妙，志節清白；二曰學通行修，經中博士；三曰明達法令，足以決疑，能案章覆問，文中御史；四曰剛毅多略，遭事不惑，明足以決，才任三輔令：皆有孝悌廉公之行。自今以後，審四科辟召，及刺史、二千石察茂才尤異孝廉之吏，務盡實覈，選擇英俊、賢行、廉絜、平端於縣邑，務授試以職。有非其人，臨計過署，不便習官事，書疏不端正，不如詔書，有司奏罪名，并正舉者。』又舊河隄謁者，世祖改以三府掾屬爲謁者領之，遷超御史中丞、刺史，或爲小郡。監察黎陽謁者，世祖以幽、并州兵騎定天下，故於黎陽立營，以謁者監之，兵騎千人，復除甚重。謁者任輕，多放情態，順帝改用公解府掾有清名威重者，遷超牧守焉。」《漢官目錄》曰：「建武十二年八月乙未詔書，三公舉茂才各一人，廉吏各二人；光祿歲舉茂才四行各一人，察廉吏三人；中二千石歲察廉吏各一人，廷尉、大司農各二人；將兵將軍歲察廉吏各二人；監察御史、司隷、州牧歲舉茂才各一人。

sourceRange.text: ，上公一人。《大戴記》曰：「傅，傅之德義也。」應劭《漢官儀》曰：「傅者，覆也。」賈生曰：「天子不喻於先聖之德，不知君民之道，不見禮義之正，詩書無宗，學業不法，此太師之責也，古者齊太公職之。天子不惠於庶民，不禮於大臣，不中於折獄，無經於百官，不哀於喪，不敬於祭，不戒於齊，不信於事，此太傅之責也，古者周公職之。天子處位不端，受業不敬，言語不敘，音聲不中，進退升降不以禮，俯仰周旋無節，此太保之責也，古者燕召公職之。天子燕業反其學，左右之習詭其師，荅諸侯，遇大臣，不知文雅之辭，已語之適，簡聞小誦，不博不習，此少師之責也。天子居處出入不以禮，衣服冠帶不以制，御器列側不以度，采服從好不以章，忿恱不以義，與奪不以節，此少傅之責也。天子居處燕私，安而易，樂而耽，飲食不時，醉飽不節，寢起早晏無常，玩好器弄無制，此少保之責也。此古天子自輔弼之禮也，自爲天子而賢智維之，故能慮無失計，舉無過事，終身得中。」，公一人。應劭曰：「自上安下曰尉，武官悉以爲稱。」《前書》曰「秦官」，鄭玄注月令亦曰「秦官」。《尚書·中候》云舜爲太尉，束晳據非秦官，以此追難玄焉。臣昭曰：緯候衆書，宗貴神詭，出沒隱顯，動挾誕怪。該覈陰陽，徼迎起伏，或有先徵，時能後驗，故守寄構思，雜稱曉輔，通儒達好，時略文滯。公輸、益州，具於張衡之詰；無口漢輔，炳乎尹敏之諷。圖讖紛僞，其俗多矣。太尉官實司天，虞舜作宰，璇衡賦政，將是據後位以書前，非唐官之實號乎？太尉所職，即舜所掌，遂以同掌追稱太尉，乃中候之妄，蓋非官之爲謬。康成淵博，自注中候，裁及注禮而忘舜位，豈其實哉！此是不發譏於中候，而正之於月令也。廣微之誚，未探碩意。《說菀》曰「當堯之時，舜爲司徒」。《新論》曰「昔堯試於大麓者，領錄天子事，如今尚書官矣」。《古史考》曰「舜居百揆，總領百事」。說者以百揆堯初別置，於周更名冢宰，斯其然矣。

localRange.text: 太傅，上公一人。本注曰：掌以善导，无常职。世祖以卓茂为太傅，薨，因省。其后每帝初即位，辄置太傅录尚书事，薨，辄省。太尉，公一人。本注曰：掌四方兵事功课，岁尽即奏其殿最而行赏罚。凡郊祀之事，掌亚献；大丧则告谥南郊。凡国有大造大疑，则与司徒、司空通而论之。国有过事，则与二公通谏争之。世祖即位，为大司马。建武二十七年，改为太尉。

sourceRange.text: 故新汲令王隆作《小學·漢官篇》，諸文倜說，較略不究。案：胡廣注隆此篇，其論之注曰：「前安帝時，越騎校尉劉千秋校書東觀，好事者樊長孫與書曰：『漢家禮儀，叔孫通等所草創，皆隨律令在理官，藏於几閣，無記錄者，乆令二代之業，闇而不彰。誠宜撰次，依擬周禮，定位分職，各有條序，令人無愚智，入朝不惑。君以公族元老，正丁其任，焉可以已！』劉君甚然其言，與邑子通人郎中張平子參議未定，而劉君遷爲宗正、衞尉，平子爲尚書郎、太史令，各務其職，未暇恤也。至順帝時，平子爲侍中典校書，方作周官解說，乃欲以漸次述漢事，會復遷河閒相，遂莫能立也。述作之功，獨不易矣。旣感斯言，顧見故新汲令王文山《小學》爲〈漢官篇〉，略道公卿外內之職，旁及四夷，博物條暢，多所發明，足以知舊制儀品。蓋法有成易，而道有因革，是以聊集所宜，爲作詁解，各隨其下，綴續後事，令世施行，庶明厥旨，廣前後憤盈之念，增助來哲多聞之覽焉。」唯班固著〈百官公卿表〉，記漢承秦置官本末，訖于王莽，差有條貫；

sourceRange.text: 三郎，並無員。虎賁中郎將，比二千石。本注曰：主虎賁宿衞。前書武帝置期門，平帝更名虎賁。蔡質漢儀曰：「主虎賁千五百人，無常員，多至千人。戴鶡冠，次右將府。」又虎賁舊作「虎奔」，言如虎之奔也，王莽以古有勇士孟賁，故名焉。孔安國曰「若虎賁獸」，言其甚猛。左右僕射、左右陛長各一人，比六百石。本注曰：僕射，主虎賁郎習射。陛長，主直虎賁，朝會在殿中。漢官曰：「陛長，墨綬銅印。」虎賁中郎，比六百石。虎賁侍郎，比四百石。虎賁郎中，比三百石。荀綽晉百官表注曰：「虎賁諸郎，皆父死子代，漢制也。」節從虎賁，比二百石。四郎。

sourceRange.text: 蔡質漢儀曰：「侍中、常伯，選舊儒高德，博學淵懿。仰占俯視，切問近對，喻旨公卿，上殿稱制，參乘佩璽秉劍。員本八人，陪見舊在尚書令、僕射下，尚書上；今官出入禁中，更在尚書下。司隸校尉見侍中，執板揖，河南尹亦如之。又侍中舊與中官俱止禁中，武帝時，侍中莽何羅挾刃謀逆，由是侍中出禁外，有事乃入，畢即出。王莽秉政，侍中復入，與中官共止。章帝元和中，侍中郭舉與後宮通，拔佩刀驚上，舉伏誅，侍中由是復出外。

sourceRange.text: 漢舊儀曰：「黃門郎屬黃門令，日暮入對青棄門拜，名曰夕郎。」宮閣簿青棄門在南宮。衛（瓘）〔權〕注吳都賦曰：「青棄，戶邊青鏤也。一曰天子門內有眉，格再重，裏青畫曰棄。」獻帝起居注曰：「帝初即位，初置侍中、給事黃門侍郎，員各六人，出入禁中，近侍帷幄，省尚書事。改給事黃門侍郎為侍中侍郎，去給事黃門之號，旋復復故。舊侍中、黃門侍郎以在中宮者，不與近密交政。誅黃門後，侍中、侍郎出入禁闈，機事頗露，由是王允乃奏比尚書，不得出入，不通賓客，自此始也。」又曰：「諸奄人官，悉以議郎、郎中稱，秩如故。諸署令兩梁冠，陛殿上，得召都官從事已下。

context.beforeSource: 及诸王朝见于殿上，引王就坐。

sourceRange.text: 均輸者，前書孟康注曰：「謂諸當所有輸於官者，皆令輸其土地所饒，平其所在時賈，官更於他處貨之。輸者既便，而官有利。」鹽鐵論：「大夫曰：『往者郡國諸侯，各以其物貢輸，往來煩雜，物多苦惡，或不償其費，故郡置輸官以相給運，而便遠方之貢，故曰均輸。開委府于京師，以籠貨物，賤則買，貴則賣，是以縣官不失實，商賈無所利，故曰平準。準平則民不失職，均輸則民不劬勞，故平準、均輸，所以平萬物而便百姓也。』文學曰：『古之賦稅於民也，因其所工，不求所拙。農人納其穫，工女效其織。今釋其所有，責其所無，百姓賤買貨物以便上求。閒者郡國或令民作布絮，吏留難與之為巿。吏之所入非獨齊、陶之縑，蜀、漢之布也，亦民閒之所為耳。行姦賣平，農民重苦，必苦女工繭稅，未見輸之均也。縣官猥發，闔門擅巿，即萬民並收。並收則物騰躍，騰躍則商賈利。自巿則吏容姦，豪吏富商，積貨儲物，以待其急，輕賈姦吏，收以取貴，未見準之平也。蓋古之均輸，所以齊勞逸而便貢輸，非以為利而賈萬物也。』」王隆小學漢官篇曰：「調均報度，輸漕委輸。」胡廣注曰：「邊郡諸官請調者，皆為調均報給之也。以水通輸曰漕。委，積也。郡國所積聚金帛貨賄，隨時輸送諸司農，曰委輸，以供國用。」前書又有都內籍田令、丞，斡官、鐵巿兩長、丞，郡國諸倉農監六十五官長、丞，皆屬之。

sourceRange.text: 古今注曰：「永元三年七月，增尚書令史員。功滿未嘗犯禁者，以補小縣，墨綬。」蔡質曰：「皆選蘭臺、符節上稱簡精練有吏能為之。」決錄注曰：「故事尚書郎以令史久缺補之，世祖始改用孝廉為郎，以孝廉丁邯補焉。邯稱病不就。詔問：『實病？羞為郎乎？』對曰：『臣實不病，恥以孝廉為令史職耳！』世祖怒曰：『虎賁滅頭杖之數十。』詔曰：『欲為郎不？』邯曰：『能殺臣者陛下，不能為郎者臣。』中詔遣出，竟不為郎。邯字叔春，京兆陽陵人也。有高節，正直不撓，後拜汾陰令，治有名跡，遷漢中太守。妻弟為公孫述將，收妻送南鄭獄，免冠徒跣自陳。詔曰：『漢中太守妻乃繫南鄭獄，誰當搔其背垢者？懸牛頭，賣馬脯，盜跖行，孔子語。以邯服罪，且邯一妻，冠履勿謝。』治有異，卒於官。

sourceRange.text: 本注曰：成帝初署尚书四人，韋昭曰：「尚，奉也。」分为四曹：漢舊儀曰：「初置五曹，有三公曹，主斷獄。」蔡質漢儀曰：「典天下歲盡集課事。三公尚書二人，典三公文書。吏曹尚書典選舉齋祀，屬三公曹。靈帝末，梁鵠為選部尚書。」常侍曹尚书主公卿事，蔡質漢儀曰：「主常侍黃門御史事，世祖改曰吏曹。」二千石曹尚书主郡国二千石事，漢舊儀曰：「亦云主刺史。」蔡質漢儀曰：「掌中〔都〕官水火、盜賊、辭訟、罪眚。」民曹尚书主凡吏上书事，蔡質漢舊儀曰：「典繕治功作，監池、苑、囿、盜賊事。」客曹尚书主外国夷狄事。尚書：「龍作納言，出入帝命。」應劭曰：「今尚書官，王之喉舌。」世祖承遵，后分二千石曹，又分客曹为南主客曹、北主客曹，蔡質漢儀曰：「天子出獵，駕，御府曹郎屬之。」凡六曹。周禮天官有司會，鄭玄曰「若今尚書」。

sourceRange.text: 每门候一人，周禮每門下士二人。干寶曰：「如今門候。」六百石。蔡質漢儀曰：「門候見校尉，執板不拜。」本注曰：雒阳城十二门，其正南一门曰平城门，漢官秩曰：「平城門為宮門，不置候，置屯司馬，秩千石。」李尤銘曰：「平城司午，厥位處中。」古今注曰：「建武十四年九月開平城門。」北宫门属卫尉。其余上西门，應劭漢官曰：「上西所以不純白者，漢家初成，故丹〔漆〕鏤之。」李尤銘曰：「上西在季，位月惟戌。」雍门，銘曰：「雍門處中，位月在酉。」广阳门，銘曰：「廣陽位孟，厥月在申。」津门，銘曰：「津名自定，位季月未。」小苑门，开阳门，應劭漢官曰：「開陽門始成未有名，宿昔有一柱來在樓上，琅邪開陽縣上言，縣南城門一柱飛去。光武皇帝使來識視，悵然，遂堅縛之，刻記其年月，因以名焉。」銘曰：「開陽在孟，位月惟巳。」粍门，銘曰：「秏門值季，月位在辰。」中东门，銘曰：「中東處仲，月位當卯。」上东门，銘曰：「上東少陽，厥位在寅。」穀门，銘曰：「穀門北中，位當于子。」夏门，銘曰：「夏門值孟，位月在亥。」凡十二门。蔡質漢儀曰：「雒陽二十四街，街一亭；十二城門，門一亭。

sourceRange.text: 本注曰：凡郡國皆掌治民，進賢勸功，決訟檢奸。常以春行所主縣，勸民農桑，振救乏絶。秋冬遣無害吏案訊諸囚，平其罪法，論課殿最。案律有無害都吏，如今言公平吏。漢書音義曰：「文無所枉害。」蕭何以文無害爲沛主吏掾。

sourceRange.text: 安帝以羌犯法，三輔有陵園之守，乃復置右扶風都尉，京兆虎牙都尉。應劭漢官曰：「蓋天生五材，民並用之，廢一不可，誰能去兵？兵之設尙矣。易稱『絃木爲弧，剡木爲矢，弧矢之利，以威天下。』春秋『三時務農，一時講武』。詩美公劉『匪居匪康，入耕出戰，乃裹餱糧，干戈載（錫）〔揚〕，四方莫當』。自郡國罷材官騎士之後，官無警備，實啓寇心。一方有難，三面救之，發興雷震，煙蒸電激，一切取辨，黔首囂然。不及講其射御，用其戒誓，一旦驅之以卽強敵，猶鳩鵲捕鷹鸇，豚羊弋豺虎，是以毎戰常負，王旅不振。張角懷挾妖偽，遐邇搖蕩，八州幷發，煙炎絳天，牧守梟裂，流血成川。爾乃遠徴三邊殊俗之兵，非我族類，忿鷙縱橫，多殭良善，以爲己功，財貨糞土。哀夫民氓遷流之咎，見出在茲，不教而戰，是謂棄之，跡其禍敗，豈虚也哉！春秋家不藏甲，所以一國威抑私力也。今雖四海殘壤，王命未洽，可折衝壓難，若指於掌，故置右扶風。

manualTranslations.literal: The Odes praise Duke Liu: "Neither dwelling at ease nor living in comfort, going out to plow and going forth to battle, wrapping dry provisions, weapons borne
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Odes praise Duke Liu: "Not idle, not at ease—farming in peace and fighting in war, packing dry rations, bearing arms

manualTranslations.zh: 自郡國罷材官騎士之後，官無警備，實啓寇心。
manualTranslations.literal: After commanderies and kingdoms abolished materiel officers and cavalrymen, the offices had no guard preparations and truly opened the way to bandit hearts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once commanderies disbanded materiel officers and cavalry, local governments lost their guard and truly invited raiders.

manualTranslations.zh: 一方有難，三面救之，發興雷震，煙蒸電激，一切取辨，黔首囂然。
manualTranslations.literal: When one quarter had trouble, three sides rushed to rescue; mobilization thundered like lightning, smoke steamed and sparks flew; everything had to be improvised on the spot, and the black-headed people were in uproar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When trouble struck one sector, three others scrambled to help; mobilization crashed like thunder while everything was improvised on the spot and the common people fell into uproar.

manualTranslations.zh: 不及講其射御，用其戒誓，一旦驅之以卽強敵，猶鳩鵲捕鷹鸇，豚羊弋豺虎，是以毎戰常負，王旅不振。
manualTranslations.literal: There was no time to teach archery and charioteering or to use the oaths of warning; driving men at once against strong enemies was like doves and magpies hunting hawks and kites, or pigs and sheep shooting at wolves and tigers—hence every battle was usually lost and the royal host could not recover its vigor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without time to drill archery and chariotry or renew battle oaths, hurling raw levies against hardened foes was like sending doves after hawks or pigs against tigers—battle after battle was lost and imperial forces could not recover.

manualTranslations.zh: 張角懷挾妖偽，遐邇搖蕩，八州幷發，煙炎絳天，牧守梟裂，流血成川。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Jiao harbored demonic fraud; far and near were shaken; eight provinces erupted together; smoke and flame reddened the sky; regional shepherds and guardians were beheaded and torn apart; blood flowed like rivers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiao spread demonic fraud; the realm shook; eight provinces rose together; smoke reddened the sky; governors were slaughtered and blood ran like rivers.

manualTranslations.zh: 爾乃遠徴三邊殊俗之兵，非我族類，忿鷙縱橫，多殭良善，以爲己功，財貨糞土。
manualTranslations.literal: Then they conscripted from afar soldiers of the three frontiers and alien customs—not our own kind—fierce and unrestrained, coercing many good people and counting it as their own merit, treating wealth like dung.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then distant frontier levies of alien custom—not our own people—were summoned; brutal and unchecked, they pressed good folk into service for private credit and treated wealth like refuse.

manualTranslations.zh: 哀夫民氓遷流之咎，見出在茲，不教而戰，是謂棄之，跡其禍敗，豈虚也哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas for the blame of the people's wandering displacement—the cause appears here; to fight without teaching is called abandoning them; tracing their disaster and defeat, how could it be empty!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas—the roots of mass displacement lie here; sending untrained men to battle is abandonment; trace the ruin and the lesson is no empty warning!

manualTranslations.zh: 春秋家不藏甲，所以一國威抑私力也。

sourceRange.text: 世祖幷省郡縣四百餘所，後世稍復增之。臣昭曰：昔在先代，列爵殊等，九服不同，畿荒制異。雖連帥相司，牧伯分長，而封疆置限，兼庸有數，如身之使臂，手之使指，故能髙卑相固，遠近維緝，群後克穆，共康兆庶。爰及周衰，稍競呑廣，邦國侵爭，遞懷貪略，猶歴數百年，乃能成其幷一，豈非樹之有本，使其然乎？秦兼天下，開設郡縣，孤立獨王，卽以顛亡。漢祖因循，雖不頓革，分置子弟，終龕諸呂之難，漸剖列郡，以減大都之權。後嚴安之徒，猶慷慨發憤，謂千里之威，卽古之強國，慮非安本無窮之計也。孝武之末，始置刺史，監糾非法，不過六條，傳車周流，匪有定鎭，秩裁數百，威望輕寡，得有察舉之勤，未生陵犯之釁。成帝改牧，其萌始大，旣非識治之主，故無取焉爾。世祖中興，監乎政本，復約其職，還遵舊制，斷親奏事，省入惜煩，漸得自重之路。因茲以降，彌於歳年，母后當朝，多以弱守，六合危動，四海潰弊，財盡力竭，綱維撓毀，而八方不能内侵，諸侯莫敢入伐，豈非幹強枝弱，控制素重之所致乎？至孝靈在位，橫流旣及，劉焉徼偽，自爲身謀，非有憂國之心，專懷狼據之策，抗論昏世，薦議愚主，盛稱宜重牧伯，謂足鎭壓萬里，挾姦樹筭，苟罔一時，豈可永爲國本，長期勝術哉？夫聖主御世，莫不大庇生民，承其休謀，傳其典制。猶雲事久獘生，無或通貫，故變改正服，革異質文，分爵三五，參差不一。況在豎騃之君，挾姦詐之臣，共所創置，焉可仍因？大建尊州之規，竟無一日之治。故焉牧益土，造帝服於岷、峨；袁紹取冀，下制書於燕、朔；劉表荊南，郊天祀地；魏祖據兗，遂構皇業：漢之殄滅，禍源乎此。及臻後代，任寄彌廣，委之邦宰之命，授之斧鉞之重，假之都督之威，開之征討之略。晉太康之初，武帝亦疑其然，乃詔曰：「上古及中代，或置州牧，或置刺史，置監御史，皆總綱紀，而不賦政，治民之事，任之諸侯郡守。昔漢末四海分崩，因以呉、蜀自擅，自是刺史内親民事，外領兵馬，此一時之宜爾。今賴宗廟之靈，士大夫之力，江表平定，天下合之爲一，當韜戢干戈，與天下休息。諸州無事者罷其兵，刺史分職，皆如漢氏故事，出頒詔條，入奏事京城。二千石專治民之重，監司淸峻於上，此經久之體也。其便省州牧。」晉武帝又見其獘矣，雖有其言，不卒其事，後嗣纘繼，牧鎭愈重，據地分爭，竟覆天下。昔王畿之大，不過千里，州之所司，廣袤兼遠。爭強虎視之辰，遷鼎革終之日，未嘗不藉蕃兵之權，挾董司之力，逼迫伺隙，陵奪沖幼。其甚者臣主揚兵，骨肉戰野，昆弟梟懸，伯叔屠裂。末壯披心，尾大不掉，旣用此始，亦病以終。傾輈愈襲，莫或途改，致雒京有銜璧之痛，秦臺有不守之酷。胡、羌遞興，氐、鮮更起，摩滅群黎，流禍百世。堅冰所漸，兼縁茲蠹。嗚呼！後之聖王，必不久滯斯跡，靈長之終，當有神筭。不然，則雄捍反拒之事，懼甚於此心，憑強作害之謀，方盛於後意。

manualTranslations.zh: 世祖幷省郡縣四百餘所，後世稍復增之。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Guangwu merged and abolished more than four hundred commanderies and counties; later ages gradually restored some.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The founding emperor merged away over four hundred commanderies and counties; succeeding reigns slowly added others back.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣昭曰：昔在先代，列爵殊等，九服不同，畿荒制異。
manualTranslations.literal: Chen Zhao says: In former ages, ranks of nobility differed in grade; the nine domains were not alike; the regulations of the metropolitan region and the wild borderlands differed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Zhao writes: In antiquity noble ranks were graded, the nine service zones followed distinct rules, and metropolitan and frontier administrations differed in form.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖連帥相司，牧伯分長，而封疆置限，兼庸有數，如身之使臂，手之使指，故能髙卑相固，遠近維緝，群後克穆，共康兆庶。
manualTranslations.literal: Although connected commanders supervised one another and regional shepherds and earls divided authority, yet territorial limits were set and attached domains had fixed numbers, like the body commanding the arm and the hand commanding the fingers; thus high and low were mutually secured, far and near were bound together, the feudal lords were harmonious, and together they brought peace to the myriad people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though overlords and regional shepherds shared governance, borders were fixed and subordinate holdings numbered, like arm and finger—high and low reinforced one another, near and far were knit together, and the feudal lords jointly secured the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 爰及周衰，稍競呑廣，邦國侵爭，遞懷貪略，猶歴數百年，乃能成其幷一，豈非樹之有本，使其然乎？
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhou declined, they gradually competed to swallow and expand; states invaded and fought one another, each in turn harboring greedy designs; only after several hundred years could unity be achieved—is this not because a tree has roots that make it so?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As Zhou decayed, states swallowed one another in greedy wars; centuries passed before unity returned—did not deep roots make that possible?

manualTranslations.zh: 秦兼天下，開設郡縣，孤立獨王，卽以顛亡。
manualTranslations.literal: Qin united the realm, established commanderies and counties, isolated the sole king, and thereby toppled and perished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qin conquered all under Heaven, imposed commanderies and counties, left the emperor isolated—and swiftly fell.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢祖因循，雖不頓革，分置子弟，終龕諸呂之難，漸剖列郡，以減大都之權。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han founder followed precedent; though he did not reform all at once, he enfeoffed sons and younger brothers, yet in the end encountered the disaster of the Lü clan; he gradually carved out commanderies to reduce the power of great metropolises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu kept much of the old order yet enfeoffed kin; still the Lü crisis erupted, and the court slowly split great domains to curb metropolitan power.

manualTranslations.zh: 後嚴安之徒，猶慷慨發憤，謂千里之威，卽古之強國，慮非安本無窮之計也。
manualTranslations.literal: Later men like Yan An still spoke with indignant passion, saying that authority over a thousand li was already the strength of an ancient great state, and fearing this was not a plan to secure the root for endless peace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later critics such as Yan An protested that a thousand-li jurisdiction equaled an ancient great power and warned that such scale could not secure the dynasty forever.

manualTranslations.zh: 孝武之末，始置刺史，監糾非法，不過六條，傳車周流，匪有定鎭，秩裁數百，威望輕寡，得有察舉之勤，未生陵犯之釁。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Emperor Wu, inspectors were first established to oversee and correct illegal acts, limited to six articles; relay carriages circulated without a fixed seat; rank was only several hundred piculs; prestige was light and thin; they could perform the diligence of inspection and recommendation without giving rise to the omen of encroachment and violation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Wu's reign inspectors were introduced to police misconduct under six articles; they toured by relay carriage without fixed headquarters, held modest rank, and could investigate without yet threatening commandery power.

manualTranslations.zh: 成帝改牧，其萌始大，旣非識治之主，故無取焉爾。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Cheng changed them to regional shepherds; the sprout then grew large; since he was not a ruler who understood governance, there is nothing to approve in this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng elevated them to regional shepherds and the office swelled; he was no master of statecraft, so the change merits no praise.

manualTranslations.zh: 世祖中興，監乎政本，復約其職，還遵舊制，斷親奏事，省入惜煩，漸得自重之路。
manualTranslations.literal: The founding emperor in the restoration watched the root of government, again reduced their duties, returned to the old system, cut off personal attendance to report affairs, spared the capital trouble and annoyance, and gradually gained a path to renewed weight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu, restoring the dynasty, trimmed the office back to the old inspector model, ended personal reporting at court, and thereby gave the post a path to renewed authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 因茲以降，彌於歳年，母后當朝，多以弱守，六合危動，四海潰弊，財盡力竭，綱維撓毀，而八方不能内侵，諸侯莫敢入伐，豈非幹強枝弱，控制素重之所致乎？
manualTranslations.literal: From this downward through the years, empress dowagers often held court and mostly ruled through weakness; the six directions trembled in peril, the four seas collapsed in exhaustion, wealth was spent and strength drained, the guiding net was bent and broken—yet the eight directions could not invade inward and feudal lords dared not enter to attack; was this not caused by a strong trunk and weak branches and by control that had long been heavy?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereafter empress dowagers often reigned from weakness while the realm tottered; treasury and strength failed and institutions frayed—yet outsiders did not invade and princes dared not rebel. Was this not because the center stayed strong while branches were kept weak?

manualTranslations.zh: 至孝靈在位，橫流旣及，劉焉徼偽，自爲身謀，非有憂國之心，專懷狼據之策，抗論昏世，薦議愚主，盛稱宜重牧伯，謂足鎭壓萬里，挾姦樹筭，苟罔一時，豈可永爲國本，長期勝術哉？
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ling reigned, the flood had already arrived; Liu Yan sought false credit for his own designs, not with a heart that worried for the state but harboring a wolfish strategy of seizure; he argued against a benighted age and recommended to a foolish sovereign, loudly praising the need to strengthen regional shepherds, saying they could suppress ten thousand li; clutching treachery and planting schemes, he deceived for a moment—how could this forever be the foundation of the state or a long-term winning strategy?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling, Liu Yan schemed for himself, not the realm, urging heavier regional shepherds to control ten thousand li—a treacherous expedient, not a lasting foundation of state.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫聖主御世，莫不大庇生民，承其休謀，傳其典制。
manualTranslations.literal: Sage rulers who govern the age all greatly shelter the living people, inherit their excellent plans, and transmit their canonical institutions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sage rulers shelter the people, inherit sound policy, and pass down established institutions.

manualTranslations.zh: 猶雲事久獘生，無或通貫，故變改正服，革異質文，分爵三五，參差不一。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet it is said that when affairs grow old, decay arises and none can fully penetrate; therefore they changed and corrected robes, altered substance and pattern, divided ranks into threes and fives, uneven and not uniform.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even so, institutions age and decay; hence robes, rites, and noble ranks were repeatedly revised and never uniform.

manualTranslations.zh: 況在豎騃之君，挾姦詐之臣，共所創置，焉可仍因？
manualTranslations.literal: How much less when childish and foolish rulers, together with treacherous and deceitful ministers, jointly created institutions—how could these simply be continued?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How much less should the creations of foolish rulers and scheming ministers be perpetuated unchanged?

manualTranslations.zh: 大建尊州之規，竟無一日之治。
manualTranslations.literal: They greatly built the scheme of exalted provinces, yet not one day of good order resulted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The grand project of exalted provinces produced not a single day of good government.

manualTranslations.zh: 故焉牧益土，造帝服於岷、峨；
manualTranslations.literal: Thus when Yi became shepherd he enlarged territory and fashioned imperial robes at Min and E;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Yan as regional shepherd expanded his domain and donned imperial regalia in the Min-E region;

manualTranslations.zh: 袁紹取冀，下制書於燕、朔；
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan Shao took Ji and issued edicts in Yan and Shuo;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao seized Ji and issued edicts across Yan and the northern frontier;

manualTranslations.zh: 劉表荊南，郊天祀地；
manualTranslations.literal: Liu Biao in southern Jing performed suburban sacrifices to Heaven and earth;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Biao in southern Jing performed suburban rites to Heaven and earth;

manualTranslations.zh: 魏祖據兗，遂構皇業：漢之殄滅，禍源乎此。
manualTranslations.literal: Cao the Wei founder held Yan and then built an imperial enterprise: the extinction of Han had its source in this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao held Yan and built an imperial enterprise—the extinction of Han began here.

manualTranslations.zh: 及臻後代，任寄彌廣，委之邦宰之命，授之斧鉞之重，假之都督之威，開之征討之略。
manualTranslations.literal: When later ages arrived, commissions grew ever broader: they entrusted the mandate of territorial governors, conferred the weight of battle-axes, lent the authority of regional commissioners, and opened the strategy of punitive campaigns.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later ages widened provincial commissions—territorial command, military authority, regional commissioners, and punitive campaigns.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉太康之初，武帝亦疑其然，乃詔曰：「上古及中代，或置州牧，或置刺史，置監御史，皆總綱紀，而不賦政，治民之事，任之諸侯郡守。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Taikang in Jin, Emperor Wu also doubted that this was right, and issued an edict saying: "In high antiquity and the middle ages, sometimes regional shepherds were placed, sometimes inspectors, sometimes supervising clerks; all oversaw the guiding net but did not levy government; matters of governing the people were entrusted to feudal lords and commandery governors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early in Jin Taikang, Emperor Wu also doubted the trend and decreed: "In antiquity and the middle ages, regional shepherds, inspectors, or supervising clerks oversaw discipline but did not govern the people; that duty belonged to feudal lords and commandery governors.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔漢末四海分崩，因以呉、蜀自擅，自是刺史内親民事，外領兵馬，此一時之宜爾。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly at the end of Han the four seas split apart, and Wu and Shu accordingly seized power for themselves; from then inspectors personally handled civil affairs within and commanded troops and horses without—this was a temporary expedient.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Han fell, Wu and Shu seized power and inspectors took civil and military duties—a temporary expedient.

manualTranslations.zh: 今賴宗廟之靈，士大夫之力，江表平定，天下合之爲一，當韜戢干戈，與天下休息。
manualTranslations.literal: Now relying on the spirit of the ancestral temple and the strength of scholar-officials, the lands south of the river are pacified and all under Heaven are united as one; we should sheath weapons and let the realm rest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now, with the south pacified and the realm reunited, arms should be sheathed and the people allowed to rest.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸州無事者罷其兵，刺史分職，皆如漢氏故事，出頒詔條，入奏事京城。
manualTranslations.literal: Provinces without emergency should disband their troops; inspectors should divide duties all according to Han precedent, going out to promulgate edicts and coming in to report affairs at the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Peaceful provinces should disband troops; inspectors should resume Han practice—promulgating edicts abroad and reporting at the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 二千石專治民之重，監司淸峻於上，此經久之體也。
manualTranslations.literal: The two-thousand-picul officials should exclusively bear the weight of governing the people, while supervising offices remain stern and lofty above—this is the enduring structure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand administrators should govern the people while inspectors remain stern overseers above—this is the lasting order.

manualTranslations.zh: 其便省州牧。」
manualTranslations.literal: Let regional shepherds be abolished for convenience."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Regional shepherds should therefore be abolished."

manualTranslations.zh: 晉武帝又見其獘矣，雖有其言，不卒其事，後嗣纘繼，牧鎭愈重，據地分爭，竟覆天下。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin again saw its decay; though he had these words, he did not complete the matter; later successors continued, regional shepherds and garrisons grew heavier, seized territory and fought for division, and in the end overturned the realm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin saw the danger but did not finish the reform; successors made regional shepherds and garrisons heavier until partition overturned the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔王畿之大，不過千里，州之所司，廣袤兼遠。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly the metropolitan region was no more than a thousand li in extent, yet what a province administered was vast in breadth and far in distance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once the royal domain spanned barely a thousand li, yet a province might govern vastly more.

manualTranslations.zh: 爭強虎視之辰，遷鼎革終之日，未嘗不藉蕃兵之權，挾董司之力，逼迫伺隙，陵奪沖幼。
manualTranslations.literal: In times when rivals glared like tigers and the tripods were moved at the end of a dynasty, never did they fail to rely on the authority of frontier troops and wield the power of provincial commissioners, pressing hard and watching for openings, encroaching upon and seizing the young and weak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In ages of fierce rivalry and dynastic collapse, men always leaned on frontier armies and provincial commissioners to press weaknesses and seize the young.

manualTranslations.zh: 其甚者臣主揚兵，骨肉戰野，昆弟梟懸，伯叔屠裂。
manualTranslations.literal: At the extreme, ministers and rulers raised armies; flesh and blood battled in the wilds; brothers were displayed on poles; uncles were torn apart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At worst, lord and minister took up arms, kin slaughtered kin, brothers were displayed on poles, and uncles were torn apart.

manualTranslations.zh: 末壯披心，尾大不掉，旣用此始，亦病以終。
manualTranslations.literal: When the tip grows strong it splits the heart; when the tail grows large it cannot be shaken off—this was both how it began and how it ended in sickness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The branch grew strong enough to split the trunk and the tail too heavy to wag—so the disease began and so it ended.

manualTranslations.zh: 傾輈愈襲，莫或途改，致雒京有銜璧之痛，秦臺有不守之酷。
manualTranslations.literal: Overturning and collision were ever repeated; none changed course on the road, bringing the agony of jade held between the teeth at Luoyang and the cruelty of the Qin terrace undefended.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Reversals piled on reversals until none changed course—Luoyang knew the agony of surrender and the Qin terrace fell undefended.

manualTranslations.zh: 胡、羌遞興，氐、鮮更起，摩滅群黎，流禍百世。
manualTranslations.literal: Hu and Qiang rose in succession; Di and Xianbei arose again; they ground down the multitudes and spread calamity for a hundred generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hu, Qiang, Di, and Xianbei rose in turn, grinding down the people and spreading calamity for generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 堅冰所漸，兼縁茲蠹。
manualTranslations.literal: Hard ice forms by gradual freezing; this pestilence too had its gradual cause.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hard ice forms by degrees—and this rot had long been gathering.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗚呼！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas!

manualTranslations.zh: 後之聖王，必不久滯斯跡，靈長之終，當有神筭。
manualTranslations.literal: Later sage kings will surely not long linger on this path; at the end of enduring fortune there ought to be a divine reckoning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later sage kings will not long follow this path; enduring fortune should end in providential correction.

manualTranslations.zh: 不然，則雄捍反拒之事，懼甚於此心，憑強作害之謀，方盛於後意。
manualTranslations.literal: If not, then deeds of fierce defiance and resistance will inspire fear greater than this present mind, and schemes to rely on strength and do harm will flourish still more in later intentions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Otherwise defiance born of strength will breed greater fear, and plots to harm by force will grow still worse.

sourceRange.text: 不置不監，無驕無忒。程是師徒，寧民康國。

sourceRange.text: 荀綽《晉百官表注》曰：「漢延平中，中二千石奉錢九千，米七十二斛。眞二千石月錢六千五百，米三十六斛。比二千石月錢五千，米三十四斛。一千石月錢四千，米三十斛。六百石月錢三千五百，米二十一斛。四百石月錢二千五百，米十五斛。三百石月錢二千，米十二斛。二百石月錢一千，米九斛。百石月錢八百，米四斛八斗。」獻帝起居注曰：「帝在長安，詔書以三輔地不滿千里，而軍師用度非一，公卿已下不得奏除。其若公田，以秩石爲率，賦（輿）〔與〕令各自收其租稅。」贊曰：帝道淵默，冢帥修德。

manualTranslations.zh: 百石月錢八百，米四斛八斗。」

sourceRange.text: 漢官儀曰：「民年二十三爲正，一歳以爲衞士，一歳爲材官騎士，習射御騎馳戰陣。八月，太守、都尉、令、長、相、丞、尉會都試，課殿最。水家爲樓船，亦習戰射行船。〔邊〕郡太守各將萬騎，行障塞烽火追虜。置長史一人，丞一人，治兵民。當兵行長領。置部尉、千人、司馬、候、農都尉，皆不治民，不給衞士。材官、樓船年五十六老衰，乃得免爲民就田。應合選爲亭長。亭長課徼巡。尉、遊徼、亭長皆習設備五兵。五兵：弓弩，戟，楯，刀劍，甲鎧。鼓吏赤幘行滕，帶劍佩刀，持楯被甲，設矛戟，習射。設十里一亭，亭長、亭候；五里一郵，郵閒相去二里半，司姦盜。亭長持二尺板以劾賊，索繩以收執賊。」風俗通曰：「漢家因秦，大率十里一亭。亭，留也，蓋行旅宿會之所館。亭史舊名負弩，改爲長，或謂亭父。

context.beforeSource: 本注曰：亭長，主求捕盜賊，承望都尉。
context.afterSource: 」里有里魁，民有什伍，善惡以告。

sourceRange.text: 建武十八年，復爲刺史，十二人各主一州，其一州屬司隸校尉。蔡質漢儀曰：「詔書舊典，刺史班宣，周行郡國，省察治政，黜陟能否，斷理冤獄，以六條問事，非條所問，卽不省。一條，強宗豪右，田宅踰制，以強陵弱，以衆暴寡。二條，二千石不奉詔書，遵承典制，倍公向私，旁詔守利，侵漁百姓，聚斂爲姦。三條，二千石不卹疑獄，風厲殺人，怒則任刑，喜則任賞，煩擾苛暴，剝戮黎元，爲百姓所疾，山崩石裂，妖祥訛言。四條，二千石選署不平，苟阿所愛，蔽賢寵頑。五條，二千石子弟怙恃榮勢，請託所監。六條，二千石違公下比，阿附豪強，通行貨賂，割損政令。諸州刺史初除，比諸持板揖不拜。」獻帝起居注曰：「建安十八年三月庚寅，省州幷郡，復禹貢之九州。冀州得魏郡、安平、鉅鹿、河閒、淸河、博陵、常山、趙國、勃海、甘陵、平原、太原、上黨、西河、定襄、鴈門、雲中、五原、朔方、河東、河内、涿郡、漁陽、廣陽、右北平、上谷、代郡、遼東、遼東屬國、遼西、玄菟、樂浪，凡三十二郡。省司隸校尉，以司隸部分屬豫州、冀州、雍州。省涼州刺史，以幷雍州部，郡得弘農、京兆、左馮翊、右扶風、上郡、安定、隴西、漢陽、北地、武都、武威、金城、西平、西郡、張掖、張掖屬國、酒泉、敦煌、西海、漢興、永陽、東安南，凡二十二郡。省交州，以其郡屬荊州。荊州得交州之蒼梧、南海、九眞、交趾、日南，與其舊所部南陽、章陵、南郡、江夏、武陵、長沙、零陵、桂陽，凡十三〔郡〕。益州本部郡有廣漢、漢中、巴郡、犍爲、蜀郡、牂牁、越巂、益州、永昌、犍爲屬國、蜀郡屬國、廣漢屬國，今幷得交州之鬱林、合浦，凡十四〔郡〕。豫州部郡本有潁川、陳國、汝南、沛國、梁國、魯國，今幷得河南、滎陽都尉，凡八郡。徐州部郡得下邳、廣陵、彭城、東海、琅邪、利城、城陽、東莞，凡八郡。靑州得齊國、北海、東萊、濟南、樂安，凡五郡。」獻帝春秋曰：「孫權以歩騭行交州刺史。」東觀書曰：「交趾刺史，持節。」諸州常以八月巡行所部郡國，胡廣注曰：「巡謂驛馬也。縣次傳駕之，以走疾，猶古言附遂。」録囚徒，胡廣曰：「縣邑囚徒，皆閲録視，參考辭狀，實其眞偽。有侵冤者，卽時平理也。」考殿最。胡廣曰：「課第長吏不稱職者爲殿，舉免之。其有治能者爲最。察上尤異州，又狀州中吏民茂才異等，歳舉一人。」初歳盡詣京都奏事，胡廣曰：「所察有條應繩異者，輒覆問之，不茹柔吐剛也。歳盡，齎所狀納京師，名奏事，差其遠近，各有常會。」中興但因計吏。胡廣曰：「不復自詣京師，其所道皆如舊典。」東觀書曰：「和帝初，張酺上言：『臣聞王者法天，熒惑奏事太微，故州牧刺史入奏事，所以通下問知外事也。數十年以來，重其道歸煩撓，故時止勿奏事，今因以爲故事。臣愚以爲刺史視事滿歳，可令奏事如舊典，問州中風俗，恐好惡過所道，事所聞見，考課衆職，下章所告，及所自舉有意者賞異之，其尤無狀，逆詔書，行罪法，冀敕戒其餘，令各敬愼所職，於以衰滅貪邪便佞。』」韓詩外傳曰：「王者必立牧，方三人，所以使闚遠牧衆也。遠方之民，有飢寒而不得衣食，獄訟而冤失，職賢而不舉者，入告天子。天子於其君之朝也，揖而進之曰：『意朕之政教，有不得爾者邪？如何乃有飢寒而不得衣食，獄訟而冤失，職賢而不舉？』然後其君退而與其卿大夫謀之。遠方之民聞，皆曰『誠天子也』。夫我居之辟，見我之近也；我居之幽，見我之明也。可欺乎哉！可欺乎哉！故牧者所以開四目，通四聰。

localRange.text: 建武十八年，复为刺史，十二人各主一州，其一州属司隶校尉。诸州常以八月巡行所部郡国，录囚徒，考殿最。初岁尽诣京都奏事，中兴但因计吏。

context.beforeSource: 成帝更爲牧，秩二千石。
context.afterSource: 」皆有從事史、假佐。
context.beforeLocal: 成帝更为牧，秩二千石。
context.afterLocal: 皆有从事史、假佐。

manualTranslations.zh: 蔡質漢儀曰：「詔書舊典，刺史班宣，周行郡國，省察治政，黜陟能否，斷理冤獄，以六條問事，非條所問，卽不省。
manualTranslations.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Observances says: "By the old canon of edicts, inspectors promulgated and proclaimed, toured the commanderies and kingdoms, inspected and examined governance, demoted or promoted according to ability, decided wrongful imprisonments, and investigated affairs by six articles; what fell outside the articles was not examined.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cai Zhi's Han Observances records: "By ancient edict, inspectors proclaimed imperial orders, toured commanderies and kingdoms, inspected governance, promoted or dismissed officials, redressed wrongful imprisonment, and investigated affairs under six articles; matters outside those articles were not pursued.

manualTranslations.zh: 一條，強宗豪右，田宅踰制，以強陵弱，以衆暴寡。
manualTranslations.literal: Article one: powerful clans and great houses whose fields and dwellings exceeded regulations, using strength to bully the weak and numbers to oppress the few.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Article one: powerful clans whose estates exceeded regulations, bullying the weak and oppressing the few.

manualTranslations.zh: 二條，二千石不奉詔書，遵承典制，倍公向私，旁詔守利，侵漁百姓，聚斂爲姦。
manualTranslations.literal: Article two: two-thousand-picul officials who did not follow edicts, uphold canonical institutions, turned from public to private, sought profit on the side, preyed upon the people, and amassed wealth as treachery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Article two: grand administrators who defied edicts, pursued private gain, preyed on the people, and amassed wealth corruptly.

manualTranslations.zh: 三條，二千石不卹疑獄，風厲殺人，怒則任刑，喜則任賞，煩擾苛暴，剝戮黎元，爲百姓所疾，山崩石裂，妖祥訛言。
manualTranslations.literal: Article three: two-thousand-picul officials who did not care for doubtful cases, encouraged killing, imposed punishments in anger and rewards in joy, were vexatious and cruel, flayed and slaughtered the people, were hated by the common folk, and were linked to omens such as mountain collapses, stone splits, and false prodigies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Article three: grand administrators who ignored doubtful cases, killed recklessly, punished in anger and rewarded in joy, tormented the people, and were hated amid omens and false reports.

manualTranslations.zh: 四條，二千石選署不平，苟阿所愛，蔽賢寵頑。
manualTranslations.literal: Article four: two-thousand-picul officials whose selections and appointments were unfair, who fawned on favorites, concealed the worthy, and pampered the obstinate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Article four: grand administrators who appointed unfairly, favored cronies, hid the worthy, and indulged the obstinate.

manualTranslations.zh: 五條，二千石子弟怙恃榮勢，請託所監。
manualTranslations.literal: Article five: sons and younger brothers of two-thousand-picul officials who relied on glory and power and made requests through those they supervised.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Article five: sons and younger brothers of grand administrators who abused their fathers' power to seek favors within the inspector's jurisdiction.

manualTranslations.zh: 六條，二千石違公下比，阿附豪強，通行貨賂，割損政令。
manualTranslations.literal: Article six: two-thousand-picul officials who violated the public to curry favor below, flattered powerful houses, trafficked in bribes, and cut and damaged government orders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Article six: grand administrators who curried favor with the powerful, accepted bribes, and undermined government orders.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸州刺史初除，比諸持板揖不拜。」
manualTranslations.literal: When provincial inspectors were first appointed, they were compared to those who held tablets and bowed without performing the full prostration."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Newly appointed provincial inspectors bowed with tablet in hand without performing the full prostration."

manualTranslations.zh: 獻帝起居注曰：「建安十八年三月庚寅，省州幷郡，復禹貢之九州。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian's Daily Records note: "In the third month of Jian'an 18, on gengyin, provinces were merged and commanderies cut to restore the nine provinces of Yu's Tribute.

manualTranslations.zh: 冀州得魏郡、安平、鉅鹿、河閒、淸河、博陵、常山、趙國、勃海、甘陵、平原、太原、上黨、西河、定襄、鴈門、雲中、五原、朔方、河東、河内、涿郡、漁陽、廣陽、右北平、上谷、代郡、遼東、遼東屬國、遼西、玄菟、樂浪，凡三十二郡。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jizhou absorbed thirty-two commanderies including Wei, Anping, Julu, Hejian, Qinghe, Boling, Changshan, Zhao, Bohai, Ganling, Pingyuan, Taiyuan, Shangdang, Xihe, Dingxiang, Yanmen, Yunzhong, Wuyuan, Shuofang, Hedong, Henei, Zhuo, Yuyang, Guangyang, Right Beiping, Shanggu, Dai, Liaodong, Liaodong Dependent State, Liaoxi, Xuantu, and Lelang.

manualTranslations.zh: 省司隸校尉，以司隸部分屬豫州、冀州、雍州。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Colonel Director of Retainers was abolished and the metropolitan region was divided among Yuzhou, Jizhou, and Yongzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 省涼州刺史，以幷雍州部，郡得弘農、京兆、左馮翊、右扶風、上郡、安定、隴西、漢陽、北地、武都、武威、金城、西平、西郡、張掖、張掖屬國、酒泉、敦煌、西海、漢興、永陽、東安南，凡二十二郡。

manualTranslations.zh: 省交州，以其郡屬荊州。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou was abolished and its commanderies transferred to Jingzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 荊州得交州之蒼梧、南海、九眞、交趾、日南，與其舊所部南陽、章陵、南郡、江夏、武陵、長沙、零陵、桂陽，凡十三〔郡〕。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jingzhou absorbed Cangwu, Nanhai, Jiuzhen, Jiaozhi, and Rinan from the old Jiaozhou together with Nanyang, Zhangling, Nan, Jiangxia, Wuling, Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang—thirteen commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 益州本部郡有廣漢、漢中、巴郡、犍爲、蜀郡、牂牁、越巂、益州、永昌、犍爲屬國、蜀郡屬國、廣漢屬國，今幷得交州之鬱林、合浦，凡十四〔郡〕。
manualTranslations.literal: Yizhou's original commanderies were Guanghan, Hanzhong, Ba, Qianwei, Shu, Zangke, Yuexi, Yizhou, Yongchang, Qianwei Dependent State, Shu Dependent State, and Guanghan Dependent State; it now also received Yulin and Hepu from Jiaozhou—fourteen commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yizhou retained Guanghan, Hanzhong, Ba, Qianwei, Shu, Zangke, Yuexi, Yizhou, Yongchang, and the three dependent states, and also received Yulin and Hepu from Jiaozhou—fourteen commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 豫州部郡本有潁川、陳國、汝南、沛國、梁國、魯國，今幷得河南、滎陽都尉，凡八郡。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuzhou originally had Yingchuan, Chen, Runan, Pei, Liang, and Lu; it now also received Henan and the commandant of Xingyang—eight commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuzhou originally comprised Yingchuan, Chen, Runan, Pei, Liang, and Lu and now also received Henan and the Xingyang commandant—eight commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 徐州部郡得下邳、廣陵、彭城、東海、琅邪、利城、城陽、東莞，凡八郡。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuzhou's commanderies were Xiapi, Guangling, Pengcheng, Donghai, Langye, Licheng, Chengyang, and Dongguan—eight commanderies in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuzhou comprised Xiapi, Guangling, Pengcheng, Donghai, Langye, Licheng, Chengyang, and Dongguan—eight commanderies in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 靑州得齊國、北海、東萊、濟南、樂安，凡五郡。」
manualTranslations.literal: Qingzhou received Qi, Beihai, Donglai, Jinan, and Le'an—five commanderies in all."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qingzhou comprised Qi, Beihai, Donglai, Jinan, and Le'an—five commanderies in all."

manualTranslations.zh: 獻帝春秋曰：「孫權以歩騭行交州刺史。」
manualTranslations.literal: Chronicle of Emperor Xian says: "Sun Quan had Bu Zhi act as inspector of Jiaozhou."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Chronicle of Emperor Xian records: "Sun Quan had Bu Zhi serve as acting inspector of Jiaozhou."

manualTranslations.zh: 東觀書曰：「交趾刺史，持節。」
manualTranslations.literal: Book of the Eastern Lodge says: "The inspector of Jiaozhi held the staff of authority."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of the Eastern Lodge notes: "The inspector of Jiaozhi bore the credential staff."

manualTranslations.zh: 諸州常以八月巡行所部郡國，胡廣注曰：「巡謂驛馬也。
manualTranslations.literal: The provinces regularly in the eighth month toured the commanderies and kingdoms under their jurisdiction. Hu Guang annotates: "Touring means relay horses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Each province customarily made an autumn circuit of its commanderies and kingdoms. Hu Guang explains: "The tour used relay horses.

manualTranslations.zh: 縣次傳駕之，以走疾，猶古言附遂。」
manualTranslations.literal: At each county stop relay teams drove them, running swiftly, as in the ancient phrase 'attached relay.'"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At each county relay teams drove them at speed, as in the ancient term for attached relay transport."

manualTranslations.zh: 録囚徒，胡廣曰：「縣邑囚徒，皆閲録視，參考辭狀，實其眞偽。
manualTranslations.literal: They reviewed prisoners. Hu Guang says: "Prisoners in counties and districts were all examined and reviewed, with testimony checked to verify truth and falsehood.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They reviewed prisoners. Hu Guang says: "County prisoners were examined, testimony checked, and truth verified.

manualTranslations.zh: 有侵冤者，卽時平理也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Where there was oppression or injustice, it was promptly redressed."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cases of oppression or injustice were promptly redressed."

manualTranslations.zh: 考殿最。
manualTranslations.literal: They assessed best and worst performance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They rated administrative performance.

manualTranslations.zh: 胡廣曰：「課第長吏不稱職者爲殿，舉免之。
manualTranslations.literal: Hu Guang says: "In ranking officials, those unfit for office were rated 'lowest' and recommended for dismissal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hu Guang says: "Officials ranked lowest for incompetence were recommended for dismissal.

manualTranslations.zh: 其有治能者爲最。
manualTranslations.literal: Those with governing ability were rated 'best.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those with governing ability were rated best.

manualTranslations.zh: 察上尤異州，又狀州中吏民茂才異等，歳舉一人。」
manualTranslations.literal: Outstanding cases were reported upward; the inspector also presented men of outstanding talent and special distinction among officials and people of the province, one man recommended each year."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Outstanding cases were reported upward, and one man of special talent among the province's officials and people was recommended each year."

manualTranslations.zh: 初歳盡詣京都奏事，胡廣曰：「所察有條應繩異者，輒覆問之，不茹柔吐剛也。
manualTranslations.literal: At first at year's end they went to the capital to report affairs. Hu Guang says: "Where what they inspected had items that should be bound by rule or were unusual, they were questioned again; they did not swallow the soft and spit out the hard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, inspectors journeyed to the capital at year's end to report. Hu Guang says: "Doubtful or unusual findings were reinvestigated; they did not favor the weak over the strong.

manualTranslations.zh: 歳盡，齎所狀納京師，名奏事，差其遠近，各有常會。」
manualTranslations.literal: At year's end they brought their reports to the capital, called 'reporting affairs,' with distances graded and fixed schedules for each."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At year's end they carried their reports to the capital—called reporting affairs—with fixed schedules according to distance."

manualTranslations.zh: 中興但因計吏。
manualTranslations.literal: In the restoration they relied only on the accounting clerks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the restoration this duty devolved on the accounting clerks who came up with the tribute tallies.

manualTranslations.zh: 胡廣曰：「不復自詣京師，其所道皆如舊典。」
manualTranslations.literal: Hu Guang says: "They no longer went in person to the capital; what they transmitted followed the old canon."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hu Guang adds: "Inspectors no longer went in person; their reports followed the old canon."

manualTranslations.zh: 東觀書曰：「和帝初，張酺上言：『臣聞王者法天，熒惑奏事太微，故州牧刺史入奏事，所以通下問知外事也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of the Eastern Lodge says: "Early in Emperor He, Zhang Ti memorialized: 'I have heard that kings model Heaven; Mars reports affairs in the Supreme Palace Enclosure, therefore regional shepherds and inspectors enter to report affairs so as to connect below and learn of outer affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of the Eastern Lodge records: "Early in Emperor He's reign Zhang Ti memorialized: 'The king models Heaven; Mars reports in the Supreme Palace Enclosure, so regional shepherds and inspectors reported at court to learn of distant affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 數十年以來，重其道歸煩撓，故時止勿奏事，今因以爲故事。
manualTranslations.literal: For several decades the burden of their journeys caused trouble and annoyance, so at times reporting was stopped; now this has become precedent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For decades the journey burdened the court, so reporting was suspended and that suspension became precedent.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣愚以爲刺史視事滿歳，可令奏事如舊典，問州中風俗，恐好惡過所道，事所聞見，考課衆職，下章所告，及所自舉有意者賞異之，其尤無狀，逆詔書，行罪法，冀敕戒其餘，令各敬愼所職，於以衰滅貪邪便佞。』」
manualTranslations.literal: I foolishly think that when an inspector has completed a full year in office, he may be ordered to report as in the old canon, inquiring into customs of the province, fearing that likes and dislikes exceed what is reported and that matters seen and heard are not conveyed; examining and assessing all offices; rewarding with distinction those reported below or self-recommended with merit; punishing by law those utterly without propriety who defy edicts, hoping to admonish the rest and make each reverently careful in his post, thereby to diminish greedy, wicked, and fawning men.'"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I propose that after a full year in office inspectors resume reporting as of old—inquiring into provincial customs, reviewing all offices, rewarding merit, and punishing those who defy edicts, so the rest may be admonished and greedy flatterers diminished.'"

manualTranslations.zh: 韓詩外傳曰：「王者必立牧，方三人，所以使闚遠牧衆也。
manualTranslations.literal: Han Ying's Outer Commentary on the Odes says: "Kings must establish shepherds, three for each direction, in order to observe from afar and shepherd the multitudes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Ying's Outer Commentary on the Odes says: "Kings must appoint shepherds—three for each direction—to watch from afar and govern the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 遠方之民，有飢寒而不得衣食，獄訟而冤失，職賢而不舉者，入告天子。
manualTranslations.literal: Among distant peoples, if there were hunger and cold without food and clothing, lawsuits with wrongful loss, or worthy men in office not recommended, they entered to report to the Son of Heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If distant peoples suffered hunger, wrongful imprisonment, or failure to recommend the worthy, the shepherd reported to the Son of Heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 天子於其君之朝也，揖而進之曰：『意朕之政教，有不得爾者邪？
manualTranslations.literal: When the Son of Heaven was at that lord's court, he bowed and advanced him, saying: 'Do you think my government and teaching have failed you in some way?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that lord's audience the Son of Heaven bowed him forward and asked: 'Do you think my government has failed you?

manualTranslations.zh: 如何乃有飢寒而不得衣食，獄訟而冤失，職賢而不舉？』
manualTranslations.literal: How is it that there are hunger and cold without food and clothing, lawsuits with wrongful loss, and worthy men in office not recommended?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How then are there hunger and cold, wrongful lawsuits, and failure to recommend the worthy?'

manualTranslations.zh: 然後其君退而與其卿大夫謀之。
manualTranslations.literal: Then that lord withdrew and deliberated with his ministers and grandees.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The lord then withdrew to consult his ministers and grandees.

manualTranslations.zh: 遠方之民聞，皆曰『誠天子也』。
manualTranslations.literal: When distant peoples heard, all said, 'Truly a Son of Heaven.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearing this, distant peoples said, 'Truly a Son of Heaven.'

manualTranslations.zh: 夫我居之辟，見我之近也；
manualTranslations.literal: Though I dwell in seclusion, he sees me as near;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though I dwell afar, he sees me as near;

manualTranslations.zh: 我居之幽，見我之明也。
manualTranslations.literal: though I dwell in obscurity, he sees me as bright.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: though I dwell in obscurity, he sees me as bright.

manualTranslations.zh: 可欺乎哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Can one be deceived!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Can one be deceived!

manualTranslations.zh: 可欺乎哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Can one be deceived!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Can one be deceived!

manualTranslations.zh: 故牧者所以開四目，通四聰。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore shepherds are what open the four eyes and connect the four ears.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore shepherds open the four eyes and connect the four ears of the ruler.

sourceRange.text: 本注曰：諸曹略如郡員，五官爲廷掾，監鄕五部，春夏爲勸農掾，秋冬爲制度掾。漢官曰：「雒陽令秩千石，丞三人四百石，孝廉左尉四百石，孝廉右尉四百石。員吏七百九十六人，十三人四百石。鄕有秩、獄史五十六人，佐史、鄕佐七十七人，斗食、令史、嗇夫、假五十人，官掾史、幹小史二百五十人，書佐九十人，〔脩〕行二百六十人。」鄕置有秩、三老、遊徼。本注曰：有秩，郡所署，秩百石，漢官曰：「鄕戸五千，則置有秩。」掌一鄕人；風俗通曰：「秩則田閒大夫，言其官裁有秩耳。」其鄕小者，縣置嗇夫一人風俗通曰：「嗇者，省也。夫，賦也。言消息百姓，均其役賦。皆主知民善惡，爲役先後，知民貧富，爲賦多少，平其差品。

localRange.text: 本注曰：诸曹略如郡员，五官为廷掾，监乡五部，春夏为劝农掾，秋冬为制度掾。乡置有秩、三老、游徼。本注曰：有秩，郡所署，秩百石，掌一乡人；其乡小者，县置啬夫一人。皆主知民善恶，为役先后，知民贫富，为赋多少，平其差品。

context.beforeSource: 」各署諸曹掾史。
context.afterSource: 三老掌教化。
context.beforeLocal: 各署诸曹掾史。
context.afterLocal: 三老掌教化。

manualTranslations.zh: 漢官曰：「雒陽令秩千石，丞三人四百石，孝廉左尉四百石，孝廉右尉四百石。
manualTranslations.literal: Han Offices says: "The Luoyang magistrate ranked at one thousand piculs; three assistants at four hundred piculs; filial-and-incorrupt left commandant at four hundred piculs; filial-and-incorrupt right commandant at four hundred piculs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Offices lists the Luoyang magistrate at one thousand piculs, three assistants at four hundred, and filial-and-incorrupt left and right commandants at four hundred each.

manualTranslations.zh: 員吏七百九十六人，十三人四百石。
manualTranslations.literal: The establishment was seven hundred ninety-six clerks, thirteen at four hundred piculs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The staff totaled seven hundred ninety-six clerks, thirteen at four hundred piculs.

manualTranslations.zh: 鄕有秩、獄史五十六人，佐史、鄕佐七十七人，斗食、令史、嗇夫、假五十人，官掾史、幹小史二百五十人，書佐九十人，〔脩〕行二百六十人。」
manualTranslations.literal: Township ranked officers and prison clerks fifty-six; assistant clerks and township assistants seventy-seven; dou-food, order-clerks, requisition officers, and acting clerks fifty; bureau clerks and document runners two hundred fifty; document assistants ninety; [xiu] runners two hundred sixty."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fifty-six township ranked officers and prison clerks; seventy-seven assistant clerks and township aides; fifty dou-food, order-clerks, requisition officers, and acting clerks; two hundred fifty bureau clerks and document runners; ninety document assistants; and two hundred sixty runners."

manualTranslations.zh: 漢官曰：「鄕戸五千，則置有秩。」
manualTranslations.literal: Han Offices says: "When a township had five thousand households, a ranked officer was placed."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Offices adds: "A township of five thousand households received a ranked officer."

manualTranslations.zh: 風俗通曰：「秩則田閒大夫，言其官裁有秩耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs says: "Ranked officer means field-side grandee—speaking of an office with measured authority."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs explains: "Ranked officer means a field-side grandee—an office of measured authority."

manualTranslations.zh: 其鄕小者，縣置嗇夫一人風俗通曰：「嗇者，省也。
manualTranslations.literal: Where the township was small, the county placed one requisition officer. The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs says: "Se means to examine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Smaller townships got one county requisition officer. The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs says: "Se means to examine.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫，賦也。
manualTranslations.literal: Fu means levy."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fu means levy."

manualTranslations.zh: 言消息百姓，均其役賦。
manualTranslations.literal: It means to inform the people and equalize their corvée and levies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The title means to keep the people informed and balance corvée and levies.

manualTranslations.zh: 本注曰：有秩，郡所署，秩百石，漢官曰：「鄕戸五千，則置有秩。」
manualTranslations.literal: The original commentary says: The ranked officer was appointed by the commandery at the one-hundred-picul grade. Han Offices says: "When a township had five thousand households, a ranked officer was placed."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commentary: The ranked officer was a commandery appointment at one hundred piculs. Han Offices adds: "Townships of five thousand households received a ranked officer."

manualTranslations.zh: 掌一鄕人；
manualTranslations.literal: He governed one township's people;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He governed the people of one township;

sourceRange.text: 古今注曰：「建武六年三月，令郡太守、諸侯相病，丞、長史行事。十四年，罷邊郡太守丞，長史領丞職。

context.beforeSource: 郡當邊戍者，丞爲長史。
context.afterSource: 」王國之相亦如之。
context.beforeLocal: 郡当边戍者，丞为长史。
context.afterLocal: 王国之相亦如之。

sourceRange.text: 應劭漢官曰：「前書百官表云，萬戸以上爲令，萬戸以下爲長。三邊始孝武皇帝所開，縣戸數百而或爲令。荊揚江南七郡，唯有臨湘、南昌、呉三令爾。及南陽穰中，土沃民稠，四五萬戸而爲長。桓帝時，以〔汝〕南陽安爲女公主邑，改號爲令，主薨復復其故。若此爲繫其本。俗説令長以水土爲之，及秩髙下，皆無明文。班固通儒，述一代之書，斯近其眞。」本注曰：皆掌治民，顯善勸義，禁奸罰惡，理訟平賊，恤民時務，秋冬集課，上計於所屬郡國。胡廣曰：「秋冬歳盡，各計縣戸口墾田，錢穀入出，盜賊多少，上其集簿。丞尉以下，歳詣郡，課校其功。功多尤爲最者，於廷尉勞勉之，以勸其後。負多尤爲殿者，於後曹別責，以糾怠慢也。諸對辭窮尤困，收主者，掾史關白太守，使取法。丞尉縛責，以明下轉相督敕，爲民除害也。明帝詔書不得僇辱黃綬，以別小人吏也。

localRange.text: 本注曰：皆掌治民，显善劝义，禁奸罚恶，理讼平贼，恤民时务，秋冬集课，上计于所属郡国。

context.beforeSource: 侯國之相，秩次亦如之。
context.afterSource: 」凡縣主蠻夷曰道。
context.beforeLocal: 侯国之相，秩次亦如之。
context.afterLocal: 凡县主蛮夷曰道。

manualTranslations.zh: 應劭漢官曰：「前書百官表云，萬戸以上爲令，萬戸以下爲長。
manualTranslations.literal: Ying Shao's Han Offices says: "The Former Book's table of offices states that ten thousand households or more made a magistrate, below ten thousand made a chief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Han Offices cites the Former Book: "Ten thousand households or more made a magistrate; fewer made a chief.

manualTranslations.zh: 三邊始孝武皇帝所開，縣戸數百而或爲令。
manualTranslations.literal: The three frontiers were first opened by Emperor Wu; counties with only several hundred households might still have a magistrate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the three frontiers opened by Emperor Wu, counties of only a few hundred households might still rate a magistrate.

manualTranslations.zh: 荊揚江南七郡，唯有臨湘、南昌、呉三令爾。
manualTranslations.literal: Among the seven commanderies of Jiangnan in Jing and Yang, only Linxiang, Nanchang, and Wu had magistrates.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Of the seven Jiangnan commanderies in Jing and Yang, only Linxiang, Nanchang, and Wu had magistrates.

manualTranslations.zh: 及南陽穰中，土沃民稠，四五萬戸而爲長。
manualTranslations.literal: At Xiang in Nanyang the soil was fertile and the people dense—forty or fifty thousand households yet only a chief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Xiang in Nanyang, fertile and crowded with forty or fifty thousand households, the post remained only a chief.

manualTranslations.zh: 桓帝時，以〔汝〕南陽安爲女公主邑，改號爲令，主薨復復其故。
manualTranslations.literal: In Emperor Huan's time, because Nanyang An was a princess's fief, the title was changed to magistrate; when the princess died it reverted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huan, Nanyang An became a princess's fief and was promoted to magistrate; after her death the old title returned.

manualTranslations.zh: 若此爲繫其本。
manualTranslations.literal: Cases like this tie back to the root principle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such cases follow the underlying rule.

manualTranslations.zh: 俗説令長以水土爲之，及秩髙下，皆無明文。
manualTranslations.literal: Popular explanation says magistrates and chiefs were made according to soil and water, and high or low rank had no written rule.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Folk explanation ties magistrate and chief grades to local conditions, with no fixed written rule for rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 班固通儒，述一代之書，斯近其眞。」
manualTranslations.literal: Ban Gu, a comprehensive scholar, described the institutions of an age—this comes near the truth."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ban Gu, master of the tradition, described an entire dynasty—this is closest to the truth."

manualTranslations.zh: 胡廣曰：「秋冬歳盡，各計縣戸口墾田，錢穀入出，盜賊多少，上其集簿。
manualTranslations.literal: Hu Guang says: "At year's end in autumn and winter, each county tallied registered households, reclaimed fields, cash and grain in and out, and number of bandits, and submitted the summary register.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hu Guang explains: "At autumn and winter year's end each county reported households, reclaimed land, revenue, and banditry in summary registers.

manualTranslations.zh: 丞尉以下，歳詣郡，課校其功。
manualTranslations.literal: Assistants and commandants and below went yearly to the commandery to have their merit examined and checked.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Assistants and commandants went up yearly for performance review.

manualTranslations.zh: 功多尤爲最者，於廷尉勞勉之，以勸其後。
manualTranslations.literal: Those with much merit and especially rated best were encouraged by the minister of justice to urge those who followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Top performers were commended by the minister of justice to encourage the rest.

manualTranslations.zh: 負多尤爲殿者，於後曹別責，以糾怠慢也。
manualTranslations.literal: Those with many faults and especially rated worst were separately reprimanded in the rear bureau to correct negligence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Worst performers were reprimanded in the rear bureau to correct slackness.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸對辭窮尤困，收主者，掾史關白太守，使取法。
manualTranslations.literal: When replies were exhausted and especially distressed, the responsible party was taken; clerks reported to the grand administrator to apply the law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When suspects were cornered in interrogation, responsible parties were seized and clerks reported to the grand administrator for legal action.

manualTranslations.zh: 丞尉縛責，以明下轉相督敕，爲民除害也。
manualTranslations.literal: Assistants and commandants bound and punished them, making clear that subordinates in turn supervised and admonished one another to remove harm for the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Assistants and commandants bound and punished offenders, showing how each level supervised the next to protect the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝詔書不得僇辱黃綬，以別小人吏也。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Ming's edict forbade humiliating holders of the yellow ribbon, to distinguish petty clerks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming forbade humiliating yellow-ribbon officers to separate petty clerks from higher ranks.

sourceRange.text: 及其誅滅，景帝懲之，遂令諸王不得治民，令内史主治民，改丞相曰相，省御史大夫、廷尉、少府、宗正、博士官。武帝改漢内史、中尉、郎中令之名，前書曰：「改漢内史爲京兆尹，中尉爲執金吾，郎中令爲光祿勳。」而王國如故，員職皆朝廷爲署，不得自置。至成帝省内史治民，更令相治民，漢舊儀曰：「大司空何武奏罷内史，相如太守，中尉如都尉，參職。是後中尉爭權，與王相奏，常不和也。」太傅但曰傅。臣昭曰：觀夫髙祖之創業也，豈直鴻勳碩德，大庇群生，蕩其毒虐，厝之和泰而已哉！至於謀深慮久，封建子弟，蕃維盤固，規謀弘遠。及於三趙不終，燕靈夭絶，齊、代、淮、楚皆爲外重，故宋昌曰「外畏齊、楚、淮南」，斯非效與？事過則獘，孰或通之？全國之難，誠固財物之富，作衞之益，亦旣得之於前矣，故賜以幾杖，用息姦謀。嗣隕局下，怨生有以，逮連師構亂，兵交梁闕，禦侮摧寇，肇自密戚。景帝遂削蕃國之權，刻骨肉之援，封爲君而不聽治其民，置爲主而稍賤其臣，矯枉過甚，遂臻於此。呂、霍之危朝，后族愈貴於來寵，呉、楚之叛奔，侯王恆藉以受誚，故賈誼欲衆建以少其力，列虚以侯其生，此乃達觀深識，監於親陪之要者也。冢嗣必傳萬裏之地，分支欲使動搖不得，於經維遠筭，且已礙矣。復哀平之際，劉氏遍於四海，宗正著録，遂以萬數。及乎後漢，彌循前跡，光武十子，並列畿外近郡，孝明八國，不能開庇遠民。國近則不可以大，不大則不足爲強，此所以本枝之援，終以少固。若使漢分兩越置二三親國，剖呉、楚樹數四列蕃，割遼海而分皇枝，開隴蜀而王子弟，使主尊顯，依漢初之貴，民無定限，許滋養之富；若有昏虐之嗣，可得廢而不得削，必傳劉氏。民信所奉，發其侵伐兼幷之釁，峻其他族篡殺之科，制其入貢輕重之法，疎其來朝往復之數。君君臣臣，永許百世之期，一國之民，長無遷動之志，四方得志，聽離官列封，懷賢抱智，隨所適樂土。強弱相侔，遠近相摧，舉其大歸，略其小滯，與其畫一，班之海内。天子之朝，自非異姓僭奪，不得興勤王之師。諸蕃國，自非雜互篡主，不降討伐之詔。犬牙相經，共爲嚴國，雖王莽善盜，將何因而敢竊，曹操雄勇，亦安能以得士。斯無俟極聖然克行，明賢粗識亦足立。故父子首足也，昆弟四支也，當使筋骨髓血，動靜足以相勝，長短大小，幹用足以相衞。豈有割脛致腹，取骨肉以增頭，剗背露骨，剝膏腴以裨頷，而謂顱顙魁岸，可得比壽松、晉，喉咽擁腫，必能長生久視哉？漢氏得之微，猶能四百載，魏人失之甚，不滿數十年。爰自晉世，矯枉太過，入列皇朝，非簡賢之授，唯親是貴，無愚智之辨。不能勝衣冠，早據公相之尊，童蒙幼子，遄登槐嶽之位。職應論道，而未離保母之養，續侯賦政，而服二三尺衣。英賢大度，稟彼昏稚，髙才碩儒，恭承藐識。公餗覆而不憂，美錦碎而愈截。兼授若流，迴遷競路，才駑任重，功尠釁多。曉比名於公旦，夕同罪於盜跖，褒稱無位，可以充德，貶退刑轘，不足以塞咎。〔威〕力強濟，聲實隆重，嫌猜畏逼，身受其獘。覆滅分體，若梟仇寇，〔齏〕粉同氣，有過他逆。忠貞之士，橫羅其凶，志節之人，狼狽其禍。閼伯、實沈，繼踵史筆，顯思顯甫，比有國書。趙倫以〔憃〕愚排天，齊攸以賢明謝世，枉鬱殄夷，冤孫就盡，不可勝載矣。豈周、漢之君多孝悌之性，晉、宋之主稟豺狼之情，蓋事勢使之然也。朝行斯術，夕窮崩亂，未能革悛，來事愈甚。蒼生爲此將盡矣，四海爲此構蹙矣！聖帝英君，欲反斯敗，必當更開同姓之國，置不增之約，罷皇胤入宮之禍，守盟牲礪河之篤，乃可還嶮墜之路，反乎全安之轍也。

localRange.text: 及其诛灭，景帝惩之，遂令诸王不得治民，令内史主治民，改丞相曰相，省御史大夫、廷尉、少府、宗正、博士官。武帝改汉内史、中尉、郎中令之名，而王国如故，员职皆朝廷为署，不得自置。至成帝省内史治民，更令相治民，太傅但曰傅。

context.beforeSource: 」至景帝時，呉、楚七國恃其國大，遂以作亂，幾危漢室。
context.afterSource: 中尉一人，比二千石。

manualTranslations.zh: 及其誅滅，景帝懲之，遂令諸王不得治民，令内史主治民，改丞相曰相，省御史大夫、廷尉、少府、宗正、博士官。
manualTranslations.literal: When they were exterminated, Emperor Jing took warning and ordered the kings not to govern the people, ordered interior clerks to govern the people instead, changed the chancellor of state to chancellor, and abolished the posts of censor-in-chief, commandant of justice, privy treasurer, director of the imperial clan, and erudits.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After their defeat Emperor Jing stripped princes of civil authority, transferred rule to imperial clerks, downgraded the chief minister to "chancellor," and eliminated replica ministries such as justice, finance, clan affairs, and the academy.

manualTranslations.zh: 武帝改漢内史、中尉、郎中令之名，前書曰：「改漢内史爲京兆尹，中尉爲執金吾，郎中令爲光祿勳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wu changed the Han names of interior clerk, commandant of the capital, and chamberlain for the palace guard. The Former Book says: "He changed Han interior clerk to metropolitan intendant of Jingzhao, commandant of the capital to commander of the metropolitan guard, and chamberlain for the palace guard to superintendent of the imperial clan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu renamed the kingdom interior clerk, capital commandant, and chamberlain for the guard. The Former Book records: "The Han interior clerk became metropolitan intendant of Jingzhao, the capital commandant became commander of the metropolitan guard, and the chamberlain for the palace guard became superintendent of the imperial clan."

manualTranslations.zh: 而王國如故，員職皆朝廷爲署，不得自置。
manualTranslations.literal: But the kingdoms remained as before; all posts were appointed by the court and could not be self-appointed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet kingdom appointments for every office now came from the center, not the prince.

manualTranslations.zh: 至成帝省内史治民，更令相治民，漢舊儀曰：「大司空何武奏罷内史，相如太守，中尉如都尉，參職。
manualTranslations.literal: By Emperor Cheng the interior clerk who governed the people was abolished and the chancellor was ordered to govern the people instead. Han Old Observances says: "Grand Minister of Works He Wu memorialized to abolish the interior clerk; the chancellor was like a grand administrator, the commandant of the capital like a commandant, sharing duties.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng abolished the kingdom interior clerk and transferred civil government to the chancellor. Han Old Observances records: "Grand Minister of Works He Wu memorialized to abolish the interior clerk; the chancellor was like a grand administrator and the capital commandant like a commandery commandant, sharing duties.

manualTranslations.zh: 是後中尉爭權，與王相奏，常不和也。」
manualTranslations.literal: After this the commandant of the capital struggled for power with the king's chancellor and they often submitted accusations against each other and were constantly at odds."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereafter the capital commandant and the king's chancellor struggled for power and constantly accused one another."

manualTranslations.zh: 太傅但曰傅。
manualTranslations.literal: The grand tutor was simply called tutor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The grand tutor was shortened to "tutor."

manualTranslations.zh: 臣昭曰：觀夫髙祖之創業也，豈直鴻勳碩德，大庇群生，蕩其毒虐，厝之和泰而已哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Chen Zhao says: Observing Gaozu's founding enterprise, was it only great merit and vast virtue, greatly sheltering the living masses, sweeping away cruelty and tyranny, and placing them in harmony and peace?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Zhao writes: Was Gaozu's founding only a matter of great merit, sheltering the people, and restoring peace?

manualTranslations.zh: 至於謀深慮久，封建子弟，蕃維盤固，規謀弘遠。
manualTranslations.literal: As to deep planning and long forethought, enfeoffing sons and younger brothers, making the screen of defense firm and secure—the design was vast and far-reaching.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His deep planning enfeoffed sons and younger brothers to make the defensive screen firm—a design vast and far-reaching.

manualTranslations.zh: 及於三趙不終，燕靈夭絶，齊、代、淮、楚皆爲外重，故宋昌曰「外畏齊、楚、淮南」，斯非效與？
manualTranslations.literal: When the three Zhao lines did not endure, Yan and Ling perished young, and Qi, Dai, Huai, and Chu all became heavy external powers, therefore Song Chang said "outwardly fearing Qi, Chu, and Huainan"—was this not effective?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the three Zhao lines failed, Yan and Ling died young, and Qi, Dai, Huai, and Chu became powerful external domains, Song Chang said "outwardly fearing Qi, Chu, and Huainan"—was that not proof?

manualTranslations.zh: 事過則獘，孰或通之？
manualTranslations.literal: When affairs pass their limit, decay follows—who can fully penetrate this?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When affairs pass their limit, decay follows—who does not see it?

manualTranslations.zh: 全國之難，誠固財物之富，作衞之益，亦旣得之於前矣，故賜以幾杖，用息姦謀。
manualTranslations.literal: The difficulty of preserving a whole state truly lay in the wealth of goods and the benefit of forming guards—this had already been gained before; therefore they were granted cane and staff to quiet treacherous designs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Preserving a whole state required wealth and guards; hence canes and staffs were granted to quiet treacherous designs.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗣隕局下，怨生有以，逮連師構亂，兵交梁闕，禦侮摧寇，肇自密戚。
manualTranslations.literal: When heirs fell in the lower ranks, resentment had its cause; when allied armies stirred rebellion and weapons clashed at the beams and towers of the palace, defense against insult and crushing of invaders began with close kin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When heirs fell and resentment grew, allied armies clashed at the palace gates—defense and rebellion alike began among close kin.

manualTranslations.zh: 景帝遂削蕃國之權，刻骨肉之援，封爲君而不聽治其民，置爲主而稍賤其臣，矯枉過甚，遂臻於此。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Jing then cut the power of frontier kingdoms, carved to the bone the support of flesh and blood, enfeoffed men as lords but did not let them govern their people, made them masters but gradually debased their ministers—correcting the bend went too far and thus reached this point.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing then stripped frontier kingdoms of power, cut flesh-and-blood support, made princes lords without civil rule and masters with debased ministers—overcorrecting until this result.

manualTranslations.zh: 呂、霍之危朝，后族愈貴於來寵，呉、楚之叛奔，侯王恆藉以受誚，故賈誼欲衆建以少其力，列虚以侯其生，此乃達觀深識，監於親陪之要者也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Lü and Huo crises endangered the court; empress clans grew ever more honored through favor; Wu and Chu rebelled and fled; marquises and kings constantly borrowed these to receive reproach; therefore Jia Yi wished to establish many fiefs to diminish their strength and set empty ranks to wait for their birth—this was penetrating vision and deep insight, watching the essentials of close kin and companions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Lü and Huo crises, favored empress clans, and Wu-Chu rebellion brought constant reproach on princes; Jia Yi therefore wished to multiply fiefs to diminish their strength—a penetrating insight into kin politics.

manualTranslations.zh: 冢嗣必傳萬裏之地，分支欲使動搖不得，於經維遠筭，且已礙矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The heir must transmit lands of ten thousand li; collateral branches were to be kept from stirring—yet in long-range planning this already obstructed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The heir must inherit vast lands while collateral lines were kept from stirring—already an obstacle to long-range planning.

manualTranslations.zh: 復哀平之際，劉氏遍於四海，宗正著録，遂以萬數。
manualTranslations.literal: Again at the Ai and Ping period the Liu clan spread across the four seas; the director of the imperial clan's register counted them by the tens of thousands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By the Ai and Ping reigns the Liu clan spread across the realm and the imperial clan register counted them by the tens of thousands.

manualTranslations.zh: 及乎後漢，彌循前跡，光武十子，並列畿外近郡，孝明八國，不能開庇遠民。
manualTranslations.literal: By Later Han they followed the former track still more; Guangwu's ten sons were all placed in near commanderies outside the capital region; Ming's eight kingdoms could not open and shelter distant peoples.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Han followed the same path: Guangwu's ten sons held near domains outside the capital, and Ming's eight kingdoms could not shelter distant peoples.

manualTranslations.zh: 國近則不可以大，不大則不足爲強，此所以本枝之援，終以少固。
manualTranslations.literal: Kingdoms near the center could not be large; if not large they were insufficient to be strong—therefore support from root and branches ultimately remained slight and weak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Near domains could not be large, and without size they could not be strong—so root-and-branch support remained slight.

manualTranslations.zh: 若使漢分兩越置二三親國，剖呉、楚樹數四列蕃，割遼海而分皇枝，開隴蜀而王子弟，使主尊顯，依漢初之貴，民無定限，許滋養之富；
manualTranslations.literal: If Han had divided the two Yue regions and placed two or three close kin kingdoms, carved Wu and Chu and planted several rows of four frontier screens, cut Liaohai and divided royal branches, opened Long and Shu and enfeoffed sons and younger brothers, making lords honored and eminent according to early Han nobility, with no fixed limit on people and allowing nourishing wealth;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Han had divided the two Yue regions into close kin kingdoms, carved Wu and Chu into several frontier screens, split Liaohai and Long-Shu among royal branches, and allowed lords the early Han honor and unlimited people to nourish wealth;

manualTranslations.zh: 若有昏虐之嗣，可得廢而不得削，必傳劉氏。
manualTranslations.literal: if there were brutal and tyrannical heirs, they could be deposed but not reduced, and the Liu line must be transmitted;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if brutal heirs appeared they could be deposed but not reduced, and the Liu line would endure;

manualTranslations.zh: 民信所奉，發其侵伐兼幷之釁，峻其他族篡殺之科，制其入貢輕重之法，疎其來朝往復之數。
manualTranslations.literal: the people would trust whom they served; signs of invasion, attack, and merger would be exposed; penalties for other clans' usurpation and murder would be severe; methods for regulating tribute weight would be set; and the number of visits to court would be spaced.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the people would trust their lords; signs of aggression would be exposed; usurpation by other clans would be severely punished; tribute and court visits would be regulated;

manualTranslations.zh: 君君臣臣，永許百世之期，一國之民，長無遷動之志，四方得志，聽離官列封，懷賢抱智，隨所適樂土。
manualTranslations.literal: lord and minister, lord and minister, would be granted a covenant for a hundred generations; the people of one state would long have no will to migrate; the four quarters achieving their aims would be allowed to leave office and receive enfeoffment; cherishing worth and embracing wisdom, each would go where pleased to a happy land.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: lord and minister would covenant for a hundred generations; a state's people would not migrate; the talented would go where they pleased;

manualTranslations.zh: 強弱相侔，遠近相摧，舉其大歸，略其小滯，與其畫一，班之海内。
manualTranslations.literal: Strong and weak would balance one another, far and near would check one another; taking the great principle and omitting small hindrances, granting each its measure, this would be distributed within the seas.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: strong and weak would balance, far and near would check one another; taking the great principle and distributing it within the seas;

manualTranslations.zh: 天子之朝，自非異姓僭奪，不得興勤王之師。
manualTranslations.literal: at the Son of Heaven's court, unless there were usurpation by another surname, no army to rescue the king could be raised.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the court would raise no rescue army unless another surname usurped the throne;

manualTranslations.zh: 諸蕃國，自非雜互篡主，不降討伐之詔。
manualTranslations.literal: among all frontier kingdoms, unless there were mixed usurpation of lords, no decree of punitive campaign would be issued.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: frontier kingdoms would receive no punitive decree unless lords usurped one another;

manualTranslations.zh: 犬牙相經，共爲嚴國，雖王莽善盜，將何因而敢竊，曹操雄勇，亦安能以得士。
manualTranslations.literal: interlocking like dogs' teeth, together forming a stern realm—even if Wang Mang were skilled at theft, by what means could he dare to seize; even if Cao Cao were fierce and brave, how could he win men by force.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: interlocking like dogs' teeth into a stern realm—even Wang Mang could not steal the throne, nor Cao Cao win men by force.

manualTranslations.zh: 斯無俟極聖然克行，明賢粗識亦足立。
manualTranslations.literal: This need not wait for the utmost sage to accomplish; a clear worthy with rough understanding would suffice to establish it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This need not wait for the utmost sage; a clear worthy with rough understanding could establish it.

manualTranslations.zh: 故父子首足也，昆弟四支也，當使筋骨髓血，動靜足以相勝，長短大小，幹用足以相衞。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore father and son are head and foot; elder and younger brothers are the four limbs; sinew, bone, marrow, and blood in movement and stillness should suffice to overcome one another; long and short, large and small, trunk and use should suffice to guard one another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Father and son are head and foot; brothers are the four limbs; sinew, bone, marrow, and blood should balance movement and stillness and guard one another.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈有割脛致腹，取骨肉以增頭，剗背露骨，剝膏腴以裨頷，而謂顱顙魁岸，可得比壽松、晉，喉咽擁腫，必能長生久視哉？
manualTranslations.literal: How could one cut the shank to enlarge the belly, take flesh and bone to add to the head, scrape the back to expose bone, strip rich fat to pad the jaw, and then say the skull and brow are lofty and massive, comparable to the longevity of pine and Jin, or that a swollen throat and neck must assure long life and far sight?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Who cuts the shank to enlarge the belly, strips the back to pad the jaw, and then claims a lofty brow like the pine of longevity or a swollen throat that assures long life?

manualTranslations.zh: 漢氏得之微，猶能四百載，魏人失之甚，不滿數十年。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han house gained it slightly and still endured four hundred years; Wei men lost it greatly and did not last several decades.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han gained it slightly and endured four hundred years; Wei lost it greatly and did not last decades.

manualTranslations.zh: 爰自晉世，矯枉太過，入列皇朝，非簡賢之授，唯親是貴，無愚智之辨。
manualTranslations.literal: From the Jin age onward, correcting the bend went too far; entering the ranks of the imperial clan was not appointment by selecting the worthy—only kin was honored, with no distinction between foolish and wise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Jin onward overcorrection made imperial rank honor kin alone, with no distinction between foolish and wise.

manualTranslations.zh: 不能勝衣冠，早據公相之尊，童蒙幼子，遄登槐嶽之位。
manualTranslations.literal: Unable to surpass ordinary officials in dress, they early occupied the honor of excellencies and chancellors; infant children swiftly ascended posts on the locust-and-catalpa terrace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Unable to surpass ordinary officials, infant children swiftly occupied excellencies and chancellorships.

manualTranslations.zh: 職應論道，而未離保母之養，續侯賦政，而服二三尺衣。
manualTranslations.literal: Their duties should have been to discourse on the Way, yet they had not left the nurse's care; continuing as marquises and administering government, they still wore clothes of two or three feet.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They should discourse on the Way yet had not left the nurse's care; they governed yet still wore child's clothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 英賢大度，稟彼昏稚，髙才碩儒，恭承藐識。
manualTranslations.literal: Heroic worthies of broad mind received instruction from those childish and young; men of high talent and great learning respectfully served their slight understanding.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heroic worthies received instruction from the childish; great scholars respectfully served slight understanding.

manualTranslations.zh: 公餗覆而不憂，美錦碎而愈截。
manualTranslations.literal: The public cauldron was overturned without worry; fine brocade was shattered and cut still more.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The public cauldron was overturned without worry; fine brocade was shattered and cut still more.

manualTranslations.zh: 兼授若流，迴遷競路，才駑任重，功尠釁多。
manualTranslations.literal: Concurrent appointments flowed like a stream; roundabout transfers competed on the road; talent was dull yet burden heavy; achievement slight yet fault many.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Concurrent appointments flowed endlessly; talent was dull yet burdens heavy; achievement slight yet faults many.

manualTranslations.zh: 曉比名於公旦，夕同罪於盜跖，褒稱無位，可以充德，貶退刑轘，不足以塞咎。
manualTranslations.literal: In the morning compared in name to the Duke of Zhou; by evening sharing guilt with Robber Zhi; praise without rank could fill virtue; demotion and execution by quartering could not suffice to cover fault.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Praised in the morning as the Duke of Zhou and condemned by evening as Robber Zhi; praise without rank could not fill virtue, nor execution cover fault.

manualTranslations.zh: 〔威〕力強濟，聲實隆重，嫌猜畏逼，身受其獘。
manualTranslations.literal: [Power] was forcibly propped up; reputation and substance were weighty; suspicion and fear pressed hard; they personally suffered decay.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Power was forcibly propped up; reputation was weighty; suspicion pressed hard; they personally suffered ruin.

manualTranslations.zh: 覆滅分體，若梟仇寇，〔齏〕粉同氣，有過他逆。
manualTranslations.literal: Overthrow and extinction split the body, like displaying a foe as an owl; [pulverizing] flesh of the same breath exceeded other rebellions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Overthrow split the body like displaying a foe; pulverizing kin exceeded other rebellions.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠貞之士，橫羅其凶，志節之人，狼狽其禍。
manualTranslations.literal: Loyal and steadfast men were swept into their calamity; men of resolve and integrity were battered by their disaster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Loyal men were swept into calamity; men of resolve were battered by disaster.

manualTranslations.zh: 閼伯、實沈，繼踵史筆，顯思顯甫，比有國書。
manualTranslations.literal: Quebo and Shichen followed one after another in the historians' brush; Xian Si and Xian Fu were compared in state documents.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Quebo and Shichen followed in the historians' brush; Xian Si and Xian Fu appeared in state documents.

manualTranslations.zh: 趙倫以〔憃〕愚排天，齊攸以賢明謝世，枉鬱殄夷，冤孫就盡，不可勝載矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao Lun with [foolish] stupidity overturned Heaven; Qi You with worthy clarity departed the world; wrongful oppression exterminated and destroyed; innocent descendants were exhausted—too many to record.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao Lun with foolish stupidity overturned Heaven; Qi You with worthy clarity departed the world; wrongful oppression destroyed innocent descendants beyond counting.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈周、漢之君多孝悌之性，晉、宋之主稟豺狼之情，蓋事勢使之然也。
manualTranslations.literal: Were Zhou and Han rulers mostly endowed with filial and brotherly nature, while Jin and Song lords possessed wolfish feeling? It was circumstance that made it so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Were Zhou and Han rulers more filial while Jin and Song lords were wolfish? Circumstance made it so.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝行斯術，夕窮崩亂，未能革悛，來事愈甚。
manualTranslations.literal: Practicing this method in the morning, by evening they reached collapse and disorder; unable to reform and repent, later affairs grew worse still.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Practicing this in the morning, by evening came collapse; unable to reform, later affairs grew worse.

manualTranslations.zh: 蒼生爲此將盡矣，四海爲此構蹙矣！
manualTranslations.literal: The living masses for this will nearly be exhausted; the four seas for this are wrung with distress!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The living masses will nearly be exhausted; the four seas are wrung with distress!

manualTranslations.zh: 聖帝英君，欲反斯敗，必當更開同姓之國，置不增之約，罷皇胤入宮之禍，守盟牲礪河之篤，乃可還嶮墜之路，反乎全安之轍也。
manualTranslations.literal: Sage emperors and heroic rulers wishing to reverse this failure must reopen kingdoms of the same surname, establish covenants not to enlarge them, abolish the disaster of imperial descendants entering the palace, keep the solemnity of covenant victims and sharpening the river, and only then can they return from the precipitous falling path and turn back to the track of complete security.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sage rulers wishing to reverse this failure must reopen same-surname kingdoms, covenant not to enlarge them, end the disaster of imperial descendants in the palace, and keep solemn covenants—only then can they return to complete security.

sourceRange.text: 古今注曰：「常以春分行部，郡國各遣一吏迎界上。」諸書不同也。

context.beforeSource: 孝武帝初置刺史十三人，秩六百石。
context.afterSource: 成帝更爲牧，秩二千石。
context.beforeLocal: 孝武帝初置刺史十三人，秩六百石。
context.afterLocal: 成帝更为牧，秩二千石。

sourceRange.text: 中興以來，食邑千戸已上置家丞、庶子各一人，不滿千戸不置家丞，又悉省行人、洗馬、門大夫。關内侯，如淳曰：「列侯出關就國，侯但爵身，其有家累者與之關内之邑，食其租稅也。」古今注曰：「建武六年，初令關内侯食邑者俸月二十五斛。」承秦賜爵十九等，爲關内侯，無土，寄食在所縣，民租多少，各有戸數爲限。荀綽晉百官表注曰：「時六國未平，將帥皆家關中，故以爲號。」劉劭爵制曰：「春秋傳有庶長鮑。商君爲政，備其法品爲十八級，合關内侯、列侯凡二十等，其制因古義。古者天子寄軍政於六卿，居則以田，警則以戰，所謂入使治之，出使長之，素信者與衆相得也。故啓伐有扈，乃召六卿，大夫之在軍爲將者也。及周之六卿，亦以居軍，在國也則以比長、閭胥、族師、黨正、州長、卿大夫爲稱，其在軍也則以卒伍、司馬、將軍爲號，所以異在國之名也。秦依古制，其在軍賜爵爲等級，其帥人皆更卒也，有功賜爵，則在軍吏之例。自一爵以上至不更四等，皆士也。大夫以上至五大夫五等，比大夫也。九等，依九命之義也。自左庶長以上至大庶長，九卿之義也。關内侯者，依古圻内子男之義也。秦都山西，以關内爲王畿，故曰關内侯也。列侯者，依古列國諸侯之義也。然則卿大夫士下之品，皆放古，比朝之制而異其名，亦所以殊軍國也。古者以車戰，兵車一乘，歩卒七十二人，分翼左右。車，大夫在左，御者處中，勇士居右，凡七十五人。一爵曰公士者，歩卒之有爵爲公士者。二爵曰上造。造，成也。古者成士昇於司徒曰造士，雖依此名，皆歩卒也。三爵曰簪褭，御駟馬者。要褭，古之名馬也。駕駟馬者其形似簪，故曰簪褭也。四爵曰不更。不更者，爲車右，不復與凡更卒同也。五爵曰大夫。大夫者，在車左者也。六爵爲官大夫，七爵爲公大夫，八爵爲公乘，九爵爲五大夫，皆軍吏也。吏民爵不得過公乘者，得貰與子若同産。然則公乘者，軍吏之爵髙者也。雖非臨戰，得公卒車，故曰公乘也。十爵爲左庶長，十一爵爲右庶長，十二爵爲左更，十三爵爲中更，十四爵爲右更，十五爵爲少上造，十六爵爲大上造，十七爵爲駟車庶長，十八爵爲大庶長，十九爵爲關内侯，二十爵爲列侯。自左庶長已上至大庶長，皆卿大夫，皆軍將也。所將皆庶人、更卒也，故以庶更爲名。大庶長卽大將軍也，左右庶長卽左右偏裨將軍也。」古今注曰：「成帝鴻嘉三年，令吏民得買爵，級千錢。

localRange.text: 中兴以来，食邑千户已上置家丞、庶子各一人，不满千户不置家丞，又悉省行人、洗马、门大夫。关内侯，承秦赐爵十九等，为关内侯，无土，寄食在所县，民租多少，各有户数为限。

context.beforeSource: 列侯舊有行人、洗馬、門大夫，凡五官。
context.afterSource: 」四夷國王，率衆王，歸義侯，邑君，邑長，皆有丞，比郡、縣。
