manualTranslations.zh: 中興以來，食邑千戸已上置家丞、庶子各一人，不滿千戸不置家丞，又悉省行人、洗馬、門大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: Since the restoration, for feoffs of one thousand households or more they placed one household aide and one junior son-of-the-house; below one thousand households they did not place a household aide, and they abolished heralds, horse washers, and gate grandees entirely.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the restoration, marquises with at least one thousand feoffed households retained an aide and a junior steward; smaller feoffs lost the household aide, and heralds, washers, and gate grandees were cut altogether.

manualTranslations.zh: 關内侯，如淳曰：「列侯出關就國，侯但爵身，其有家累者與之關内之邑，食其租稅也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Marquis-within-the-passes: Ru Chun says: "When full marquises left the passes to go to their states, the marquis kept only the title in person; those with household dependents were given towns within the passes to eat their rent and tax."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Marquis-within-the-passes: Ru Chun explains: "When full marquises left the passes for their states, the title alone went with the holder; dependents were given towns within the passes to draw rent and tax."

manualTranslations.zh: 古今注曰：「建武六年，初令關内侯食邑者俸月二十五斛。」
manualTranslations.literal: Notes Ancient and Modern say: "In the sixth year of Jianwu they first ordered that marquises-within-the-passes with food feoffs receive twenty-five hu stipend per month."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Notes Ancient and Modern record: "In Jianwu 6 marquises-within-the-passes with food feoffs were first granted twenty-five hu monthly."

manualTranslations.zh: 承秦賜爵十九等，爲關内侯，無土，寄食在所縣，民租多少，各有戸數爲限。
manualTranslations.literal: Continuing the Qin nineteenth rank of ennoblement, they were marquises-within-the-passes; they had no land but lodged grain income in the county where they resided; the people's rent, more or less, was limited according to household numbers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Marquises-within-the-passes inherited the Qin nineteenth-grade title: they held no land but drew allowance charged against a host county, with yields prorated to registered households.

manualTranslations.zh: 荀綽晉百官表注曰：「時六國未平，將帥皆家關中，故以爲號。」
manualTranslations.literal: Xun Chuo's Annotated Jin Table of Officials says: "At that time the six states were not yet pacified; generals and commanders all had homes in Guanzhong, therefore this title was used."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo's Annotated Jin Table of Officials notes: "While the six states were still unconquered, commanders were domiciled in Guanzhong, hence the title."

manualTranslations.zh: 劉劭爵制曰：「春秋傳有庶長鮑。
manualTranslations.literal: Liu Shao's Treatise on Ranks says: "The Spring and Autumn Annals mention Chief-of-the-Line Bao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Shao's Treatise on Ranks begins: "The Spring and Autumn Annals mention Chief-of-the-Line Bao.

manualTranslations.zh: 商君爲政，備其法品爲十八級，合關内侯、列侯凡二十等，其制因古義。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Lord of Shang governed, he completed the legal grades as eighteen ranks; together with marquis-within-the-passes and full marquis there were twenty ranks in all; the system followed ancient meaning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Lord of Shang established eighteen grades; with marquis-within-the-passes and full marquis there were twenty ranks in all, following ancient principle.

manualTranslations.zh: 古者天子寄軍政於六卿，居則以田，警則以戰，所謂入使治之，出使長之，素信者與衆相得也。
manualTranslations.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven entrusted military government to the six ministers: in peace they farmed; in alarm they fought—what is called entering to govern them and going out to lead them; trusted men matched the multitude.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Son of Heaven entrusted military affairs to the six ministers: in peace they farmed, in alarm they fought—trusted men leading the multitude.

manualTranslations.zh: 故啓伐有扈，乃召六卿，大夫之在軍爲將者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore when Qi attacked Youhu he summoned the six ministers; grandees in the army served as generals.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Qi attacked Youhu he summoned the six ministers; grandees in the army served as generals.

manualTranslations.zh: 及周之六卿，亦以居軍，在國也則以比長、閭胥、族師、黨正、州長、卿大夫爲稱，其在軍也則以卒伍、司馬、將軍爲號，所以異在國之名也。
manualTranslations.literal: By Zhou's six ministers as well, they dwelt in the army; in the state they were called neighborhood chief, lane clerk, clan instructor, ward rectifier, district chief, and minister-grandee; in the army they were called squad, company, marshal, and general—therefore names in the state differed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhou's six ministers likewise served in camp; in the state they bore civil titles, in the army military titles—hence the names differed.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦依古制，其在軍賜爵爲等級，其帥人皆更卒也，有功賜爵，則在軍吏之例。
manualTranslations.literal: Qin followed the ancient system: in the army ennoblement was granted as grades; those who led men were all corvée soldiers; when merit ennobled them, they fell under the category of army officers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qin followed antiquity: army ranks were granted in grades; leaders were corvée soldiers; merit ennoblement made them army officers.

manualTranslations.zh: 自一爵以上至不更四等，皆士也。
manualTranslations.literal: From the first rank upward to the fourth rank, Not Replaced, all were shi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From the first rank through the fourth, Not Replaced, all were common soldiers.

manualTranslations.zh: 大夫以上至五大夫五等，比大夫也。
manualTranslations.literal: From grandee upward through the five ranks to Grand Grandee, they were comparable to grandees.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From grandee through the five ranks to Grand Grandee, they were comparable to grandees.

manualTranslations.zh: 九等，依九命之義也。
manualTranslations.literal: The nine ranks followed the meaning of the nine commands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The nine ranks followed the meaning of the nine commands.

manualTranslations.zh: 自左庶長以上至大庶長，九卿之義也。
manualTranslations.literal: From Left Chief-of-the-Line upward to Great Chief-of-the-Line followed the meaning of the nine ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Left Chief-of-the-Line to Great Chief-of-the-Line followed the meaning of the nine ministers.

manualTranslations.zh: 關内侯者，依古圻内子男之義也。
manualTranslations.literal: Marquis-within-the-passes followed the ancient meaning of viscounts and barons within the royal domain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Marquis-within-the-passes followed the ancient meaning of viscounts and barons within the royal domain.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦都山西，以關内爲王畿，故曰關内侯也。
manualTranslations.literal: Qin made its capital west of the mountains and took the area within the passes as the royal domain; therefore they were called marquises-within-the-passes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qin's capital lay west of the mountains with Guanzhong as the royal domain; hence the title marquis-within-the-passes.

manualTranslations.zh: 列侯者，依古列國諸侯之義也。
manualTranslations.literal: Full marquises followed the ancient meaning of feudal lords of ranked states.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Full marquises followed the ancient meaning of feudal lords of ranked states.

manualTranslations.zh: 然則卿大夫士下之品，皆放古，比朝之制而異其名，亦所以殊軍國也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the grades below ministers, grandees, and shi all imitated antiquity, comparing court institutions while differing in name—this too distinguished army and state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus the lower grades imitated antiquity, matching court institutions under different names to distinguish army and state.

manualTranslations.zh: 古者以車戰，兵車一乘，歩卒七十二人，分翼左右。
manualTranslations.literal: In antiquity they fought with chariots; one war chariot had seventy-two foot soldiers, divided to flank left and right.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In antiquity one war chariot carried seventy-two foot soldiers flanking left and right.

manualTranslations.zh: 車，大夫在左，御者處中，勇士居右，凡七十五人。
manualTranslations.literal: On the chariot the grandee was on the left, the driver in the center, and the brave warrior on the right—seventy-five men in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the chariot the grandee stood left, the driver center, the warrior right—seventy-five men in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 一爵曰公士者，歩卒之有爵爲公士者。
manualTranslations.literal: The first rank, called Public Warrior, was a foot soldier who had rank as Public Warrior.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The first rank, Public Warrior, was a ranked foot soldier.

manualTranslations.zh: 二爵曰上造。
manualTranslations.literal: The second rank was Upper Accomplished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The second rank was Upper Accomplished.

manualTranslations.zh: 造，成也。
manualTranslations.literal: Accomplished means completed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Accomplished means completed.

manualTranslations.zh: 古者成士昇於司徒曰造士，雖依此名，皆歩卒也。
manualTranslations.literal: In antiquity accomplished shi who ascended to the minister of education were called Accomplished Shi; though this name was borrowed, all were foot soldiers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In antiquity accomplished shi presented to the minister of education were called Accomplished Shi; though the name was borrowed, all were foot soldiers.

manualTranslations.zh: 三爵曰簪褭，御駟馬者。
manualTranslations.literal: The third rank was Hairpin Steed, driver of the four-horse team.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The third rank, Hairpin Steed, drove the four-horse team.

manualTranslations.zh: 要褭，古之名馬也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yaoniao was an ancient famous horse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yaoniao was an ancient famous horse.

manualTranslations.zh: 駕駟馬者其形似簪，故曰簪褭也。
manualTranslations.literal: The driver of the four-horse team resembled a hairpin in form; therefore it was called Hairpin Steed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The four-horse driver resembled a hairpin; hence Hairpin Steed.

manualTranslations.zh: 四爵曰不更。
manualTranslations.literal: The fourth rank was Not Replaced.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The fourth rank was Not Replaced.

manualTranslations.zh: 不更者，爲車右，不復與凡更卒同也。
manualTranslations.literal: Not Replaced meant serving as chariot right; one no longer shared duties with ordinary corvée soldiers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Not Replaced meant chariot right, no longer sharing duties with ordinary corvée soldiers.

manualTranslations.zh: 五爵曰大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: The fifth rank was grandee.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The fifth rank was grandee.

manualTranslations.zh: 大夫者，在車左者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Grandee meant the one on the left of the chariot.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grandee meant the one on the left of the chariot.

manualTranslations.zh: 六爵爲官大夫，七爵爲公大夫，八爵爲公乘，九爵爲五大夫，皆軍吏也。
manualTranslations.literal: The sixth rank was Officer Grandee, the seventh Public Grandee, the eighth Public Chariot, the ninth Grand Grandee—all army officers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sixth through ninth ranks—Officer Grandee, Public Grandee, Public Chariot, and Grand Grandee—were all army officers.

manualTranslations.zh: 吏民爵不得過公乘者，得貰與子若同産。
manualTranslations.literal: Commoners whose rank could not exceed Public Chariot might transfer it to a son or same-birth kin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commoners capped at Public Chariot could transfer rank to a son or same-birth kin.

manualTranslations.zh: 然則公乘者，軍吏之爵髙者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus Public Chariot was a high rank among army officers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus Public Chariot was a high rank among army officers.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖非臨戰，得公卒車，故曰公乘也。
manualTranslations.literal: Though not in battle, one could obtain a public soldier's chariot; therefore it was called Public Chariot.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though not in battle one could obtain a public soldier's chariot; hence Public Chariot.

manualTranslations.zh: 十爵爲左庶長，十一爵爲右庶長，十二爵爲左更，十三爵爲中更，十四爵爲右更，十五爵爲少上造，十六爵爲大上造，十七爵爲駟車庶長，十八爵爲大庶長，十九爵爲關内侯，二十爵爲列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: The tenth rank was Left Chief-of-the-Line, the eleventh Right Chief-of-the-Line, the twelfth Left Renewer, the thirteenth Central Renewer, the fourteenth Right Renewer, the fifteenth Lesser Upper Accomplished, the sixteenth Greater Upper Accomplished, the seventeenth Four-Chariot Chief-of-the-Line, the eighteenth Great Chief-of-the-Line, the nineteenth marquis-within-the-passes, the twentieth full marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ranks ten through twenty ran from Left Chief-of-the-Line through Right Renewer, Lesser and Greater Upper Accomplished, Four-Chariot and Great Chief-of-the-Line, marquis-within-the-passes, and full marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 自左庶長已上至大庶長，皆卿大夫，皆軍將也。
manualTranslations.literal: From Left Chief-of-the-Line upward to Great Chief-of-the-Line, all were ministers and grandees, all army generals.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Left Chief-of-the-Line to Great Chief-of-the-Line all were ministers and grandees, all army generals.

manualTranslations.zh: 所將皆庶人、更卒也，故以庶更爲名。
manualTranslations.literal: Those they led were all commoners and corvée soldiers; therefore the names used commoner and renewer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those they led were commoners and corvée soldiers; hence the names commoner and renewer.

manualTranslations.zh: 大庶長卽大將軍也，左右庶長卽左右偏裨將軍也。」

sourceRange.text: 太公陰符曰：「武王問太公：『願聞治亂之要。』太公曰：『其本在吏。』武王曰：『吏者治也，所以爲治，其亂者何？』太公曰：『故吏重罪有十。』武王問『吏之重罪。』太公曰；『一、吏苛刻；二、吏不平；三、吏貪汚；四、吏以威力迫脅於民；五、吏與史合姦；六、吏與人亡情；七、吏作盜賊，使人爲耳目；八、吏賤買賣貴於民；九、吏增易於民；十、吏振懼於民。夫治者有三罪，則國亂而民愁；盡有之，則民流亡而君失其國。』武王曰：『民亦有罪乎？』太公曰：『民有十大於此，除者則國治而民安。』武王曰：『十大何如？』太公曰：『民勝吏，厚大臣，一大也。民宗強，侵陵群下，二大也。民甚富，傾國家，三大也。民尊親其君，天下歸慕，四大也。衆暴寡，五大也。民有百里之譽，千里之交，六大也。民以吏威爲權，七大也。恩行於吏，八大也。民服信，以少爲多，奪人田宅，贅人妻於，九大也。民之基業畜産爲人所苦，十大也。所謂一家害一里，一里害諸侯，諸侯害天下。』武王曰：『絶吏之罪，塞民之大，奈何？』太公曰：『察民之暴吏，明其賞，審其誅，則吏不敢犯罪，民不敢大也。』武王曰：『是民吏相伺，上下不和而結其讎。』太公曰：『爲君守成，爲吏守職，爲民守事。如此，各居其道則國治，國治則都治，都治則里治，里治則家治，家治則善惡分明，善惡分明則國無事，國無事則吏民外不懷怨，内不徼事。』」其郡有鹽官、鐵官、工官、都水官者，隨事廣狹置令、長及丞，秩次皆如縣、道，無分士，給均本吏。本注曰：凡郡縣出鹽多者置鹽官，主鹽稅。出鐵多者置鐵官，主鼓鑄。胡廣曰：「鹽官掊坑而得鹽，或有鑿井煮海水而以得之者。鑄銅爲器械，當鑄冶之時，扇熾其火，謂之鼓鑄。」有工多者置工官，主工稅物。有水池及魚利多者置水官，主平水收漁稅。

manualTranslations.zh: 太公陰符曰：「武王問太公：『願聞治亂之要。』
manualTranslations.literal: Taigong's Secret Tallies says: "King Wu asked Taigong: 'I wish to hear the essentials of order and disorder.'"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taigong's Secret Tallies records: "King Wu asked Taigong: 'I wish to hear the essentials of order and disorder.'"

manualTranslations.zh: 太公曰：『其本在吏。』
manualTranslations.literal: Taigong said: 'Its root lies in officials.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'Its root lies in officials.'

manualTranslations.zh: 武王曰：『吏者治也，所以爲治，其亂者何？』
manualTranslations.literal: King Wu said: 'Official means governance; they are what bring order—what brings disorder?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Wu said: 'Official means governance; they bring order—what brings disorder?'

manualTranslations.zh: 太公曰：『故吏重罪有十。』
manualTranslations.literal: Taigong said: 'Therefore officials have ten heavy crimes.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'Therefore officials have ten heavy crimes.'

manualTranslations.zh: 武王問『吏之重罪。』
manualTranslations.literal: King Wu asked about 'the officials' heavy crimes.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Wu asked about 'the officials' heavy crimes.'

manualTranslations.zh: 太公曰；
manualTranslations.literal: Taigong said;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taigong said;

manualTranslations.zh: 『一、吏苛刻；
manualTranslations.literal: 'First, officials are harsh and severe;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 'First, officials are harsh and severe;

manualTranslations.zh: 二、吏不平；
manualTranslations.literal: second, officials are unfair;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: second, officials are unfair;

manualTranslations.zh: 三、吏貪汚；
manualTranslations.literal: third, officials are greedy and corrupt;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: third, officials are greedy and corrupt;

manualTranslations.zh: 四、吏以威力迫脅於民；
manualTranslations.literal: fourth, officials use power and might to coerce the people;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: fourth, officials use power to coerce the people;

manualTranslations.zh: 五、吏與史合姦；
manualTranslations.literal: fifth, officials conspire with clerks;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: fifth, officials conspire with clerks;

manualTranslations.zh: 六、吏與人亡情；
manualTranslations.literal: sixth, officials are heartless toward people;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: sixth, officials are heartless toward people;

manualTranslations.zh: 七、吏作盜賊，使人爲耳目；
manualTranslations.literal: seventh, officials act as bandits and make men their eyes and ears;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: seventh, officials act as bandits and use men as spies;

manualTranslations.zh: 八、吏賤買賣貴於民；
manualTranslations.literal: eighth, officials buy cheap and sell dear to the people;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: eighth, officials buy cheap and sell dear to the people;

manualTranslations.zh: 九、吏增易於民；
manualTranslations.literal: ninth, officials alter and change accounts against the people;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: ninth, officials falsify accounts against the people;

manualTranslations.zh: 十、吏振懼於民。
manualTranslations.literal: tenth, officials terrify the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: tenth, officials terrify the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫治者有三罪，則國亂而民愁；
manualTranslations.literal: When rulers have three crimes, the state is disordered and the people grieved;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When rulers commit three crimes, the state is disordered and the people grieved;

manualTranslations.zh: 盡有之，則民流亡而君失其國。』
manualTranslations.literal: when they have all of them, the people flee and the ruler loses his state.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they have all of them, the people flee and the ruler loses his state.'

manualTranslations.zh: 武王曰：『民亦有罪乎？』
manualTranslations.literal: King Wu said: 'Do the people also have crimes?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Wu said: 'Do the people also have crimes?'

manualTranslations.zh: 太公曰：『民有十大於此，除者則國治而民安。』
manualTranslations.literal: Taigong said: 'The people have ten greater than these; remove them and the state is governed and the people secure.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'The people have ten greater than these; remove them and the state is governed and the people secure.'

manualTranslations.zh: 武王曰：『十大何如？』
manualTranslations.literal: King Wu said: 'What are the ten great ones like?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Wu said: 'What are the ten great ones?'

manualTranslations.zh: 太公曰：『民勝吏，厚大臣，一大也。
manualTranslations.literal: Taigong said: 'The people overcome officials and enrich great ministers—one great crime.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'The people overcome officials and enrich great ministers—the first great crime.

manualTranslations.zh: 民宗強，侵陵群下，二大也。
manualTranslations.literal: The people honor the strong and encroach upon subordinates—two great crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people honor the strong and encroach upon subordinates—the second.

manualTranslations.zh: 民甚富，傾國家，三大也。
manualTranslations.literal: The people are very rich and overturn the state—three great crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people grow very rich and overturn the state—the third.

manualTranslations.zh: 民尊親其君，天下歸慕，四大也。
manualTranslations.literal: The people honor and cherish their lord and all under Heaven turns in admiration—four great crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people honor their lord and all under Heaven turns in admiration—the fourth.

manualTranslations.zh: 衆暴寡，五大也。
manualTranslations.literal: The many oppress the few—five great crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The many oppress the few—the fifth.

manualTranslations.zh: 民有百里之譽，千里之交，六大也。
manualTranslations.literal: The people have fame for a hundred li and alliances for a thousand li—six great crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people win fame for a hundred li and alliances for a thousand li—the sixth.

manualTranslations.zh: 民以吏威爲權，七大也。
manualTranslations.literal: The people take officials' authority as power—seven great crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people treat officials' authority as power—the seventh.

manualTranslations.zh: 恩行於吏，八大也。
manualTranslations.literal: Favor flows through officials—eight great crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Favor flows through officials—the eighth.

manualTranslations.zh: 民服信，以少爲多，奪人田宅，贅人妻於，九大也。
manualTranslations.literal: The people are compliant and trusting, making few into many, seizing others' fields and dwellings, and taking others' wives in marriage—nine great crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people are compliant, inflate numbers, seize fields and dwellings, and take others' wives—the ninth.

manualTranslations.zh: 民之基業畜産爲人所苦，十大也。
manualTranslations.literal: The people's foundations, estates, and livestock are harmed by others—ten great crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people's foundations, estates, and livestock are harmed by others—the tenth.

manualTranslations.zh: 所謂一家害一里，一里害諸侯，諸侯害天下。』
manualTranslations.literal: This is what is called one household harming one ward, one ward harming feudal lords, feudal lords harming all under Heaven.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is what is called one household harming one ward, one ward harming feudal lords, feudal lords harming all under Heaven.'

manualTranslations.zh: 武王曰：『絶吏之罪，塞民之大，奈何？』
manualTranslations.literal: King Wu said: 'How can one cut off officials' crimes and block the people's great crimes?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Wu said: 'How can one cut off officials' crimes and block the people's great crimes?'

manualTranslations.zh: 太公曰：『察民之暴吏，明其賞，審其誅，則吏不敢犯罪，民不敢大也。』
manualTranslations.literal: Taigong said: 'Investigate violent officials among the people, clarify rewards, examine punishments, and officials will not dare to commit crimes and the people will not dare their great crimes.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'Investigate violent officials, clarify rewards, examine punishments, and officials will not dare crime nor the people their great crimes.'

manualTranslations.zh: 武王曰：『是民吏相伺，上下不和而結其讎。』
manualTranslations.literal: King Wu said: 'This means people and officials spy on each other, above and below are not harmonious, and they form grudges.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Wu said: 'Then people and officials spy on each other, above and below fall out, and grudges form.'

manualTranslations.zh: 太公曰：『爲君守成，爲吏守職，爲民守事。
manualTranslations.literal: Taigong said: 'Let the ruler guard accomplishment, let officials guard their duties, let the people guard their tasks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'Let the ruler guard accomplishment, officials guard their duties, and the people guard their tasks.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此，各居其道則國治，國治則都治，都治則里治，里治則家治，家治則善惡分明，善惡分明則國無事，國無事則吏民外不懷怨，内不徼事。』」
manualTranslations.literal: Thus, each keeping to his path, the state is governed; when the state is governed the metropolis is governed; when the metropolis is governed the ward is governed; when the ward is governed the household is governed; when the household is governed good and evil are distinguished; when good and evil are distinguished the state has no affairs; when the state has no affairs officials and people outwardly harbor no resentment and inwardly seek no improper gain.'"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus each keeps to his path: the state is governed, then the metropolis, ward, and household; good and evil are distinguished, the state has no affairs, and officials and people harbor no outward resentment or inward scheming.'"

manualTranslations.literal: In commanderies that had salt offices, iron offices, craft offices, or capital-construction water offices, according to the size of the task they placed magistrates, chiefs, and assistants; the salary grades were all like counties and circuits; there was no separate territorial jurisdiction; clerks were supplied evenly from the regular establishment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commanderies rich in salt, iron, crafts, or waterworks set magistrates, chiefs, and assistants scaled to the workload, paid like county officials, without an independent territory, drawing clerks from the standard pool.

manualTranslations.zh: 本注曰：凡郡縣出鹽多者置鹽官，主鹽稅。

manualTranslations.zh: 鑄銅爲器械，當鑄冶之時，扇熾其火，謂之鼓鑄。」

manualTranslations.zh: 有工多者置工官，主工稅物。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Industrial centers added craft bureaus to tax manufactures.

manualTranslations.zh: 有水池及魚利多者置水官，主平水收漁稅。
manualTranslations.literal: Those with ponds and much fish profit set water offices in charge of leveling water and collecting fishing tax.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Where ponds and fisheries flourished, water bureaus regulated irrigation works and fishing levies.

sourceRange.text: 鄭玄曰：「華蟲，五色之蟲。《周禮》繢人職曰『鳥獸蛇雜四時五色之位以章之』，謂是也。王者相變，至周而以日月星辰畫於旌旗，所謂三辰旂旗，昭其明也。而冕服九章，初一曰龍，次二曰山，次三曰華蟲，次四曰火，次五曰宗彝，皆畫以爲繢；次六曰藻，次七曰粉米，次八曰黼，次九曰黻，皆絺以爲繡。則衮之衣五章，裳四章，凡九也。鷩畫以雉，謂華蟲也。其衣三章，裳四章，凡七也。毳畫虎蜼，謂宗彝也。其衣三章，裳二章，凡五也。絺刺粉米無畫也。其衣一章，裳二章，凡三也。」《法言》曰：「聖人文質者也，車服以彰之，藻色以明之，聲音以揚之，詩書以光之。籩豆不陳，玉帛不分，琴瑟不鏗，鍾鼓不耺，吾無以見乎聖也！

sourceRange.text: 《獨斷》曰：「漢制禮無文。」荀綽《晉百官表注》曰：「建光中，尚書陳忠以爲『令史質堪上言，太官宜著兩梁，尚書孟布奏，太官職在鼎俎，不列陛位，堪欲令比大夫兩梁冠，不宜許。臣伏惟太官令職在典掌王饔，統六清之飲，列八珍之饌，正百品之羞，納四方之貢，所奉尤重，用思又勤。明詔慎口實之御，防有敗之姦，增崇其選。侍御史主捕案，太醫令奉方藥供養，符節令掌幡信金虎，故位從大夫，車有韜沂，冠有兩梁，所以殊親疏，別內外也。太官令以供養言之，爲最親近，以職事言之，爲最煩多，令又高選，又執法比太醫令，科同服等，而冠二人殊，名實不副。又博士秩卑，以其傳先王之訓，故尊而異之，令服大夫之冕。猶此言之，兩梁冠非必列於陛位也。建初中，太官令兩梁冠。春秋之義，大於復古。如堪言合典，可施行。克厭帝心，即聽用之』。」《獻帝起居注》曰：「中平六年，令三府長史兩梁冠，五時衣袍，事位從千石、六百石。

sourceRange.text: 日月星辰，山龍華蟲，孔安國注《尚書》曰：「華，象草華；蟲，雉也。」作繢宗彝，《古文尚書》「繢」作「會」。孔安國曰：「以五采成此畫焉。」宗廟彝樽，亦以山、龍、華蟲爲飾。藻火粉米，孔安國曰：「藻，水草有文者。火爲火字，粉若粟米，米若聚米。」黼黻絺繡，孔安國曰：「黼若斧形。黻爲兩己相背。葛之精者曰絺。五色備曰繡。」杜預注《左傳》曰：「白與黑謂之黼，黑與青謂之黻。」以五采章施于五色作服。孔安國曰：「以五采明施于五色，作尊卑之服。」天子備章，鄭玄《周禮注》曰：「此古天子冕服十二章。」公自山以下，侯伯自華蟲以下，子男自藻火以下，卿大夫自粉米以下。

sourceRange.text: 《漢官》曰：「尚書僕射，銅印青綬。」四百石、三百石、二百石黃綬，一采，淳黃圭，長丈五尺，六十首。自黑綬以下，縌綬皆長三尺，與綬同采而首半之。百石青紺綬，一采，宛轉繆織圭，長丈二尺。丁孚《漢儀》載太僕、太中大夫襄言：「乘輿綬，黃地冒白羽，青絳綠五采，四百首，長二丈三尺。詔所下王綬，冒亦五采，上下無差。諸王綬四采，絳地冒白羽，青黃去緣，二百六十首，長二丈一尺。公主綬如王。侯，絳地，紺縹三采，百二十首，長丈八尺。二千石綬，羽青地，桃華縹三采，百二十首，長丈八尺。黑綬，羽青地，絳二采，八十首，長一丈七尺。黃綬一采，八十首，長丈七尺。以爲常式。民織綬不如式，沒入官，犯者爲不敬。二千石綬以上，禁民無得織以粉組。」皇太后詔可，王綬如所下。

sourceRange.text: 五霸迭興，戰兵不息，佩非戰器，韍非兵旗，於是解去韍佩，留其係璲，徐廣曰：「今名璲爲縌。」以爲章表。故《詩》曰「鞙鞙佩璲」，此之謂也。鞙鞙，佩玉貌。璲，瑞也。鄭玄箋曰：「佩璲者，以瑞玉爲佩，佩之鞙鞙然。」韍佩旣廢，秦乃以采組連結於璲，光明章表，轉相結受，故謂之綬。

sourceRange.text: 冕冠，垂旒，前後邃延，邃，垂也。延，冕上覆。玉藻。《周禮》曰：「五采繅十有二就，皆五采玉，十有二，玉笄朱紘。」鄭玄注曰：「繅，雜文之名也。合五采絲爲之繩，垂於延之前後，各十二，所謂邃延也。就，成也。繩之每一帀而貫五采玉，十有二旒則十二玉也。每就閒蓋一寸。朱紘，以朱組爲紘也。紘一條屬兩端於武，此爲衮衣之冕。十二旒則用玉二百八十八。鷩衣之冕，繅九旒，用玉二百一十六。毳衣之冕，七旒，用玉百六十八。絺衣之冕，五旒，用玉百二十。玄衣之冕，三旒，用玉七十二。」孝明皇帝永平二年，初詔有司采《周官》、《禮記》、《尚書》皐陶篇，乘輿服從歐陽氏說，公卿以下從大小夏侯氏說。冕皆廣七寸，長尺二寸，前圓後方，朱綠裏，玄上，前垂四寸，後垂三寸，係白玉珠爲十二旒，以其綬采色爲組纓。《說文》曰：「組，綬屬也，小者以爲冕纓焉。」《禮記》曰「玄冠朱組纓，天子之服」是也。

sourceRange.text: 《前書》曰：「相國、丞相皆秦官，金印紫綬。高帝相國綠綬。」徐廣曰：「金印綠綟綬。」綟音戾，草名也。以染似綠，又云似紫。紫綬名緺綬，緺音瓜，其色青紫。綟字亦盭，音同也，傳寫者誤作「縶」。公加殊禮，皆服之。何承天云：「緺音媧。青紫色綬。綟，紫色也。」公、侯、將軍紫綬，二采，紫白，淳紫圭，長丈七尺，百八十首。《前書》曰：「太尉金印紫綬。御史大夫位上卿，銀印青綬，成帝更名大司空，金印紫綬。將軍亦金印。」《漢官儀》曰：「馬防爲車騎將軍，銀印青綬，在卿上，絕席。和帝以竇憲爲車騎將軍，始加金紫，次司空。

sourceRange.text: 《前書》注云：「以正月卯日作。」乘輿黃赤綬，四采，黃赤縹紺，淳黃圭，長二丈九尺九寸，五百首。《漢舊儀》曰：「璽皆白玉螭虎紐，文曰『皇帝行璽』、『皇帝之璽』、『皇帝信璽』、『天子行璽』、『天子之璽』、『天子信璽』，凡六璽。皇帝行璽，凡封之璽賜諸侯王書；信璽，發兵徵大臣；天子行璽，策拜外國，事天地鬼神。璽皆以武都紫泥封，青囊白素裏，兩端無縫，尺一板中約署。皇帝帶綬，黃地六采，不佩璽。璽以金銀縢組，侍中組負以從。秦以前民皆佩綬，金、玉、銀、銅、犀、象爲方寸璽，各服所好。奉璽書使者乘馳傳。其驛騎也，三騎行，晝夜千里爲程。」《吳書》曰：「漢室之亂，天子北詣河上，六璽不自隨，掌璽者投井中。孫堅北討董卓，頓軍城南，官署有井，每旦有五色氣從井出。堅使人浚得傳國璽。其文曰『受命于天，旣壽永昌』。方圍四寸，上有紐文槃五龍，瑨七寸管，龍上一角缺。」《獻帝起居注》曰：「時六璽不自隨，及還，於閣上得。」《晉陽秋》曰：「冉閔大將軍蔣幹以傳國璽付河南太守戴施，施獻之，百僚皆賀。璽光照洞徹，上蟠螭文隱起，《書》曰『昊天之命，皇帝壽昌』。秦舊璽也。」徐廣曰：「《傳國璽文》曰『受天之命，皇帝壽昌』。」諸侯王赤綬，徐廣曰：「太子及諸王金印，龜紐，纁朱綬。」四采，赤黃縹紺，淳赤圭，長二丈一尺，三百首。荀綽《晉百官表注》曰：「皇太子朱綬，三百二十首。

sourceRange.text: 《東觀書》曰：「永平二年正月，公卿議春南北郊，東平王蒼議曰：『孔子曰：「行夏之時，乘殷之路，服周之冕。」爲漢制法。高皇帝始受命創業，制長冠以入宗廟。光武受命中興，建明堂，立辟雍。陛下以聖明奉遵，以禮服龍衮，祭五帝。禮缺樂崩，乆無祭天地冕服之制。接尊事神，禮絜齋盛服，敬之至也。日月星辰，山龍華藻，天王衮冕十有二旒，以則天數；旂有龍章日月，以備其文。今祭明堂宗廟，圓以法天，方以則地，服以華文，象其物宜，以降神明，肅雍備思，博其類也。天地之禮，冕冠裳衣，宜如明堂之制。

sourceRange.text: 首多者系細，少者系麤，皆廣尺六寸。《東觀書》曰：「建武元年，復設諸侯王金璽綟綬，公侯金印紫綬。九卿、執金吾、河南尹秩皆中二千石，大長秋、將作大匠、度遼諸將軍、郡太守、國傅相皆秩二千石，校尉、中郎將、諸郡都尉、諸國行相、中尉、內史、中護軍、司直秩皆二千石，以上皆銀印青綬。中外官尚書令、御史中丞、治書侍御史、公將軍長史、中二千石丞、正、平、諸司馬、中宮王家僕、雒陽令秩皆千石，尚書、中謁者、謁者、黃門冗從、四僕射、諸都監、中外諸都官令、都候、司農部丞、郡國長史、丞、候、司馬、千人秩皆六百石，家令、侍、僕秩皆六百石，雒陽巿長秩四百石，主家長秩皆四百石，以上皆銅印黑綬。諸署長楫櫂丞秩三百石，諸秩千石者，其丞、尉皆秩四百石，秩六百石者，丞、尉秩三百石，四百石者，其丞、尉秩二百石，縣國丞、尉亦如之，縣、國三百石長相，丞、尉亦二百石，明堂、靈臺丞、諸陵校長秩二百石，丞、尉、校長以上皆銅印黃綬。縣國守宮令、相或千石或六百石，長相或四百石或三百石，長相皆以銅印黃綬。而有秩者侍中、中常侍、光祿大夫秩皆二千石，太中大夫秩皆比二千石，尚書、諫議大夫、侍御史、博士皆六百石，議郎、中謁者秩皆比六百石，小黃門、黃門侍郎、中黃門秩皆比四百石，郎中秩皆比三百石，太子舍人秩二百石。」太皇太后、皇太后入廟服，紺上皁下，蠶，青上縹下，皆深衣制，徐廣曰：「即單衣。」隱領袖緣以絛。翦氂蔮，簪珥。珥，耳璫垂珠也。簪以瑇瑁爲擿，長一尺，端爲華勝，上爲鳳皇爵，以翡翠爲毛羽，下有白珠，垂黃金鑷。
